tree:0xw6gj61i6zh5s.why: A short shared ending after God's will: He is the Mighty, the Wise (14:4, guiding and misguiding whom He wills) and the Mighty, the Merciful (30:5, giving victory to whom He wills). Mostly a closing pair of names, but the swap of the second name after the same phrase is a real memorizer trap.

tree:19ohwgw0nx8bcg.why: Rare clause: you resent us only because we believed. Said to the People of the Book (5:59) and by Pharaoh's magicians to Pharaoh (7:126). Same accusation thrown back at those who punish faith, worth pondering.
tree:19ohwgw0nx8bcg.relation: Believers in two stories answer persecution the same way: their only fault is their faith.

tree:0vjb85d00hjoo9.why: Only the stock closing promising a painful punishment is shared, after different subjects: disbelievers who would ransom themselves with the whole earth (5:36), and hypocrites who mock the poor givers of charity (9:79). Nothing particular to learn.

tree:1ayloox1ukpo9h.why: The same prayer, save me from the wrongdoing people, said by Musa fleeing Egypt (28:21) and by Pharaoh's wife (66:11), both escaping the same tyrant. A rich pair for pondering and a memorizer link.
tree:1ayloox1ukpo9h.relation: Two believers in Pharaoh's house pray the same words to be saved from his people.

tree:00szyww0d7ho70.why: Rare clause, We know best what they say, continuing differently: the sinners on the Day guessing how long they stayed (20:104), and comfort to the Prophet that he is no tyrant over them (50:45). Memorizer value, with God's full knowledge as the shared point.

tree:0u43g811cgbaq3.why: We raise in degrees whom We will: said of Ibrahim's argument against his people (6:83) and of Yusuf's plan to keep his brother (12:76). Two prophets raised by knowledge God gave them, with different endings.
tree:0u43g811cgbaq3.relation: God raises His prophets in rank through the knowledge and insight He gives them.

tree:1dpjk7s00g0nc6.why: Rain sent from the sky reviving dead land: the deniers admit it is God yet reason no further (29:63), and it is the pattern of the resurrection (43:11). Same sign drawn to two lessons, easy to mix.
tree:1dpjk7s00g0nc6.relation: The same sign of rain reviving the land points to God as Creator and to the raising of the dead.

tree:1t4bist0ksat2d.why: Rare clause: you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours, met with God forgetting them in return (32:14, 45:34). Same scene of the Fire with different continuations; strong memorizer and pondering value.
tree:1t4bist0ksat2d.relation: Recompense in kind: those who forgot the Day are themselves forgotten.

tree:01mj6xc0hapoek.why: What an excellent servant, he was ever turning back: praise given to Sulayman (38:30) and Ayyub (38:44) in one surah. One in wealth and one in affliction earn the same praise.
tree:01mj6xc0hapoek.relation: Two prophets, one tested with riches and one with suffering, praised in identical words.

tree:0u80bdd1ck247j.why: The rare praise of God as excellent Protector and excellent Helper closes 8:40 and 22:78, with a small difference in the opening particle that a memorizer must hold. The 22:78 row reads on across the surah boundary into 23:1, which should be checked.
tree:0u80bdd1ck247j.relation: Whether people turn away (8:40) or hold fast to God (22:78), He is the protector of the believers.

tree:16haokf02165gf.why: Same refrain about detailing the signs for people who know, after a ruling: lawful adornment for the believers (7:32), and repentant enemies becoming brothers in faith (9:11). Different lead-in particles to keep apart.

tree:1ucqvai0ci6a66.why: God relating to the Prophet news of what came before, to make his heart firm (11:120) and as a reminder from Him (20:99). Same purpose of the stories, two lead-ins to tell apart.
tree:1ucqvai0ci6a66.relation: Why the stories are told: to strengthen the Prophet and to remind.

tree:0ysmbsl07b6qzh.why: Zakariyya's prayer for a child in two surahs: grant me from Yourself good offspring (3:38), and an heir (19:5). Same story, different wording of the request.
tree:0ysmbsl07b6qzh.relation: The same prayer of Zakariyya, told in two places.

tree:1vgevdm0kk1qm6.why: Has the story of Musa reached you, opening the Musa narrative in two surahs, with and without the leading conjunction: the fire (20:10) and the call in the sacred valley (79:16). Same story, a clear memorizer trap.

tree:1gzpeo110a0pnl.why: Will any be destroyed but the people who do wrong (6:47) or who defy (46:35)? Same rhetorical warning, one word changed at the end, a typical memorizer trap.
tree:1gzpeo110a0pnl.relation: Destruction falls only on those who earn it.

tree:0r2jxd10u8b5mn.why: Guarding their prayer as a mark of those who believe: the believers in the Hereafter (6:92) and the praying who are honoured in gardens (70:34). Same description of the faithful, different lead-ins.
tree:0r2jxd10u8b5mn.relation: Keeping the prayer is named as the sign of true faith in the Hereafter.

tree:1xyaq1f0tsaghd.why: The revelation described as the truth confirming what came before: the Children of Israel reject it although it confirms what they hold (2:91), and it confirms what was before it (35:31). Same description, two endings to keep apart.
tree:1xyaq1f0tsaghd.relation: The Quran confirms earlier scripture, which leaves those who reject it without excuse.

tree:1y14g0w07p8mrw.why: He is the one who gives life and death, then two continuations: the alternation of night and day (23:80), and His command 'Be' (40:68). Same divine attribute, different lead-in particle and ending to remember.

tree:13lqirf1vvo20l.why: Both ayat address the enemies with the same offer: if you stop or repent, it is better for you, and if you return or turn away, you will not escape God (8:19 to the Quraysh at Badr, 9:3 to the polytheists at the declaration of disavowal). Same choice put two ways.
tree:13lqirf1vvo20l.relation: The door of repentance kept open to the enemy, with the same warning for those who refuse it.

tree:1srv5zz0964oxx.why: The same words, it is from God, said truthfully by Maryam about her provision (3:37) and falsely by those who twist scripture (3:78), in the same surah. A sharp contrast worth pondering.
tree:1srv5zz0964oxx.relation: Contrast: a true claim that something is from God, and a lie wearing the same words.

tree:14r3r8d1a5gxet.why: Every soul will be paid in full on the Day: for what it earned, and they will not be wronged (3:25), and for what it did, and He knows best what they do (39:70). Same scene, small word swaps that a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:14r3r8d1a5gxet.relation: Full and just recompense of every soul on the Day of gathering.

tree:1sp7np81ea3m9k.why: God may turn in mercy to those whose deeds are mixed (9:102) and even to the hypocrites if He wills (33:24), both closing on His forgiveness. Same hope of repentance, worth pondering beside each other.
tree:1sp7np81ea3m9k.relation: God's door of repentance is open to the wavering and even to the hypocrites.

tree:0o9o55i19eg03q.why: They distort words from their places: said twice of some of the Children of Israel, with different continuations (4:46 their mocking speech, 5:13 they forgot part of what they were reminded of). Same accusation, a memorizer trap.
tree:0o9o55i19eg03q.relation: Distorting the scripture follows from breaking the covenant and hardened hearts.

tree:02jv1x90mifqkb.why: Calling on others besides God: what can neither harm nor benefit (22:12), and who will not answer until the Day of Resurrection (46:5). Same argument against false worship, two descriptions to keep apart.
tree:02jv1x90mifqkb.relation: What people call on besides God is powerless and does not even hear.

tree:115be9b1ocb0ot.why: The same promise from two prophets to their people: seek forgiveness and He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain, said by Hud (11:52) and by Nuh (71:11). Same theme of prophets calling their people; strong pondering pair.
tree:115be9b1ocb0ot.relation: Two prophets promise the same worldly blessing for repentance: rain, strength, wealth and children.

tree:0mk1y1z0nxnjcb.why: He shows you the lightning in fear and hope, then the heavy clouds (13:12) or the rain that revives the earth (30:24). Same sign, a rare clause with different lead-ins and continuations.

tree:09zbg9q0e8d5f0.why: They strive to spread corruption in the land: the punishment of those who wage war on God (5:33), and the Jews who kindle wars God puts out (5:64). Same surah, same description of corruption, worth seeing together.
tree:09zbg9q0e8d5f0.relation: Spreading corruption in the land is met with severe punishment and with God not loving the corrupt.

tree:0yu7hcj142w8gz.why: The same question, what should they spend, asked twice in one surah with two answers: on parents, relatives, orphans and the needy (2:215), and the surplus (2:219). A classic memorizer pair and a lesson: what to spend on, and how much.
tree:0yu7hcj142w8gz.relation: One question answered twice: who receives the spending, and what amount to give.

tree:146lhf50tz355d.why: The same promise, He will forgive you some of your sins, spoken by the jinn to their people (46:31) and by Nuh to his (71:4), with different continuations. Same call of a messenger to his people.
tree:146lhf50tz355d.relation: Callers to God, human and jinn, offer their people the same forgiveness.

tree:1uryyv50lgmxlb.why: God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection: between the religions (22:17) and between those who differed (32:25). Same promise of a final verdict on human disagreement, different endings.
tree:1uryyv50lgmxlb.relation: Disputes over religion are settled only by God on the Day.

tree:14t5jag1d9cvvu.why: He accepts repentance from His servants, then takes the charities (9:104) or pardons misdeeds (42:25). Rare clause, worth pondering beside each other: repentance welcomed and charity received.
tree:14t5jag1d9cvvu.relation: God accepts both the repentance and the giving of His servants.

tree:1hqxfvh0xviicp.why: The believer of Pharaoh's people twice says he fears for them a day: like the day of the confederates (40:30), and the Day of mutual calling (40:32). Same speech; the two objects of fear are easy to confuse.
tree:1hqxfvh0xviicp.relation: The believer warns of both a worldly ruin like past nations and the Day of Judgement.

tree:19zq8s900g2mz3.why: The shared words are only that God guides whom He wills, followed by unrelated clauses: spending for one's own good (2:272), and none knows the soldiers of your Lord (74:31). Different subjects and the continuations are different structures.

tree:0xctmp10tv879b.why: God guides whom He wills: messengers sent in their people's language (14:4), and the Prophet unable to guide those he loves (28:56). Endings differ (Mighty and Wise, and He knows best who are guided). Guidance belongs to God alone, worth pondering.
tree:0xctmp10tv879b.relation: Messengers convey the message, but guidance itself is God's alone.

tree:1oj0htn1xjs1lz.why: The shared words straddle two sentences: the Day of Resurrection ends one clause and a new exclamation begins. The subjects differ (the curse on Aad in 11:60, the losers among the wrongdoers in 42:45). Nothing to learn from the overlap.

tree:0t8711d1rg6tkd.why: On the day the Hour arrives, that day people will separate (30:14), and the followers of falsehood will lose (45:27). Same scene of the Hour, a rare clause with two endings to keep apart.
tree:0t8711d1rg6tkd.relation: The Hour divides people and exposes the losers.

tree:0v1dwll01bnv5n.why: Woe to us, we were wrongdoers: the cry of a destroyed town (21:14) and of deniers touched by a breath of punishment (21:46), in one surah. Same late confession, worth pondering.
tree:0v1dwll01bnv5n.relation: The wrongdoers confess only when punishment touches them, when it no longer helps.

tree:0osuaja16c0oi2.why: The declaration we believe in God and what was revealed to us: the classic pair 2:136 and 3:84 (to us and upon us, then the list of prophets), and the believers' reply to the People of the Book in 5:59. Same profession of faith, a strong memorizer set.
tree:0osuaja16c0oi2.relation: The believers' faith in all revelation is the only thing held against them.

tree:1me6ljd1pf6be1.why: They took gods besides Him, answered three ways: why bring no clear proof (18:15), bring your proof (21:24), and they create nothing and are created (25:3). Same argument against idols, a memorizer set with different continuations.
tree:1me6ljd1pf6be1.relation: The gods taken besides God have no proof and no power.

tree:1ughm0z0kxqenb.why: Those who took protectors besides Him: their excuse that they bring them nearer to God (39:3), God watches them (42:6), and God alone is the Protector (42:9). Same theme, a memorizer set with three continuations.
tree:1ughm0z0kxqenb.relation: The protectors taken besides God, answered: He watches them and He alone protects.

tree:1pkwut91q4h15l.why: Fear God that you may succeed closes three commands: enter houses by their doors (2:189), do not consume usury (3:130), and be patient and steadfast (3:200). A memorizer set with clear lead-ins. The 3:200 row reads on across the surah boundary into 4:1, which should be checked.

tree:1d8spq50zky16n.why: When he said to his father and his people: Ibrahim's question in three surahs, what are these statues (21:52), what do you worship (26:70), and what is it you worship (37:85). Same story, a classic memorizer trap.
tree:1d8spq50zky16n.relation: Ibrahim's opening question to his people, told three ways.

tree:04xj9ji1gl4ats.why: We sent before you no messenger: the shared message of oneness (21:25), Satan casting into a prophet's wish (22:52), and ask the messengers whether gods besides the Merciful were made (43:45). Same theme of earlier messengers, a memorizer set.
tree:04xj9ji1gl4ats.relation: All earlier messengers carried the same message that there is no god but God.

tree:1rvy8o40kpzo82.why: Except those who repent: after that and reform (3:89, 24:5, identical) or before you overpower them (5:34). The exception of repentance from three severe rulings, a strong memorizer set.
tree:1rvy8o40kpzo82.relation: Even after the gravest sins, repentance opens the way to God's forgiveness.

tree:10l868d0n37cbx.why: They deceive, mislead or destroy only themselves, and they do not perceive: hypocrites (2:9), some of the People of the Book (3:69), and deniers who keep others from the Quran (6:26). Three different verbs before the same ending.
tree:10l868d0n37cbx.relation: Every scheme against the truth harms only its plotters, without their knowing.

tree:0nvzovp0yhhek7.why: Except in the best way: approaching the orphan's wealth (6:152, 17:34, which run identical and then branch) and debating the People of the Book (29:46). Strong memorizer set, and a shared lesson of dealing in the best manner.
tree:0nvzovp0yhhek7.relation: The best manner governs both handling the weak's property and arguing with others.

tree:1n56o671alnmj7.why: That you worship none but God: the Prophet's warning (11:2), messengers to Aad and Thamud refused (41:14), and Hud's warning (46:21). Same call of prophets to their people, with different continuations.
tree:1n56o671alnmj7.relation: Every prophet's call opens with the same demand to worship God alone.

tree:1uf0xhg0qrxguu.why: No messenger or prophet came to them but they mocked him, said three times (15:11, 36:30, 43:7) with small differences in the lead-in and the noun. Same theme, a classic memorizer set.
tree:1uf0xhg0qrxguu.relation: Mockery of messengers is the constant pattern of the deniers.

tree:1usyfge1rqtiqs.why: Will they be recompensed except for what they used to do: identical in 7:147 and 34:33, with a variant in 28:84 about those who did evil. Same law of recompense, a memorizer set.

tree:080b43z0qj9vut.why: The confession that there is no god but Him, Lord of the mighty Throne, closes the Prophet's word of trust (9:129) and the hoopoe's report against sun-worship (27:26). Rare exact clause, good memorizer pair. The 9:129 row reads on across the surah boundary into 10:1, which should be checked.
tree:080b43z0qj9vut.relation: The Lord of the mighty Throne: enough for the Prophet when people turn away, and the only one worthy of worship, not the queen's sun.

tree:1yfcs3a03rs7xu.why: The earth revived after its death, a sign for those who hear (16:65) and who reason (30:24), and proof that He will revive the dead (30:50). Same sign, with endings a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:1yfcs3a03rs7xu.relation: Rain reviving dead land is both a sign of God and a picture of the resurrection.

tree:1d6hqos18poudk.why: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters: twice with the emphatic form (2:147, 10:94) and once without (3:60). A classic memorizer trap.
tree:1d6hqos18poudk.relation: The Prophet is told three times to hold firmly to the truth from his Lord.

tree:0ltej5k0e4ujnw.why: The punishment of disgrace in this worldly life: lifted from the people of Yunus when they believed (10:98), and tasted by earlier deniers and by Aad, with the Hereafter's punishment greater still (39:26, 41:16). Same theme, worth pondering.
tree:0ltej5k0e4ujnw.relation: Contrast: the one people spared worldly disgrace through faith, and those who tasted it with worse to come.

tree:13373360aklf7a.why: He made the night for you to rest in: identical opening in 10:67 and 40:61 with different endings, and the night as a garment in 25:47. Same sign of night and day, a memorizer set.
tree:13373360aklf7a.relation: Night for rest and day for sight, a mercy that calls for listening and thanks.

tree:0r3g5ln0nznecf.why: That which you used to deny, said to the deniers when they meet it: the Fire (32:20), the Day of sorting (37:21), and the scene of 83:17. Same reproach with different lead-ins.
tree:0r3g5ln0nznecf.relation: On the Day the deniers are shown exactly what they denied.

tree:0gqv9m00vacj0c.why: Those who believed and were God-fearing: the friends of God (10:63), and those saved from the destruction of Thamud (27:53, 41:18) with two forms of the verb. A memorizer set, and a clear lesson that faith with fear of God saves.
tree:0gqv9m00vacj0c.relation: Faith joined with God-consciousness is what saves, in this world and the next.

tree:1i90qiu1oekt0s.why: Those who believed, emigrated and strove: the order of wealth, lives and the way of God changes between 8:72, 8:74 and 9:20. A classic memorizer set on one theme.
tree:1i90qiu1oekt0s.relation: The rank of the early emigrants who gave their wealth and lives.

tree:1konsxp09zci7z.why: Those who disbelieve in the signs of God: they have a severe punishment (3:4), they despair of His mercy (29:23), and they are the losers (39:63). Same subject, three outcomes to keep apart.
tree:1konsxp09zci7z.relation: Rejecting God's signs leads to punishment, despair and loss.

tree:1xcdflm1j1petw.why: Those who fear their Lord unseen, with three continuations: they dread the Hour (21:49), they keep up the prayer (35:18), and they have forgiveness and a great reward (67:12). Same description of the believers, a memorizer set.
tree:1xcdflm1j1petw.relation: Fear of God unseen shows in dread of the Hour and in prayer, and is rewarded.

tree:07mh94z1426md9.why: Those they call on besides Him do not answer (13:14), do not judge anything (40:20), and hold no intercession (43:86). Same argument on the powerlessness of false gods.
tree:07mh94z1426md9.relation: The false gods can neither answer, nor judge, nor intercede.

tree:1vcbsgi0neqy98.why: Responding to the Messenger after being wounded (3:172) set beside opposing the Messenger after guidance became clear (4:115, 47:32, near identical). The pair 4:115 and 47:32 is a strong memorizer link; 3:172 adds a contrast.
tree:1vcbsgi0neqy98.relation: Contrast: some obey the Messenger even after injury, others oppose him even after clear guidance.

tree:1yety1k0zj02d8.why: To God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, ending knowing and wise (48:4) and then mighty and wise (48:7), twins in one surah; 4:170 has the same closing after what is in the heavens and the earth. A memorizer trap on which name comes where.

tree:1mqcq8106no14j.why: They keep up the prayer and spend from what We provided them: describing the God-fearing (2:3), the true believers (8:3), and the humble (22:35), each with a different form of the verb. A classic memorizer set.
tree:1mqcq8106no14j.relation: Prayer and spending together are named as the mark of the believers again and again.

tree:0rh3rz71vou2qv.why: The Book, no doubt in it: a guidance for the God-fearing (2:2), and from the Lord of the worlds (10:37, 32:2), the latter two followed by the charge that he invented it. A strong memorizer set.
tree:0rh3rz71vou2qv.relation: The Quran's certainty is stated against those who claim it was invented.

tree:19v2i5w0altdui.why: The disbelievers' prayer or plotting is only in error: their call to idols (13:14), Pharaoh's plot against the believers (40:25), and their cry in the Fire (40:50). A rare ending that ties together worldly and otherworldly futility.
tree:19v2i5w0altdui.relation: Whatever the disbelievers call on or plot comes to nothing.

tree:1e0qz8i0f1vfgw.why: Only the opening of three unrelated stock statements is shared: God does not change a people's state (13:11), does not break His promise (13:31), does not guide the wrongdoers (28:50). Different subjects, and the shared words stop before the meaning starts.

tree:10ekofm0xj3fum.why: Only the stock closing that God sees what they do is shared, after unrelated subjects: those who wish for long life (2:96), the ranks of people with God (3:163), and the Children of Israel's blindness (5:71).

tree:10v0d290nqymwn.why: The shared closing names God as Mighty, Owner of retribution, after different subjects: those who deny His signs (3:4), the one who hunts in the sacred state again (5:95), and His promise to His messengers (14:47). A closing pair of names with nothing particular to learn.

tree:19do41z0w5g13d.why: Your wealth and your children are a trial, and with God is a great reward: nearly identical in 8:28 and 64:15, a strong memorizer pair. 9:22 shares only the reward clause, closing the description of the emigrants' gardens, a different subject.
tree:19do41z0w5g13d.changes: Removed 9:22: it shares only the closing reward clause, not the theme of wealth and children as a trial.
tree:19do41z0w5g13d.relation: Wealth and children test a person, while the greater reward is with God.

tree:0vmqvfw1ar52k4.why: Whom God curses or leaves astray, you will never find a helper (4:52) or a way (4:88, 4:143) for him, all in one surah. A memorizer set on one theme.
tree:0vmqvfw1ar52k4.relation: No one can save the person God has abandoned.

tree:0sotlu80yumdqq.why: The shared words mean only 'after' in three unrelated settings: exchanging God's favour (2:211), emigrating after being wronged (16:41), and arguing about God after His call was answered (42:16). Different subjects.

tree:1kx1agp08ficm9.why: The full name, the Messiah Jesus son of Mary: in the good news to Mary (3:45), in the claim that they killed him (4:157), and in the warning against excess (4:171). Same subject, worth pondering what is said of him in each.
tree:1kx1agp08ficm9.relation: Who Jesus is: honoured and near to God, a messenger and His word, not killed and not divine.

tree:0nr1ygq0pmbxiu.why: Then wish for death, if you are truthful: the challenge to those claiming the Hereafter is theirs alone (2:94, 62:6, followed by they will never wish it), and avert death from yourselves (3:168) to the hypocrites. A memorizer set on one challenge.
tree:0nr1ygq0pmbxiu.relation: Those who claim special favour with God, or blame others' deaths, are challenged by death itself.

tree:0q0h0hp0hj0euz.why: Your shelter is the Fire and you have no helpers: identical in 29:25 and 45:34, with a variant in 11:113 warning not to incline toward the wrongdoers. A memorizer set on the abandonment of the people of the Fire.

tree:17lnyn30ibsy07.why: And to Thamud their brother Salih: identical openings in 7:73 and 11:61, and a different form in 27:45. Same story, a classic memorizer set.
tree:17lnyn30ibsy07.relation: Salih's call to Thamud, the same in every telling.

tree:0rxfxpq17j3z5q.why: Go to Pharaoh, he has transgressed: said to Musa alone (20:24, 79:17) and to Musa and Harun together (20:43). Same story, a classic memorizer trap.
tree:0rxfxpq17j3z5q.relation: The same command to confront Pharaoh, given first to Musa and then to both brothers.

tree:050ooit1k23z2t.why: Twin ayat in one surah: if God made the night (28:71) or the day (28:72) perpetual until the Day of Resurrection, what god besides Him could bring light or rest? A strong memorizer pair and a sign to ponder. In 7:167 the shared word is a relative pronoun (someone who will afflict them), not the question 'what god', so it does not belong.
tree:050ooit1k23z2t.changes: Removed 7:167: its shared word is a relative pronoun, not the interrogative of 28:71 and 28:72.
tree:050ooit1k23z2t.relation: Night and day each a mercy no one but God could restore if He withheld it.

tree:0jv4b0m1nqec96.why: Is there not in Hell a residence for the disbelievers (29:68, 39:32, both after who is more unjust than one who lies about God) or for the arrogant (39:60). Same theme of lying about God, a memorizer set.
tree:0jv4b0m1nqec96.relation: Lying against God and denying the truth leads to the same end.

tree:0ygpqc30uesfrn.why: The night and the day, the sun and the moon: made subservient (16:12), created each in an orbit (21:33), and signs not to be worshipped (41:37). Same sign, three lessons drawn from it.
tree:0ygpqc30uesfrn.relation: The heavenly bodies are servants and signs of God, not objects of worship.

tree:1twnbf11r9301r.why: I have been commanded to be among the Muslims (Nuh, 10:72) and among the believers (the Prophet, 10:104), in one surah. One word changes, a memorizer trap, and the same stance of two messengers.
tree:1twnbf11r9301r.relation: Nuh and Muhammad declare the same commanded submission before their people.

tree:0zoow5z1ib1jtv.why: Judgement belongs only to God, said by the Prophet (6:57), by Yusuf in prison (12:40), and by Yaqub to his sons (12:67), with three different continuations. Classic memorizer set on one creed.
tree:0zoow5z1ib1jtv.relation: Prophets in very different settings affirm that decision rests with God alone.

tree:1trqza70kfroqp.why: Whatever good you spend, God knows it: after who should receive it (2:215), the poor who do not beg (2:273), and spending what you love (3:92). Same theme of spending, a memorizer set.
tree:1trqza70kfroqp.relation: No act of giving is lost; God knows each one.

tree:1mlnk6m01qqg06.why: Only the stock closing that God knows what they do is shared, after unrelated subjects: following conjecture (10:36), and wrongdoers denying their deeds at death (16:28).

tree:1h8hbwk0b80mr2.why: God loves the God-fearing, closing three ayat on keeping covenants: whoever fulfils his pledge (3:76), and honouring treaties with polytheists who kept theirs (9:4, 9:7). Same theme, worth pondering.
tree:1h8hbwk0b80mr2.relation: Faithfulness to one's word, even with enemies, is part of fearing God.

tree:0omm0pq02pas4s.why: God loves those who act justly, closing three ayat on fairness: judging between the People of the Book (5:42), reconciling fighting believers (49:9), and dealing justly with peaceful non-Muslims (60:8). Same theme in three settings.
tree:0omm0pq02pas4s.relation: Justice is owed to everyone: to other faiths, to quarrelling believers, and to non-hostile neighbours.

tree:0skn5lp18tqsfr.why: Your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection in what they differed: identical in 10:93 and 45:17, both after the Children of Israel differed once knowledge came, and with His judgement in 27:78. A strong memorizer set.
tree:0skn5lp18tqsfr.relation: Division after knowledge came is left to God's judgement.

tree:0f3elwq19qeinc.why: Indeed in that is a lesson, for those with insight (3:13 the victory at Badr, 24:44 night and day) and for whoever fears (79:26 Pharaoh's end). A rare word for lesson, and two different endings that a memorizer must hold.

tree:1gmsyie0kjv3a8.why: Though before they were in clear error: the gift of a messenger who teaches the Book and wisdom (3:164, 62:2, near identical); 30:49 uses the same lead-in for despair before the rain. A strong memorizer set.
tree:1gmsyie0kjv3a8.relation: God's mercy, in a messenger or in rain, comes to those who were lost or despairing.

tree:000bv711uu3mrj.why: Many of the people are defiantly disobedient (5:49), heedless of Our signs (10:92), and deniers of meeting their Lord (30:8). A memorizer set with three endings, and one picture of most people's failure toward revelation.

tree:1jpargy05vy3is.why: If it is Him you worship: eat the good things and give thanks (2:172, 16:114, both followed by the same list of forbidden foods), and prostrate to God, not to the sun and moon (41:37). A memorizer set on worship as gratitude.
tree:1jpargy05vy3is.relation: Worship shown both by thanks for provision and by prostration to the Creator alone.

tree:1847ifp168truj.why: They follow only conjecture and they only guess: said of most people (6:116), of the polytheists (10:66), and of those who blame God's will for their idolatry (43:20). A memorizer set on the polytheists' lack of knowledge.
tree:1847ifp168truj.relation: Shirk rests on guessing, never on knowledge.

tree:1byf3nm15eb9by.why: The angels to Ibrahim: we have been sent to the people of Lut (11:70) and to a criminal people (15:58, 51:32). Same story, a memorizer set.

tree:1njui4q1xcy0i8.why: We sent down to you the Book in truth: to judge between people (4:105), confirming and guarding earlier scripture (5:48), so worship God sincerely (39:2). Same statement with three purposes.
tree:1njui4q1xcy0i8.relation: Why the Book came down in truth: to judge, to confirm, and to lead to sincere worship.

tree:16lb3tp06s6cm5.why: Give us victory over the disbelieving people closes three prayers: Talut's army before Jalut (2:250), the end of al-Baqara (2:286), and the companions of the prophets (3:147). Same prayer, a memorizer set. The 2:286 row reads on across the surah boundary into 3:1, which should be checked.
tree:16lb3tp06s6cm5.relation: Believers of every age ask for steadfastness and victory in the same words.

tree:1g630sb1g7cet5.why: Striving with wealth and lives in God's way: the emigrants (8:72), the hypocrites who hated it (9:81), and the true believers (49:15). Same phrase, with a clear contrast.
tree:1g630sb1g7cet5.relation: Contrast: striving with wealth and self defines the true believers, and hating it exposes the hypocrites.

tree:1fatt0k11ipp5u.why: He is the Forgiving, the Merciful, each time after real forgiveness: Yaqub promising to seek it for his sons (12:98), Musa forgiven after killing (28:16), and the call not to despair of God's mercy (39:53). The closing is common, but here the theme is shared.
tree:1fatt0k11ipp5u.relation: Even grave sins are forgiven: the brothers of Yusuf, Musa, and all who have wronged themselves.

tree:19fomeg11y8wl8.why: How can I have a son: Zakariyya twice (3:40, 19:8, the order of age and barren wife reversed) and Maryam (19:20). Same question of a miraculous birth, a classic memorizer set.
tree:19fomeg11y8wl8.relation: Two miraculous births, each met with the same astonished question.

tree:0pvjx2v0ny1wox.why: The forbidden foods, including what was dedicated to other than God, in 5:3, 6:145 and 16:115, with different word orders and continuations. Same ruling, a memorizer set.

tree:0lpsy4f0iyyr3j.why: Those are the ones who lost themselves: those whose scales are light (7:9, 23:103) and those who lied about God (11:21), with three endings. A memorizer set on the same loss.
tree:0lpsy4f0iyyr3j.relation: The true loss is losing one's own self.

tree:0grfd990jwb4xj.why: Only the stock clause promising a painful punishment is shared, after different subjects: disbelievers dying in disbelief (3:91), deniers of the meeting with God (29:23), and oppressors (42:42).

tree:0bpummu1nugix6.why: For them is a humiliating punishment, after taking God's signs in mockery (31:6, 45:9, near identical) and denying them (22:57). The humiliation matches the mockery; a good memorizer set.
tree:0bpummu1nugix6.relation: Those who make a mockery of God's signs are themselves humiliated.

tree:0950ljn1i1dxrx.why: Only the generic frame 'and they, in it, do not ...' is shared. The subjects differ (worldly seekers paid in full in this life vs the people of Hell who cannot hear) and the verbs differ, so there is nothing to confuse or to ponder.

tree:0auafnl0ztb5fn.why: A real mutashabih in two neighbouring surahs: the same verdict on the deniers ends both ayat, opened once with 'rather' and once with 'or'. Easy to swap when reciting.
tree:0auafnl0ztb5fn.relation: Same charge against the deniers of the messenger: transgression, not reason, drives them.

tree:0iefw0a1y7qohm.why: Both ayat are about dying while a disbeliever and what then awaits: curse in 2:161, prepared punishment in 4:18. Same theme, close wording, worth holding together.
tree:0iefw0a1y7qohm.relation: Death in disbelief closes the door: no repentance at the last moment (4:18), only the curse (2:161).

tree:1lfhjk31qhdgtn.why: Strong mutashabih: both open with the disbelievers who die as disbelievers, then 'nothing will be accepted' (3:91) vs 'God will not forgive them' (47:34). Same theme, different consequence to remember.
tree:1lfhjk31qhdgtn.relation: Death in disbelief: no ransom accepted and no forgiveness.

tree:0z434wk1yzqt84.why: Same ayah-final clause, opened with 'and' in 7:198 and 'so' in 36:9. Both describe people who face the guidance yet cannot see it, which is a theme worth pondering, and the opening letter is the memorizer's trap.
tree:0z434wk1yzqt84.relation: Blindness to guidance: looking without seeing (7:198), veiled by a barrier (36:9).

tree:132t83w0ythhnm.why: Both are prostration ayat ending 'and they are not arrogant': the angels and all creatures in 16:49, the believers in 32:15. The believers are described with the angels' quality.
tree:132t83w0ythhnm.relation: Similarity: humble prostration joins the believers to the angels.

tree:1wzoso71lcnbmr.why: A striking contrast in the same words: Joseph knew his brothers while they did not know him (12:58); the deniers know their messenger yet act as if they did not (23:69). The opening letter differs (and/so).
tree:1wzoso71lcnbmr.relation: Contrast: not recognizing out of ignorance vs denying what is known.

tree:1uom7cp0hnn55p.why: Same story, same closing, father and son: Jacob entrusts Benjamin to God (12:64) and Joseph forgives his brothers (12:92), both ending with God as the most merciful of the merciful.
tree:1uom7cp0hnn55p.relation: Jacob's trust and Joseph's forgiveness rest on the same faith in God's mercy.

tree:0ise1yk0k2rvb0.why: Only 'He knows best what' is shared, a common phrase. One ayah is about the reckoning on the Day of Judgement, the other about the charge that the Prophet forged the Quran. Nothing to confuse or ponder.

tree:0p6o0qa0j84qt2.why: The rarer order of the two names (Wise before Knowing) closes both ayat, after 'and He is' in 43:84 and 'indeed He is' in 51:30. Useful for a memorizer who expects the usual order.

tree:09hxjed0rtg9e3.why: This name of God occurs only in these two ayat, after 'your Lord is' (15:86) and 'yes, and He is' (36:81). Both tie God's creating to His power to raise and judge.
tree:09hxjed0rtg9e3.relation: The Creator who knows all can surely create again.

tree:1o5n4to0ozk52w.why: Both remind people that God brought them into being: from one soul (6:98) and with hearing, sight and hearts (67:23). Same opening, different blessing named.
tree:1o5n4to0ozk52w.relation: God's creating of man as a call to understand (6:98) and to give thanks (67:23).

tree:17syjqw1m30mt4.why: God sends down rain after despair (42:28) and sends down clear signs to bring people out of darkness (57:9). Rain and revelation side by side is a classic thought to ponder.
tree:17syjqw1m30mt4.relation: Similarity: rain revives the land, revelation revives hearts; both are His mercy.

tree:0a9sa050iy56ax.why: Both are declarations of God's oneness closing on the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. 2:163 states it plainly; 59:22 adds knowledge of the unseen and the seen.

tree:1jvx1030c77uov.why: Both close a mention of God's help or mercy with the same pair of names, after 'and He is' (30:5) and 'indeed He is' (44:42). The phrase is common, but here the lead-in fits the closing in both.
tree:1jvx1030c77uov.relation: God's help for whom He wills and His mercy on whom He has mercy, both from the Mighty, the Merciful.

tree:1j98weh0qg5zsd.why: The closing 'and He is the Most High, the Most Great' occurs only here, and in both it follows 'to Him belongs what is in the heavens and the earth'. A clear mutashabih between the Throne Verse and 42:4.

tree:1mtup5v1b2z5wj.why: Same pair of names closing two ayat, after 'your Lord is' in 11:66 (saving Salih) and 'and He is' in 42:19 (provision). The lead-in is what a memorizer must keep apart.

tree:01qoaxj1hdkwir.why: The only two ayat ending 'and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware', both about God's knowledge: He perceives all sight (6:103), He knows what He created (67:14).
tree:01qoaxj1hdkwir.relation: The names fit the point: nothing escapes the One who is subtle and aware.

tree:0d6m2vz1mkak25.why: Both end 'and He is the best of providers' in a talk about wealth: the Prophet asks no payment, his Lord's reward is better (23:72); what you spend He replaces (34:39).
tree:0d6m2vz1mkak25.relation: Provision from God is better than what people give or keep.

tree:1xcascl05yqg93.why: Only the stock phrase 'it is better for him' is shared. Voluntary extra fasting (2:184) and honouring God's sanctities on the pilgrimage (22:30) are different subjects, and nothing more links them.

tree:0e8ca551x5w3dx.why: Both are about speech: debate in the best way (16:125) and say what is best (17:53). The same words are followed by a different reason (your Lord knows / Satan sows discord).
tree:0e8ca551x5w3dx.relation: The best words: in calling others to God and among believers, against Satan's discord.

tree:1tkzglh066esxn.why: The faces of the disbelievers in two moments: now they show rejection when the ayat are recited (22:72); on the Day they darken when they see what they denied (67:27).
tree:1tkzglh066esxn.relation: Contrast: the face shows hostility in this world and grief in the next.

tree:1xcvsap0x3am13.why: Both describe the wrongdoers' faces in the Fire: thrown face-first (27:90), turned over while they wish they had obeyed (33:66). Same scene from two sides.

tree:0duhivo09wkfzi.why: The only two places with 'they wish you would disbelieve', both warning against taking enemies as allies. Same theme, different position in the ayah (opening vs ending).
tree:0duhivo09wkfzi.relation: The enemy's true wish is your disbelief, so do not take them as protectors.

tree:1b8t4wg1kw60mo.why: God's mercy embraces everything: God says it (7:156), and the angels pray with it (40:7), adding knowledge. A beautiful pair to ponder.
tree:1b8t4wg1kw60mo.relation: God's word about His mercy and the angels' prayer that answers it.

tree:09mftyq0tgjjda.why: Two ayat of one passage on the end of time in an-Naml: when the word falls due, the Beast comes out (27:82); the word falls due and they cannot speak (27:85). A pair a memorizer must keep in order.
tree:09mftyq0tgjjda.relation: The same decree, first as a sign before the Hour, then as the silencing of the wrongdoers.

tree:0yfxc8r0lxndcz.why: The only two descriptions of the Fire whose fuel is people and stones: prepared for the disbelievers (2:24), and a warning to believers to guard themselves and their families (66:6).
tree:0yfxc8r0lxndcz.relation: The same Fire threatens the deniers and is a reason for believers to protect their homes.

tree:149uwip15lgln3.why: Unlawful gain is fire in the belly, said twice: of those who hide the Book for a small price (2:174) and of those who eat the orphan's wealth (4:10). Rare image, close wording.
tree:149uwip15lgln3.relation: Similarity: both sell a trust for money, and both eat fire.

tree:0iwzxsq1lh1cna.why: Both address the people of understanding and then end differently: 'that you may be mindful' (2:179) and 'that you may succeed' (5:100). A clean memorizer's trap.

tree:07xrutt0kuywyh.why: Only the common call 'O people, only ...' is shared. One ayah is about people who rebel after being saved at sea (10:23), the other the Prophet stating he is a warner (22:49). Different subjects, nothing to learn.

tree:1ww1eiq15nqdmu.why: Both are about enemies stretching out their hands against the believers: God held them back (5:11), and they would do it if they could (60:2).
tree:1ww1eiq15nqdmu.relation: God's past protection (5:11) and the standing danger from enemies (60:2).

tree:1b6h7j30q26o71.why: Two neighbouring ayat about desert Arabs, one counts what he spends as a loss, the other as a way to draw near to God. Same words, opposite intention.
tree:1b6h7j30q26o71.relation: Contrast: the same spending is a burden to one and a means of nearness to another.

tree:0stegkx1v44z03.why: God completing His favour on a chosen servant: Joseph and Jacob's family (12:6) and the Prophet Muhammad (48:2). Same promise to two prophets.
tree:0stegkx1v44z03.relation: Similarity: the favour completed on Joseph and on Muhammad, both after hardship.

tree:06hjuw80kp436m.why: Only the common phrase 'and God turns in mercy to' is shared. 9:15 is about fighting the oath-breakers, 33:73 about the trust carried by man. The lead-ins and closings differ, so a reciter is unlikely to mix them.

tree:19elbjw0gs059a.why: The only two places with 'and they think they are rightly guided', both about people who take devils as allies or companions (7:30, 43:36-37).
tree:19elbjw0gs059a.relation: Following devils while thinking oneself guided: the worst kind of misguidance.

tree:0t3mdql1dgm06h.why: God establishing the truth by His words: at Badr, cutting off the disbelievers (8:7), and against the claim that the Prophet forged the Quran (42:24).
tree:0t3mdql1dgm06h.relation: God makes the truth stand by His words, in battle and in revelation.

tree:1x6gjxf10r8v6j.why: Two images of the dead coming out of the graves: like scattered locusts (54:7) and rushing as if to a target (70:43). Same scene, different simile.
tree:1x6gjxf10r8v6j.relation: The Resurrection scene drawn with two similes.

tree:0t1q79p0ic728p.why: Nothing is hidden from God: Abraham says it in prayer (14:38), and it is shown on the Day when all come out before Him (40:16). Negation differs, which a memorizer must note.

tree:0lv02tn19511rt.why: God does not break His promise: said to those hastening the punishment (22:47) and about the Romans' coming victory (30:6). 'Will never' vs 'does not' is the trap.
tree:0lv02tn19511rt.relation: God's promise holds, whether of punishment or of victory.

tree:0e2yfie0jsz3da.why: Both describe the patient believers who repel evil with good and spend from what they are given, in a different order and with a different reward named.
tree:0e2yfie0jsz3da.relation: The same character praised in two places: patience, repelling evil with good, spending.

tree:1rn0fba11o3bya.why: Two neighbouring ayat: on the Day they are called to prostrate and cannot (68:42), because in the world they were called while healthy and refused (68:43).
tree:1rn0fba11o3bya.relation: Contrast: the call refused in health becomes the call they cannot answer.

tree:1w1acct13pkkzr.why: Those who call to the Fire: idolaters one might marry (2:221) and Pharaoh's leaders (28:41). 2:221 contrasts it with God calling to the Garden.
tree:1w1acct13pkkzr.relation: Contrast: who invites to the Fire and who invites to Paradise.

tree:0q0skmm1sdpbd6.why: Houses of God and the remembrance of His name: the worst wrongdoer prevents it (2:114); in houses God allowed to be raised it is done morning and evening (24:36).
tree:0q0skmm1sdpbd6.relation: Contrast: blocking the mosques vs filling them with remembrance.

tree:0ck2kmb1ihd6zj.why: Both are about God's will in guidance: He did not will to purify some hearts (5:41); whom He wills to guide, He opens his chest (6:125). The words are common but the theme is the same.
tree:0ck2kmb1ihd6zj.relation: God's will behind a heart's purity or openness to Islam.

tree:0o4ad461lvwiow.why: The same warning: do you feel safe that He will not send a storm of stones on you? 'Do you then feel safe' (17:68) vs 'or do you feel safe' (67:17), and what follows differs.

tree:1146qvq00gl73u.why: Both invite people to look at creation: the shadows bowing (16:48) and the sky and earth around them (34:9). The opening differs ('have they not' with and/so).

tree:030ilgs1qwndgu.why: Two reminders of blessings made for people: night for rest and day for sight (27:86), a safe sanctuary (29:67). The opening differs by one letter.
tree:030ilgs1qwndgu.relation: Signs of mercy that should lead to faith, yet they deny.

tree:1dtnbfu1b4iqh2.why: What Satan wants: to lead far astray through seeking judgment from false authorities (4:60), and to sow enmity through wine and gambling (5:91).
tree:1dtnbfu1b4iqh2.relation: Satan's aims named plainly in two places.

tree:0agzlh80mqdj32.why: God will replace you with another people: if you do not go out to fight (9:39), if you turn away from spending (47:38). Same threat, two duties.
tree:0agzlh80mqdj32.relation: God does not need us; turning away from His cause means being replaced.

tree:07k1ff20vl7z9m.why: Both close a parable with 'thus God sets forth parables': the foam and the water (13:17) and the good tree (14:25). Neighbouring surahs, close wording.
tree:07k1ff20vl7z9m.relation: Two parables of truth that lasts: what benefits stays, the good tree gives fruit.

tree:17nu8k4027hozw.why: The words match but the structure does not: 2:102 says the sorcery they learn does harm them and does not benefit, 10:18 says the idols neither harm nor benefit. Under the card rules that is a different phrase, and the subjects (magic, idol worship) differ too.

tree:1hx46p50iq2tzx.why: Both threaten a painful punishment to those who hang back from fighting in God's cause: the believers at Tabuk (9:39) and the Bedouin who stayed behind (48:16).
tree:1hx46p50iq2tzx.relation: Same warning against holding back when called to go out.

tree:1mxv0ql14i9z03.why: Only the short clause 'and pardons much' is shared, with different subjects: the Prophet passing over much that the People of the Book hid (5:15), and God pardoning sins behind misfortunes (42:30). A rare phrase alone with different subjects is not enough.

tree:0gwk7ol0lbfc1r.why: Only the stock closing 'He knows what you do' is shared, with different lead-ins. Keeping oaths (16:91) and God accepting repentance (42:25) are different subjects.

tree:0yrwzpy07xltas.why: Only 'they know that God' is shared. Hypocrites who forget that God knows what they hide (2:77) and the slanderers who will know on the Day that God is the clear Truth (24:25) are different subjects.

tree:1uftfc21rbreh2.why: The only two places where God covers the day with the night, each in a passage listing signs of creation (the heavens and Throne in 7:54, the earth and its fruits in 13:3).
tree:1uftfc21rbreh2.relation: Night and day as a sign of the Creator's ordering.

tree:0ckk3tt0vq96ld.why: Forgiving those who wronged you: Joseph forgives his brothers (12:92), and the believers are told to forgive a relative who slandered (24:22), with 'do you not love that God forgive you?'
tree:0ckk3tt0vq96ld.relation: Similarity: a wronged man's forgiveness of kin, and the hope of God's forgiveness that should move us to it.

tree:077hb2w055vnhs.why: The only two ayat ending 'and they do what they are commanded', both about angels: those who fear their Lord above them (16:50) and the stern keepers of the Fire (66:6).
tree:077hb2w055vnhs.relation: Angels' complete obedience, as worshippers and as guards of the Fire.

tree:1jpuse90nbr081.why: Only 'they have no power over anything' is shared. The showy spender losing his reward (2:264) and the People of the Book having no control of God's grace (57:29) are different subjects.

tree:0gag7nx0qscvyn.why: The same question on the Day of Judgement, 'what answer were you given / did you give?', put to the messengers (5:109) and to the people they were sent to (28:65).
tree:0gag7nx0qscvyn.relation: Both sides of the message are questioned: the senders and the receivers.

tree:1vzgj3w1ryuqh8.why: Two cries of regret: the owner of the ruined garden wishing he had not associated (18:42), and the one given his book in his left hand (69:25). Same words, the world and the Hereafter.
tree:1vzgj3w1ryuqh8.relation: Regret too late, in this life and in the next.

tree:0uk332u0x0371k.why: Believers saying 'our Lord, we believe' and then asking: to be written with the witnesses (5:83), for forgiveness and mercy (23:109). Same opening, different request.

tree:1ysh7cy1788iog.why: Two neighbouring ayat on divorce, both turning on whether the couple can keep within God's limits. A memorizer must keep apart the wording and endings of each.

tree:0xxxygf1vt9wkf.why: Two calls to the believers, to be mindful of God (8:29) and to repent sincerely (66:8), both promising that He will remove their bad deeds, then a different reward.
tree:0xxxygf1vt9wkf.relation: Taqwa and repentance both wipe away sins.

tree:1wsy4wr1p0kdx9.why: Neighbouring surahs, same promise in the singular: whoever believes and does good (64:9) or whoever is mindful of God (65:5) has his sins removed, then the reward differs.

tree:0fyvpy61bqzmag.why: Only the common phrase 'it is not for us to' is shared. Shu'ayb refusing to return to his people's religion (7:89) and the believers told how to answer the slander (24:16) are different subjects.

tree:0fk2x2a180rbey.why: Both deny that God has a son: glory be to Him (4:171) and how could He when He has no consort (6:101).
tree:0fk2x2a180rbey.relation: The same denial argued two ways: transcendence and creation.

tree:1mw42hv15vlw09.why: Two prophets disowning any authority over revelation in the same words: Jesus never said what he had no right to (5:116), Muhammad cannot change the Quran of his own accord (10:15).
tree:1mw42hv15vlw09.relation: Similarity: a messenger only conveys; he does not add or alter.

tree:16qmkb31fhspnv.why: Same surah, same closing that differs in its last word: 'what they used to do' with two different verbs (6:108, 6:159). A classic memorizer's trap.

tree:1yycytr1njvhun.why: Only 'be sent down on you from' is shared. The envy of those who disbelieve (2:105) and the rain at Badr (8:11) are unrelated subjects.

tree:19z3yw60lpqee8.why: Both are signs of the sky with lightning: He sends down hail from mountains of cloud (24:43) and water that revives the earth (30:24).
tree:19z3yw60lpqee8.relation: From the same sky come harm and mercy, fear and hope.

tree:0n3j1do00bg3zi.why: Turning back on one's heels, both as a test of following the Messenger: the change of qibla (2:143) and the rumour of his death at Uhud (3:144).
tree:0n3j1do00bg3zi.relation: Tests that show who truly follows the Messenger.

tree:1dxj4qt171oc6l.why: Who guides to the truth: God, not the partners (10:35), and the Book the jinn heard (46:30).
tree:1dxj4qt171oc6l.relation: God guides to the truth, and so does His Book.

tree:1efd0us02xe9bk.why: Only 'the Day of Resurrection, then' is shared, a common time phrase. Jesus raised up (3:55) and the one who defrauds (3:161) are different subjects.

tree:14y8m231k2kl3n.why: Only 'the Day of Resurrection, what' is shared, and the 'what' is a different word in each (a negation in 5:36, a relative pronoun in 16:92).

tree:0e55gvs19xgwqk.why: Joseph (12:22) and Moses (28:14) receive judgment and knowledge in almost identical ayat, differing only by 'and was mature'; Lot (21:74) shares the gift but continues with his rescue. A key memorizer card.
tree:0e55gvs19xgwqk.relation: Similarity: God's gift of wisdom to prophets as the reward of the doers of good, each then tested.

tree:08uastr14m8w9r.why: The deniers' question 'when we are bones ...?' twice in al-Isra with the same tail (17:49, 17:98) and once in an-Nazi'at with 'decayed' (79:11). The memorizer must keep the tails apart.
tree:08uastr14m8w9r.relation: The same denial of resurrection, answered each time by God's power to create.

tree:0ozij4o0dy5loc.why: Those who believe in God and His messengers: rewarded for not dividing between them (4:152), counted among the truthful and the witnesses (57:19), and the Garden prepared for them (57:21).
tree:0ozij4o0dy5loc.relation: Faith in all the messengers and what it earns.

tree:1yohl1b0scod55.why: The rebuke 'were not My verses recited to you?' to the people of the Fire, with three different endings: turning on heels (23:66), denying (23:105), arrogance (45:31).
tree:1yohl1b0scod55.relation: Every excuse falls away: the verses were recited, and they turned away.

tree:0w9cswh13prj9t.why: Three deeds done seeking God's pleasure: giving one's self (2:207), spending wealth (2:265), and doing good in private counsel (4:114). Same intention, three forms.
tree:0w9cswh13prj9t.relation: Seeking God's pleasure is what gives a deed its worth.

tree:0mwec57183785h.why: The same line of prophets three times close together in al-Baqara: the god of Jacob's fathers (2:133), the faith of believers (2:136), the false claim that they were Jews or Christians (2:140).
tree:0mwec57183785h.relation: One chain of prophets, one religion, claimed wrongly by others.

tree:0j9ami71pxbnxj.why: Following only the revelation: the Prophet says he follows what is revealed to him from his Lord (7:203) and is told twice to follow it (10:109, 33:2), with different tails.
tree:0j9ami71pxbnxj.relation: The Messenger's only path is the revelation.

tree:0tc7mbo0ndco6o.why: A classic: told to follow what God sent down, they answer that they follow their fathers, with 'found' as two different verbs (2:170, 31:21); 7:3 gives the command itself.
tree:0tc7mbo0ndco6o.relation: Revelation against blind imitation of the forefathers.

tree:1vrk9bc18yugj8.why: An appointed term followed by 'then': the term of a life and the return to God (6:60), the stages of the unborn child (22:5), and the sacrificial animals until they reach the House (22:33). The two al-Hajj ayat are a memorizer's pair; 22:33 has a different subject.

tree:0ovpt240gsaa5s.why: God took the covenant of the prophets (3:81), of those given the Book (3:187), and of the Children of Israel (5:12). Same opening, three covenants.
tree:0ovpt240gsaa5s.relation: Covenants taken by God and how each was kept or broken.

tree:1j6tc3n0g54z2h.why: Mocked messengers and the end of their deniers: 'then I seized them, and how was My punishment', with two different last words (13:32, 40:5 vs 22:44).
tree:1j6tc3n0g54z2h.relation: God gives the deniers time, then seizes them.

tree:0rd6fq21cpbgoq.why: Classic mutashabih: Pharaoh's people and those before them were seized for their sins, closing differently in 3:11 and 8:52; 40:21 applies the same to earlier nations.
tree:0rd6fq21cpbgoq.relation: Past nations seized for their sins as a warning to the present.

tree:1dbfakn037nd47.why: The believers driven out of their homes: promised reward (3:195), permitted to fight back (22:40), and given a share of the spoils (59:8).
tree:1dbfakn037nd47.relation: The emigrants' sacrifice and God's answer to it.

tree:1meef7u1xx39vm.why: The Children of Israel told to enter the gate prostrating: the order of the commands is reversed between 2:58 and 7:161, and 4:154 recalls it among the covenants. A key memorizer card.
tree:1meef7u1xx39vm.relation: One command in the story told three times.

tree:0m5buw71wsayih.why: Abraham's words in al-Baqara: his prayer for a safe land (2:126), his argument with the king (2:258), and his request to see the dead raised (2:260). Same opening, close together.
tree:0m5buw71wsayih.relation: Abraham's faith seen in prayer, in debate, and in seeking certainty.

tree:1b5n5ft1sdm71z.why: When God is mentioned: believers' hearts tremble (8:2, 22:35), while the hearts of those who deny the Hereafter shrink when He alone is mentioned (39:45).
tree:1b5n5ft1sdm71z.relation: Contrast: the same remembrance moves one heart to awe and another to disgust.

tree:0n1pger04zd0sl.why: Divorce rulings that open the same way: 2:231 and 2:232 share the first clause then split (do not retain to harm / do not prevent remarriage); 65:1 addresses the Prophet. A memorizer's card.

tree:0pz25k21owkuqw.why: Each time a test comes, a group of them turns: fearing people when fighting is ordered (4:77), turning away from judgment (24:48), associating after relief (30:33).
tree:0pz25k21owkuqw.relation: A pattern of character: a party turns away when faith is tested.

tree:1nfr8k10ba8tdj.why: 'Then I would surely be among the wrongdoers' with different lead-ins: said to the Prophet (2:145), by the witnesses (5:107), and by Noah (11:31). A memorizer's trap.

tree:0lo4iye0uck68o.why: Man's character when evil touches him: despairing (17:83), full of long prayer (41:51), anxious (70:20). 17:83 and 41:51 share the whole first half.
tree:0lo4iye0uck68o.relation: Human weakness in hardship, described from three sides.

tree:1lk3reb08xgnxf.why: God sends a wind on a people: as help for the believers against the confederates (33:9), and as a raging wind destroying 'Ad (41:16, 54:19).
tree:1lk3reb08xgnxf.relation: Contrast: the same wind is victory for believers and destruction for deniers.

tree:1tudq9x015hovz.why: Seeking refuge with God: 7:200 and 41:36 are nearly identical about Satan's prompting, differing in the closing names; 40:56 seeks refuge from proud disputers. A classic memorizer card.

tree:0xq1yrb0urf22x.why: Pharaoh and his chiefs met the signs with arrogance: 'a criminal people' in 7:133 and 10:75, 'a haughty people' in 23:46. Same story, one word changed.

tree:0081pi81he479c.why: Three prayers in Al Imran asking forgiveness of sins, each adding a different request: protection from the Fire (3:16), steadfastness (3:147), dying with the righteous (3:193).

tree:140rdyf1uubj17.why: 'Forgive us and have mercy on us' in three prayers, each closing with a different praise of God: our Protector (2:286), the best of forgivers (7:155), the best of the merciful (23:109).

tree:0cjzslx1in2ah3.why: The command to set one's face to the religion, upright: once in Yunus (10:105) and twice in ar-Rum (30:30, 30:43) with different continuations. A clear memorizer's card.
tree:0cjzslx1in2ah3.relation: The same command tied to the natural disposition (30:30) and to the coming Day (30:43).

tree:0oo78441hbmy9a.why: 'Most of them do not reason' closes three ayat with different lead-ins (and / rather / none). The subjects differ (invented taboos, polytheists who admit God sends rain, people calling from outside the rooms), so its value is mainly for the memorizer.

tree:0wvw7n01k507bq.why: Iblis refusing to prostrate, told three ways: refused and was arrogant (2:34), refused to be with those who prostrate (15:31), refused, end of ayah (20:116). Key memorizer card.
tree:0wvw7n01k507bq.relation: One story: pride as the first disobedience.

tree:1bm26zk1nlwmty.why: The polytheists follow only conjecture and only guess: 6:116 and 10:66 in the third person, 6:148 addressing them directly. Same words, a pronoun to watch.
tree:1bm26zk1nlwmty.relation: Polytheism rests on guesswork, not knowledge.

tree:17jx9970epbjsl.why: What are the deniers waiting for? 6:158 and 16:33 open identically and then differ; 18:55 asks what keeps people from believing, with the same expectation of punishment.
tree:17jx9970epbjsl.relation: Delaying faith until the signs or the punishment come, when it is too late.

tree:1ma02dh1hpdbh9.why: 2:282 and 4:29 both allow trade 'unless it be a trade' (present trade, trade by mutual consent): a real pair on dealings. 28:19 uses the words in a different structure ('unless you want to be a tyrant'), so it is left out.
tree:1ma02dh1hpdbh9.changes: Removed 28:19: its 'that you be' is a different structure and a different subject (the Egyptian accusing Moses).
tree:1ma02dh1hpdbh9.relation: Two rulings on trade: written debts with an exception for cash trade, and lawful trade by consent.

tree:0w7ezrk1g6xr78.why: The hypocrites exposed with 'truly it is they who are ...': the corrupters (2:12), the fools (2:13), the liars (58:18). The two al-Baqara ayat are a famous pair with different endings.
tree:0w7ezrk1g6xr78.relation: What the hypocrites call others is what they are.

tree:1x2of3p0082lab.why: 'Evil indeed is what ...': twice about bearing burdens (6:31, 16:25), once about how they judge a daughter's birth (16:59). The verb at the end is the trap.

tree:1nje9a41u2bicq.why: 'Except a few of them' in the Talut story twice (2:246 turning away from fighting, 2:249 drinking from the river) and in 5:13 about the Children of Israel's treachery. Same people, same pattern.
tree:1nje9a41u2bicq.relation: Only a few remain faithful when tested.

tree:1jutam60m0eaka.why: 4:22 and 4:23, neighbouring ayat on forbidden marriages, both end the ruling with 'except what has already passed'. 41:43 shares only the frame ('except what has been said to the messengers'), a different subject.
tree:1jutam60m0eaka.changes: Removed 41:43: its clause is about what was said to earlier messengers, not about the past being pardoned.

tree:0tl3j3515aahux.why: 'Except whom He has mercy on': no refuge from the flood but His mercy (11:43), people keep differing except whom your Lord has mercy on (11:119), and none is helped on the Day except whom God has mercy on (44:42).
tree:0tl3j3515aahux.relation: God's mercy as the only exception from ruin.

tree:02og4jy1dmoxfa.why: 27:87 and 39:68 describe the blowing of the Trumpet in almost the same words: terror vs swooning, then 'except whom God wills', then different tails. 25:57 is about whoever wills to take a way to his Lord, a different structure and subject.
tree:02og4jy1dmoxfa.changes: Removed 25:57: its 'whoever wills' is the human will to take a path, not God's exception on the Day.
tree:02og4jy1dmoxfa.relation: The Trumpet seen in two moments: terror and swooning.

tree:0t3ldzx0va7zjd.why: 'Only a clear warner' with three lead-ins: 'he is' about the Prophet (7:184), 'I am' from Noah (26:115), 'and I am' from the Prophet (46:9). A memorizer's trap.

tree:1kx13gd1hef4d9.why: Loss in this world and the next with no helper: deeds void (3:22), punishment of the disbelievers (3:56), and the hypocrites who return to disbelief (9:74), whose tail differs.

tree:05qvi0i0u6ryg0.why: To God belongs the heavens and the earth, and to God all returns: 'matters return' in 3:109 and 57:5, 'the destination' in 24:42. A memorizer's trap.

tree:0ksqk6109qz2ld.why: The killing of the prophets without right listed among the crimes of the Children of Israel, three times with different continuations (3:112, 3:181, 4:155).
tree:0ksqk6109qz2ld.relation: One crime recalled in each charge sheet against them.

tree:0ycm4a709lv8ql.why: The Garden promised to the mindful: described with rivers and shade (13:35), with rivers of water, milk, wine and honey (47:15), and as the eternal Garden contrasted with the Fire (25:15).

tree:0lp9ixr1dglw9z.why: Worldly life, then the Day: the enjoyment of this life then return to Us (10:23), then brought to account (28:61), then disowning each other (29:25).
tree:0lp9ixr1dglw9z.relation: What is enjoyed together in this life is followed by reckoning.

tree:0qweih90ysoem3.why: Wanting this life and its adornment: paid in full here (11:15), what is with God is better (28:60), the Prophet's wives offered the choice (33:28).
tree:0qweih90ysoem3.relation: The choice between this world's adornment and what is with God.

tree:0gs3pec10m5m9g.why: 31:33 and 35:5 share the warning 'let not the life of this world deceive you'; 18:28 tells the Prophet not to turn his eyes from the poor believers seeking this world's adornment. Same warning about the world's lure.

tree:1ksc6m802fe51k.why: 'Fear God, to whom you will be gathered' closes rulings on hunting in ihram (5:96) and on private talk (58:9); 6:72 has 'and He it is'. A memorizer's trap.

tree:1bq27aj19c5lad.why: 6:99 and 16:10 both open 'He it is who sends down water from the sky' and then list what grows from it. 4:136 uses the words for the Book sent down before, a different structure.
tree:1bq27aj19c5lad.changes: Removed 4:136: its 'sent down before' is about earlier scripture, not rain from the sky.
tree:1bq27aj19c5lad.relation: Water from the sky as the source of life and provision.

tree:13yi9k80a0wg6s.why: The Quran confirms what came before it: 6:92, and twice with 'it is not forged, but a confirmation ... and a detailing' with different objects (10:37, 12:111).

tree:12p0zrz1mn1k8l.why: Rewarded by the best of what they did (29:7, 39:35) and punished by the worst of what they did (41:27). Same words, one changed.
tree:12p0zrz1mn1k8l.relation: Contrast: believers judged by their best deeds, deniers by their worst.

tree:0iq8gqk1bhnp1u.why: He who gives life and death: Abraham's answer to the king (2:258), and twice as His description with different tails (23:80, 40:68).
tree:0iq8gqk1bhnp1u.relation: Life and death as the proof of the Lord.

tree:0qi9dff0iurgpv.why: Both speak of the believers among you and of succession on earth: God promises to make them successors (24:55), and tells them to spend from what He made them successors over (57:7).
tree:0qi9dff0iurgpv.relation: Succession on earth is both a promise and a trust to spend from.

tree:0v455xi1ocvaj8.why: 'Those who were mindful of their Lord': 3:198 and 39:20 open with the same 'but' and give gardens vs lofty rooms; 39:73 shows them driven to the Garden in groups. A real slip for memorizers.
tree:0v455xi1ocvaj8.relation: The reward of the mindful: gardens, rooms, and the welcome at the gates.

tree:1nsju9x0orrfnr.why: 'Those of them who did wrong': an exception in 2:150 and 29:46, and those who changed the word in 7:162 (where 'of them' is the detail that differs from 2:59). Useful for memorizers.

tree:1wugham0nmo2z8.why: Only 'those who disbelieved, to' is shared, in three senses: until the Day (3:55), gathered to Hell (8:36), driven to Hell (39:71). The Hell pair already has its own card; 3:55 is unrelated.

tree:0el1dob0kyv821.why: Only the phrase 'those who disbelieved in their Lord' is shared; the three ayat say different things (they set up equals, they bear chains, their deeds are ashes). Nothing to confuse or ponder together.

tree:0nksemv1r7fi4z.why: Only 'those who disbelieved: no' is shared, with three unrelated sayings (the Hour will not come, do not listen to the Quran, make no excuses today).

tree:0qfhhcv138dpnn.why: 3:10 and 3:116 are identical for most of the ayah and end differently (fuel of the Fire / companions of the Fire). 34:31 is the deniers' 'we will never believe', a different structure.
tree:0qfhhcv138dpnn.changes: Removed 34:31: its 'never' is their own vow not to believe, not the wealth that will not avail.

tree:1sgi4uy19fng6y.why: 'Those who disbelieved will have' is a stock opening of the punishment formula, found in many places. These three ayat add nothing that sets them apart from the rest.

tree:0jond7x0s2u9j3.why: Only 'those who disbelieved ... if' is shared, in three unrelated settings (prayer in fear, ransom on the Day, wishing they were Muslims).

tree:02nmnmv0m7a3yd.why: The deniers' demand for a sign: 13:7 and 13:27 identical and then answered differently; 25:32 asks why the Quran was not sent down all at once.
tree:02nmnmv0m7a3yd.relation: Demands for signs, answered with what the Messenger is and why revelation came gradually.

tree:0xpvho40vpzf20.why: 'Where are your / My partners whom you claimed?': 'your partners' in 6:22 and 'My partners' twice in al-Qasas (28:62, 28:74). A pronoun a memorizer must hold.

tree:0r1qvd80o2xaue.why: In at-Tawba, the believers who find nothing but their effort are mocked by hypocrites (9:79), and those who find nothing to spend are excused (9:91). 24:33 is about those unable to marry, a different subject.
tree:0r1qvd80o2xaue.changes: Removed 24:33 (those who cannot find means to marry), which shares only the frame.
tree:0r1qvd80o2xaue.relation: God values the poor believer's small effort that the hypocrites mock.

tree:0xfiepl1yo7i4v.why: Only 'those after them' is shared: the followers of the messengers fighting (2:253) and the nations after Noah (40:31). Unrelated subjects.

tree:0cqcfp2151v06k.why: Three places telling what God forbade the Jews and why: for their wrongdoing (4:160), for their transgression (6:146), and 'We did not wrong them' (16:118).
tree:0cqcfp2151v06k.relation: The prohibitions on the Jews were a penalty for their own wrong.

tree:0zad4xc1dczn12.why: Only 'those who are, from ...' is shared, a grammatical frame with different objects (signs, idle talk, prayer) and opposite subjects (deniers and believers).

tree:0jxw71m02ro8t0.why: 21:16 and 38:27: We did not create the heaven and earth and what is between in play / in vain. 44:29 (the sky did not weep for them) only touches the words with a different structure.
tree:0jxw71m02ro8t0.changes: Removed 44:29: there 'and what' is a negation in another clause, not 'and what is between them'.
tree:0jxw71m02ro8t0.relation: Creation has a purpose, against the deniers' assumption.

tree:1p4sjnt1pcwljb.why: 11:107 and 11:108 are mirror ayat: the people of the Fire and of the Garden abide as long as heavens and earth last, except as your Lord wills, then different endings. 19:93 is a different structure.
tree:1p4sjnt1pcwljb.changes: Removed 19:93: its 'except' follows a negation of everyone coming as a servant, a different structure.
tree:1p4sjnt1pcwljb.relation: Contrast: the same eternal abiding, for the wretched and for the happy.

tree:0024pow1u55k90.why: Questions about the heavens and earth answered by 'say: God': to whom belongs (6:12, 'to God'), who is Lord (13:16), who provides (34:24).
tree:0024pow1u55k90.relation: Arguing from creation to God's sole right to worship.

tree:0mfcqy102whqmf.why: Only 'the heavens and the earth, not' is shared, and the 'not' starts a different sentence each time (no god but He, it will not come but suddenly, they are not equal).

tree:0hcoqvy0go1swa.why: Intercession only for one granted it: who took a covenant with the Merciful (19:87), whom the Merciful permits (20:109), who bore witness to the truth (43:86).
tree:0hcoqvy0go1swa.relation: Intercession belongs to God and is given only by His leave.

tree:0au26pz1s6au7b.why: Sun, moon and stars made subservient by His command (7:54, 16:12, same words), and prostrating to Him (22:18).
tree:0au26pz1s6au7b.relation: The heavenly bodies serve and worship their Creator.

tree:1usc1n11rsslmv.why: Glad tidings to those who do good deeds: gardens (2:25), a great reward (17:9), a good reward (18:2). Neighbouring 17:9 and 18:2 differ by one word.

tree:1m13ar911h020j.why: Punishment 'because of what they used to ...', ending with three different verbs: defiantly disobey (6:49), turn away (6:157), spread corruption (16:88). A memorizer's trap.

tree:15w2typ1r6lyu1.why: The punishment on the Day of Resurrection: doubled for the sinner (25:69), the evil punishment twice in az-Zumar (39:24, 39:47).

tree:1x0ye7m1mydyye.why: The Book, judgment and prophethood given to prophets: none would then call to worship himself (3:79), if these reject it others will hold it (6:89), and given to the Children of Israel (45:16).
tree:1x0ye7m1mydyye.relation: The trust of the Book and prophethood, and how it passes on.

tree:1wtpprn09e5tjn.why: Lying knowingly: some of the People of the Book say lies about God while they know (3:75, 3:78), and hypocrites swear to lies while they know (58:14). The verb before it (say / swear) is the trap.
tree:1wtpprn09e5tjn.relation: Deliberate lying about God and under oath.

tree:014w1v11hjl7m3.why: Only 'God' next to 'those who disbelieved' is shared, across three unrelated sentences (worst of creatures, the Fire promised, turned back in rage).

tree:0zpzdiq1m8mfb2.why: God, the One, the Subduer, closing three ayat with different lead-ins: Joseph's question to his prison companions (12:39), 'no god but' (38:65), 'He is' (39:4).
tree:0zpzdiq1m8mfb2.relation: Oneness argued against many lords, against other gods, against a son.

tree:0hjyokj1vx4b3f.why: 'God sees His servants' closes three ayat: after God's pleasure for the mindful (3:15), after 'your duty is only to convey' (3:20), and after the believer of Pharaoh's people entrusts his affair to God (40:44).

tree:06b06240svkys2.why: Selling God's signs or covenant for a small price: the believing People of the Book do not (3:199), the oath-breakers did (9:9), and believers are told not to (16:95).
tree:06b06240svkys2.relation: The small price of this world against what is with God.

tree:0iybcsn0zasqcj.why: 'Better and more lasting': the converted magicians about God (20:73), and what is with God set against worldly enjoyment, twice with different tails (28:60, 42:36).
tree:0iybcsn0zasqcj.relation: What is with God outlasts everything this world gives.

tree:0aqsjx50dsrx1x.why: 'God is full of bounty' on the worlds (2:251), on the believers (3:152), great bounty (3:174). The ending is the trap.

tree:0wboesr0pcnp0n.why: 59:6 and 59:7 are neighbouring ayat on what God gave His Messenger as spoils without fighting. 9:97 has 'what God sent down to His Messenger', a different verb and subject.
tree:0wboesr0pcnp0n.changes: Removed 9:97: it is about revelation sent down, not spoils given.

tree:02ee8721umpb1o.why: 'Those whom God has favoured among the prophets': the company of the obedient (4:69) and the prophets who fell in prostration (19:58). 6:53 uses another verb, a different phrase.
tree:02ee8721umpb1o.changes: Removed 6:53: it has a different verb in a mocking question, not the favoured prophets.
tree:02ee8721umpb1o.relation: Those God favoured, and the promise to be with them.

tree:1tp2bkq1nq35pc.why: 'God is Free of need, Praiseworthy' closes three ayat on spending, gratitude and disbelief, with three different lead-ins ('that', 'then indeed', 'and God'). A memorizer's trap.
tree:1tp2bkq1nq35pc.relation: God needs neither our charity, our thanks nor our faith.

tree:0jq3g8p0gzzczz.why: A pattern: 'whoever ... God, then God is ...' with three different closings (swift in account, mighty and wise, severe in punishment). Subjects differ; the value is keeping the closings apart.

tree:0wdddkn05ioug7.why: 'For them is a punishment' is one of the commonest formulas; here it follows different subjects (disbelieving in the signs, hurting the Prophet, straying from God's way). Nothing to set these three apart.

tree:0q13sgk03k6wwq.why: 'God ... what He wills' is a very common phrase; here with three different verbs (erases, does, creates) and unrelated subjects. Nothing specific to learn from these three.

tree:1x8jgv01m862k8.why: Blocking believers from God's way: the People of the Book (3:99) and Shu'ayb's people (7:86), in nearly the same words. 9:18 ('who maintains the mosques is he who believes') is a different structure.
tree:1x8jgv01m862k8.changes: Removed 9:18: its 'who believes' is the subject of a different sentence.
tree:1x8jgv01m862k8.relation: The same sin in two nations: barring believers and seeking to make the path crooked.

tree:1amnnfb02xcpyt.why: 'God and His Messenger, those ...': those who obey them will receive mercy (9:71), those who oppose them are among the most humiliated (58:20), the emigrants who support them are the truthful (59:8).
tree:1amnnfb02xcpyt.relation: Contrast: obeying and supporting God and His Messenger vs opposing them.

tree:1ubgnxt083sohz.why: 8:20 and 8:46 both command obeying God and His Messenger, then 'do not' with a different warning (turning away / disputing). 9:29 only has 'what God and His Messenger forbade', a different structure.
tree:1ubgnxt083sohz.changes: Removed 9:29: its 'and not' begins a list of the enemy's traits, not a command to believers.

tree:0y1qiso0et6lxy.why: These are three of many an-Nisa ayat closing with 'and God is ...'; the subjects (spending, manslaughter, emigration) are unrelated. A general pattern, not a card.

tree:18q65fe1xqal8a.why: 'And for them is a punishment' is a stock closing; the three ayat (hypocrites, those who reject the signs, apostates) end with three different adjectives but share nothing more specific.

tree:16bpoqk10th5w2.why: 'God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection' in 4:141 and 22:69. 60:10 is God's present ruling on emigrant women, a different sense of judging.
tree:16bpoqk10th5w2.changes: Removed 60:10: there it is a legal ruling now, not the judgment of the Day.
tree:16bpoqk10th5w2.relation: Disputes left to God's judgment on the Day.

tree:0l71jty1p058d0.why: 'Did I not tell you?' from God to the angels (2:33), from Jacob when his sight returned (12:96), and from the best of the garden owners (68:28). Each time the one who knew is proven right.
tree:0l71jty1p058d0.relation: Knowledge vindicated: God, Jacob, and the wise brother.

tree:107xelt195stpp.why: Mankind as one nation: they were one and then differed (2:213), God could have made them one (11:118), and if not for that risk He would give the deniers houses of silver (43:33).
tree:107xelt195stpp.relation: Unity and difference among people as part of God's plan.

tree:1bhaehy0n1x5lw.why: Asking for a short delay: from the fighting (4:77), from the punishment (14:44), from death to give charity (63:10). Three forms of the verb, one wish.
tree:1bhaehy0n1x5lw.relation: Wishing for time that will not be given.

tree:0lzvu2u154ixgg.why: 'And to God is the destination' closes three ayat after different lead-ins: a warning about taking disbelievers as allies (3:28), God's dominion (24:42), purification (35:18).

tree:0x35lyp1i5jmqh.why: Classic al-Ma'ida pair: 'to God is your return, all of you, and He will inform you of what you ...' ending 'differ about' (5:48) vs 'do' (5:105); 11:4 has the short form.

tree:1vdnadi0ymscpk.why: 24:48 and 24:51 contrast the hypocrites who turn away when called to God and His Messenger for judgment with the believers who say we hear and obey. 4:100 (emigrating to God and His Messenger) is a different structure.
tree:1vdnadi0ymscpk.changes: Removed 4:100: emigrating to God is not the call to judgment.
tree:1vdnadi0ymscpk.relation: Contrast: the same call answered by turning away and by obedience.

tree:0b3f9k51jnikk5.why: Taking a way to one's Lord: 73:19 and 76:29 are identical ('this is a reminder, so whoever wills ...'), and 25:57 says the Prophet asks no wage except that people take that way.
tree:0b3f9k51jnikk5.relation: The message is a reminder; the choice to take the path is left to each person.

tree:12h12qt1h5jk5x.why: The Prophet states his command: to worship God and not associate (13:36), to worship the Lord of this city (27:91), to worship God sincerely (39:11). Close wording, different objects.

tree:1ajoseb1tojsad.why: 'That was a nation that has passed' twice in al-Baqara (2:134, 2:141, identical), and 13:30 sends the Prophet to a nation before which nations had passed.
tree:1ajoseb1tojsad.relation: Each generation bears its own deeds; ancestry does not save.

tree:0lbvlob1w7uw67.why: 'Had God willed He would have made you one nation, but ...' with three reasons: to test you (5:48), He guides and leaves astray (16:93), He admits whom He wills to His mercy (42:8).
