tree:0ho75930zuogzx.why: An ayah ending about what they doubted: the punishment brought to Lut's people (15:63), and Isa, the word of truth (19:34). Different subjects but a shared ending a memorizer can confuse. Both rows read on into the next ayah.

tree:146w4y10msh77b.why: The law of retaliation written in the Torah (5:45) and the arrogant in the Fire (40:48): different particles and structures.

tree:0x5c7js0h2227i.why: The cup of Paradise: passed among them without idle talk (52:23), served mixed with ginger (76:17). Same scene, different completion.
tree:0x5c7js0h2227i.relation: The drink of Paradise, free of sin and fragrant.

tree:14itmts131l7g8.why: No fatigue touches the people of Paradise: said of them (15:48) and said by them in thanks (35:35). Same promise, different person.
tree:14itmts131l7g8.relation: The promise of rest, then the believers voicing it in Paradise.

tree:1vn8in61k8txew.why: Regret over neglect of the Hour (6:31) and full payment in this world (11:15): a pronoun and a conjunction meet by chance.

tree:11hej170ik3vp9.why: Had God known good in them (8:23) and if you know good in your slaves (24:33): the same phrase, entirely different subjects.

tree:15agzqa0largwa.why: Two descriptions of the gardens in ar-Rahman: two springs flowing (55:50) and two springs gushing (55:66). A classic memorizer pair.
tree:15agzqa0largwa.relation: The higher pair of gardens and the lower pair, told apart by their springs.

tree:0i4purg1moypto.why: Enter the Fire with the nations (7:38) and enter Egypt in safety (12:99): a common verb, unrelated scenes.

tree:0sr44nf0rmiaoj.why: Two prophets answer a threat with the same question: Shuayb to the chiefs who threaten exile (7:88), Musa to Pharaoh who threatens prison (26:30).
tree:0sr44nf0rmiaoj.relation: A prophet threatened by the powerful answers: even if?

tree:0ogsrzi09nx2uc.why: Musa's two replies, about the place they sought (18:64) and the agreement with his father-in-law (28:28), share only the opening said, that. No point together.

tree:0im1h130n0rg99.why: Two prophets answer their deniers by leaving the matter to their Lord's knowledge: the Prophet (21:4) and Shuayb (26:188). Short replies easy to confuse.
tree:0im1h130n0rg99.relation: The prophet's answer to denial: my Lord knows.

tree:18dyeat1v8unl9.why: Two prophets begin with glory to You when facing God: Isa disowning what was said of him (5:116), Musa after asking to see God (7:143).
tree:18dyeat1v8unl9.relation: Prophets answer God's majesty by declaring Him free of all fault.

tree:1x6vjju147feeg.why: Musa twice says perhaps my Lord or perhaps your Lord: comforting his people (7:129) and setting out to Madyan alone (28:22). His hope in God, for others and for himself.
tree:1x6vjju147feeg.relation: Musa's hope in his Lord, alone in flight and as leader of his people.

tree:1613sx30iug3cf.why: Two times in the same surah a firm no: God reassures Musa before Pharaoh (26:15), and Musa reassures his people at the sea (26:62).
tree:1613sx30iug3cf.relation: Musa received the reassurance from God, and later gave it to his people with the same word.

tree:0jkwri11mvquy5.why: Ibrahim's fear of going astray (6:77) and Pharaoh's threat of prison (26:29) share only the opening particle. Different structures and subjects.

tree:1a8zq9d06znist.why: You will not see Me (7:143) and I will not send him (12:66): the negation is a common word, the scenes unrelated.

tree:1x4tjwb1d2n67b.why: Lut's wish for strength (11:80) and Musa's remark about payment (18:77): a common conditional particle, nothing in common.

tree:03dzhlf1csmult.why: Who are my helpers (3:52) and who will revive bones (36:78): an interrogative only, unrelated subjects.

tree:0v5hv411ubru6b.why: She seduced me (12:26) and it is my staff (20:18): a pronoun after said, unrelated.

tree:12du92a1ydfcli.why: God's reply about the disbeliever's provision (2:126) and Ibrahim's reply about despair (15:56): the shared opening is a different structure each time.

tree:1yma44u1rvqdc6.why: Two sons address their fathers about a dream: Yusuf when it comes true (12:100), Ismail when told to obey it (37:102). A meaningful pair for pondering.
tree:1yma44u1rvqdc6.relation: Prophetic dreams between father and son: one fulfilled in honour, one accepted in submission.

tree:00zneje0nejbag.why: Adam addressed by name twice: God tells him to inform the angels (2:33), Satan tempts him with the tree (20:120).
tree:00zneje0nejbag.relation: Contrast: God's call to Adam raises him with knowledge, Satan's call deceives him.

tree:0c5e0xx1hfvn47.why: Sulayman addresses two audiences in one surah: the people about the favour given him (27:16), the chiefs about the throne (27:38). A memorizer pair.
tree:0c5e0xx1hfvn47.relation: Sulayman's speech to his people and to his court.

tree:0ehi8pk0k6409u.why: Two wishes: the believing man in Paradise wishes his people knew (36:26), the denier wishes he were far from his companion (43:38). Same opening, opposite ends.
tree:0ehi8pk0k6409u.relation: Contrast: a wish of mercy from Paradise and a wish of regret from the punishment.

tree:1bfh7nu1xwkbcq.why: Two pairs pray together, our Lord: Adam and his wife confessing wrong (7:23), Musa and Harun voicing fear (20:45). Same opening, a memorizer pair.
tree:1bfh7nu1xwkbcq.relation: Two pairs turn to their Lord, one in repentance and one in fear.

tree:07ofr9411y0648.why: The sayings of the Jews and the Christians set side by side: each denies the other (2:113), each claims a son for God (9:30). Same frame, and both compare them to earlier deniers.
tree:07ofr9411y0648.relation: The claims of the two peoples of the Book, about each other and about God.

tree:13nuopk0muqcao.why: The queen on what kings do (27:34) and the daughter of Madyan inviting Musa (28:25) share only the opening she said. Unrelated.

tree:1xqww4j1idor17.why: A party says something meant to make the believers turn back: People of the Book plotting a feigned faith (3:72) and hypocrites at the Trench telling Yathrib to go home (33:13).
tree:1xqww4j1idor17.relation: The enemies within use words to make the believers go back.

tree:1qwbm091slqjlv.why: A rare command, build a building, said over the youths of the cave (18:21) and for Ibrahim's fire (37:97). Easy to confuse in recitation; very different ends.
tree:1qwbm091slqjlv.relation: One building honours the sleepers, the other is built to burn a prophet.

tree:0kyckbo0uyr4e4.why: The angels rebuke those who did not emigrate (4:97) and the hypocrites claim a share (4:141). Both use a rhetorical question, but speakers and subjects differ.

tree:0gp9b1u12xv544.why: Ibrahim's people admit their own wrong (21:64) and followers blame their leaders in Hell (37:28). A pronoun after they said, nothing more.

tree:0bua27j06sch8t.why: Lut's people (15:70) and the keepers of Hell (40:50) ask different questions with the same particle. Unrelated.

tree:1jh3gh01gmkfky.why: A people explaining hardship as normal (7:95) and deniers boasting they could say the like (8:31). The particle is all that is shared.

tree:05qzzfj03idtvx.why: The deniers say their hearts are wrapped: as covered (2:88) and in coverings against the call (41:5). The same excuse in two forms.
tree:05qzzfj03idtvx.relation: Closed hearts claimed as an excuse, answered with God's curse in one and a challenge in the other.

tree:1bqt4qm0z9cia6.why: Same surah, same battle: the hypocrites tell their brothers that had they stayed home they would not have died (3:156, 3:168). God answers both times.
tree:1bqt4qm0z9cia6.relation: The hypocrites' claim that staying back saves from death, and God's reply.

tree:0iapjjl0q4qyr7.why: In one surah, the hypocrites speak to two groups: mocking questions to the people of knowledge (47:16) and secret promises to those who hate the revelation (47:26). A memorizer pair that also shows their two faces.
tree:0iapjjl0q4qyr7.relation: The hypocrites' two faces: mockery to the believers, loyalty to the deniers.

tree:17bzbl70lzk139.why: Pharaoh's people claiming the good (7:131) and believers declining idle talk (28:55): the shared words are a different structure.

tree:0lw8md501glqgd.why: Who did this to our gods (21:59) and who is stronger than us (41:15): unrelated questions.

tree:17dk2de1r5491q.why: Asked what they worship, Yaqub's sons answer your God and the God of your fathers (2:133), Ibrahim's people answer idols (26:71).
tree:17dk2de1r5491q.relation: Contrast: Ibrahim's descendants inherit his faith, his people inherit idols.

tree:1u7lfbp0najj77.why: The deniers' excuse, we found our fathers doing it, for shameful deeds (7:28) and for idol worship (21:53). Word order differs, a memorizer pair.
tree:1u7lfbp0najj77.relation: Blind following of the fathers as an excuse for sin and for shirk.

tree:1gx4q6w0776jpo.why: Why should we not fight (2:246) and what is the Most Merciful (25:60): the shared words are a different structure.

tree:0i7yt5o0vjsz7s.why: Two replies of Madyan to Shuayb in the same surah, both opening by his name: mockery of his prayer (11:87) and contempt for his weakness (11:91).
tree:0i7yt5o0vjsz7s.relation: Shuayb's people move from mockery to threat.

tree:06n1eh00cqhwz4.why: Thamud addresses Salih by name: challenging him to bring the punishment (7:77) and reproaching his hope among them (11:62).
tree:06n1eh00cqhwz4.relation: Salih's people, once hopeful of him, end by daring the punishment.

tree:082nqq40z3ab9g.why: Towns destroyed before the Day of Resurrection (17:58) and deniers asking for their share before the Reckoning (38:16): different names of the Day, different points.

tree:06lo88b0yu4ew7.why: Musa's killing of a man recalled twice: by God as a favour of rescue (20:40), and by the Israelite as a reproach (28:19).
tree:06lo88b0yu4ew7.relation: The same deed seen by God, who saved him, and by a man who threw it at him.

tree:1mgl6hs0mqrqk0.why: Two commands to fight in al-Tawba, naming two groups: the People of the Book who reject faith (9:29) and the deniers nearest you (9:123). A memorizer pair.
tree:1mgl6hs0mqrqk0.relation: Whom to fight, by belief and by nearness.

tree:1kjknf60a3nhuo.why: God has encompassed it, said of spoils not yet won (48:21) and of all things in knowledge (65:12), both beside God having power over all things. Close wording.
tree:1kjknf60a3nhuo.relation: What is beyond our reach is within God's power and knowledge.

tree:0iyy6pm024rvh8.why: Yusuf thanks God for His kindness (12:100) and God has made fine provision for the believer (65:11): different subjects, only a verb shared.

tree:0hsfzg51xrahwl.why: Yaqub took a pledge from his sons (12:80) and God took the believers' covenant (57:8). Different takers and points, only the phrase shared.

tree:12cnvtk06dqoe8.why: Clothing sent down to the children of Adam (7:26) and clear ayat sent down against opponents (58:5): a common verb phrase, unrelated.

tree:0x8c3gg09ig6iw.why: Right made clear from error (2:256) and ruins made clear to you (29:38): a common verb, unrelated subjects.

tree:0j2x6by0uqplns.why: The command of your Lord has come for Lut's people (11:76) and the signs of the Hour have come (47:18): a common verb phrase, different subjects.

tree:1jmec5r0r6rl81.why: A stream placed below Maryam (19:24) and a measure set for everything (65:3): only the phrase has made.

tree:0qw5e3i0hzhjye.why: Two definitions of success: being moved from the Fire into Paradise (3:185), and obeying God and His messenger (33:71). Same words, different completion.
tree:0qw5e3i0hzhjye.relation: True success is escaping the Fire, and the way to it is obedience.

tree:0xbkv4405jgsfi.why: A party distorting God's word (2:75) and a sign in two armies (3:13): only the particle and verb are shared.

tree:1aat2501bbktks.why: My ayat were recited to you (23:66) and a good example in Ibrahim (60:4): only the opening particle and verb.

tree:0nzcl0l1hnlvcr.why: The same consolation to the Prophet, if they deny you, others denied before: naming the peoples (22:42) and the messengers (35:4).
tree:0nzcl0l1hnlvcr.relation: Consolation: denial is the old way of nations with their messengers.

tree:084ygvn1xd81o9.why: Deniers who rejected it before (34:53) and enemies who rejected the truth (60:1): a common verb, different subjects.

tree:0o819xd0jrsm4b.why: Salih's people recall their hope in him (11:62) and the blind man recalls he could see (20:125): only you had been.

tree:1ilom7d08b3ju5.why: A wound touched the other side too (3:140) and hardship touched our fathers (7:95): the same verb, different points.

tree:1wpavpr1rnxdun.why: The emigrant's reward falls due with God (4:100) and wrath has fallen on Hud's people (7:71): a common verb, different subjects.

tree:16e9n8c02085tc.why: An ayah ending, a clear Quran, after the Book's ayat (15:1) and after a reminder (36:69). Both describe the revelation; a memorizer must keep the openings apart. Both rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:16e9n8c02085tc.relation: The Quran described as clear: its ayat and its reminder.

tree:0dgcxjv0zyou1n.why: Comfort of the eyes: what the servants of the Merciful ask for in their families (25:74), and what is hidden for believers as reward (32:17).
tree:0dgcxjv0zyou1n.relation: The comfort of the eyes asked for in this life and kept hidden for the next.

tree:0600ubr0hqfdrt.why: A town that was: safe and content until it denied God's blessings (16:112), and wrongdoing so it was broken (21:11). A memorizer pair about towns punished.
tree:0600ubr0hqfdrt.relation: Ingratitude and wrongdoing bring ruin to a town.

tree:1df7uu103m4hmb.why: Hardened hearts: those who would not humble themselves in hardship (6:43), and the People of the Book after a long time (57:16), a warning to the believers.
tree:1df7uu103m4hmb.relation: How hearts harden: refusing humility in trial and letting time pass without remembrance.

tree:0f627pp0vqi2c5.why: Two laws of retaliation, each ending in a conditional: whoever transgresses may be answered in kind (2:194), whoever forgoes it earns expiation (5:45).
tree:0f627pp0vqi2c5.relation: Retaliation is allowed, but forgoing it is better: the right and the virtue.

tree:149vh271wuuuaf.why: What We told you before about foods forbidden to the Jews (16:118) and the messengers We told you of (40:78): the same verb phrase, different subjects.

tree:1xoy21t154uddj.why: A rare phrase, We decreed to, used of the Children of Israel in the Book (17:4) and of Musa receiving the command (28:44). Both about God's word to Musa's people.
tree:1xoy21t154uddj.relation: What God decreed to Musa, and what He decreed about his people's future.

tree:1ku34vt0aikvl9.why: In Yusuf, the women cut their hands when they saw him (12:31), and Yusuf later asks the king about those very women (12:50). The second recalls the first.
tree:1ku34vt0aikvl9.relation: The event and its later use to clear Yusuf's name.

tree:0b9z8hc1bb0f8w.why: Two prayers that open, say O God, then a title: Owner of the kingdom (3:26) and Originator of the heavens and earth (39:46).
tree:0b9z8hc1bb0f8w.relation: The Prophet taught to address God by His kingship and by His creation and judgement.

tree:0qe0r4j1wi8c4v.why: The same answer, even if?, against blind following: even if the intercessors have no power (39:43), even if I bring better guidance than your fathers (43:24).
tree:0qe0r4j1wi8c4v.relation: Reason against blind loyalty to idols and to ancestors.

tree:108wmqh0v5k9mr.why: Say: come, opens two invitations: to the mutual curse with the Christians (3:61) and to hear what God has forbidden (6:151). A memorizer pair.
tree:108wmqh0v5k9mr.relation: The Prophet's call to settle a dispute and to learn God's commands.

tree:0q8axt00eioxne.why: Say: peace, to the believers who come with mercy and forgiveness (6:54) and to the deniers as a parting word before they will know (43:89).
tree:0q8axt00eioxne.relation: Contrast: peace as welcome to believers and as farewell to deniers.

tree:031cnud0n2y6ud.why: Then why, the Prophet's answer to two claims of the People of the Book: that they believe (2:91) and that they are God's beloved (5:18). Same argument shape.
tree:031cnud0n2y6ud.relation: Their own deeds and God's punishment refute their claims.

tree:07mnalk0qt6bm0.why: Say to My servants, then a command: to pray and spend (14:31), to speak the best words (17:53). God's tender address, a memorizer pair.
tree:07mnalk0qt6bm0.relation: God calls the believers My servants, then teaches them worship and speech.

tree:0udjtef08o3n7t.why: Turning away paired with a fitting word: eloquent words to the hypocrites (4:63) and gentle words to those you cannot help (17:28). The same instruction of tact in two settings.
tree:0udjtef08o3n7t.relation: Even when turning away, the believer is told to speak a suitable word.

tree:0uv1t7z1djv8pr.why: About the new moons (2:189) and about the good things of life (7:32): the answer formula say, they are, opens two unrelated rulings.

tree:1erv57o0j0uv8q.why: His heart is sinful for hiding testimony (2:283) and God guides his heart (64:11): only the noun and the ending formula meet.

tree:10jkzqk0nih0iy.why: What believers should have said about the slander (24:16) and what deniers said about the Hour (45:32): the shared words are a different structure.

tree:12fpva21ctdwge.why: God's two addresses to Adam: dwell in the Garden (2:35) and this is your enemy (20:117). A key memorizer pair in the story of Adam.
tree:12fpva21ctdwge.relation: The gift of the Garden and the warning that came with it.

tree:1fpesz50bz81mz.why: Oaths your hearts intended (2:225) and testing what is in your hearts at Uhud (3:154): the shared words are a noun and the opening of different ending formulas.

tree:1lrrawd0q0ocnp.why: Hypocrisy in their hearts until the Day (9:77) and hearts softening to God's remembrance (39:23): different structures.

tree:033g6p01gem8p8.why: Two neighbouring ayat, two kinds of hearts: sick and hard ones, tested by Satan's whispers (22:53), and humble ones that submit to the truth (22:54).
tree:033g6p01gem8p8.relation: Contrast: the same trial hardens some hearts and humbles others.

tree:17symqy1cuz4h8.why: Few of My servants are grateful (34:13) and few of the later ones (56:14): a common phrase, different subjects.

tree:048jzqf1u6i7k9.why: A little, then: you will return (44:15), you are criminals (77:46). Both are short reprieves for deniers, ending differently.
tree:048jzqf1u6i7k9.relation: The deniers' respite is short and changes nothing.

tree:17xs1gs1hy0l8o.why: God gives the deniers a little enjoyment, then drives them to punishment: in reply to Ibrahim (2:126) and as a general rule (31:24). Same wording, first person and plural.

tree:0tedvcy07urlve.why: God heard those who said He is poor (3:181) and they imitate the deniers before them (9:30): a generic phrase, different points.

tree:10buml919nncml.why: The same command, fear God and speak a right word: to guardians of orphans (4:9) and to all believers (33:70). Each row reads on into the next ayah, which shows its fruit.
tree:10buml919nncml.relation: Right speech as a fruit of fearing God, in a family duty and in general.

tree:0n3zcxo0pq3fuw.why: Their claim to have killed the Messiah (4:157) and God's reassurance against what they say (36:76): different structures.

tree:1m9ve3e1ad3ugm.why: Two lists of peoples who denied their messengers, each naming Ibrahim's people, then Madyan or Lut. A memorizer must keep the lists apart.
tree:1m9ve3e1ad3ugm.relation: The same line of destroyed peoples, in a warning to hypocrites and in comfort to the Prophet.

tree:0ek70et1ihzalp.why: Two rulings in al-Maida, hatred of a people that barred you (5:2) and a people who meant to attack (5:11). The particle that follows is a different structure each time.

tree:1u89rd91f16j0r.why: The people of Tubba named among destroyed nations in two surahs, once as a question to Quraysh (44:37), once in a list (50:14). A rare name, a memorizer pair.
tree:1u89rd91f16j0r.relation: Tubba's people, powerful and destroyed, as a warning.

tree:0aa52ma1p8nl0c.why: You are an ignorant people: Musa to the Israelites who wanted an idol (7:138), Lut to his people (27:55). Two prophets, same rebuke. Both rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:0aa52ma1p8nl0c.relation: Ignorance in worship and in morals, rebuked in the same words.

tree:06rntbq1wir3tg.why: A common ending about a disbelieving people: Shuayb's grief (7:93) and the queen's background (27:43). Different subjects. Both rows read on into the next ayah.

tree:0nxcflg1ljuvr8.why: The same angels, called unfamiliar people by Lut (15:62) and by Ibrahim (51:25). The rows read on to show each host's reaction.
tree:0nxcflg1ljuvr8.relation: One visit of angels, met with unease by two prophets.

tree:03hbmc600zlcz0.why: A curse on Ad (11:60) and Shuayb's list of punished peoples (11:89) share only the name of Hud's people. Not a phrase or theme in common.

tree:1eppdav1wgg9h5.why: After destroying a people, God raised or let inherit other people (21:11, 44:28). The rows read on to show their end.
tree:1eppdav1wgg9h5.relation: Peoples are replaced: the land passes to others.

tree:1dbu1co1hh0fam.why: A rare phrase, a ruined people: the idolaters described by their gods (25:18) and the Bedouins who stayed behind (48:12). The rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:1dbu1co1hh0fam.relation: Forgetting the reminder and thinking ill of God both ruin a people.

tree:0cdbxi604o7d20.why: In 7:160 his people is the subject asking for water, in 71:1 it is the object of Nuh's mission. Different structures.

tree:0b3a25s1x449w6.why: Ibrahim's people argue with him (6:80) and Pharaoh calls to his people (43:51): narrative glue, nothing shared.

tree:0c6itqd11qkch1.why: The destruction of Pharaoh's works (7:137) and Pharaoh misleading his people (20:79): the conjunction is a different structure each time.

tree:0hh39cy0uq3ryo.why: Earlier peoples stronger and richer were destroyed: said to the hypocrites (9:69) and to Qarun (28:78). Same argument, the last noun differs.
tree:0hh39cy0uq3ryo.relation: Strength and wealth did not save those before.

tree:0jh0d4z1ub5u31.why: The wrongdoers told to taste punishment (10:52) and the God-fearing asked about revelation (16:30): it was said to, a generic frame.

tree:00hx4vu1x92884.why: Mankind was one community: then God sent prophets (2:213), then they differed (10:19). Same opening, two halves of one story.
tree:00hx4vu1x92884.relation: From one community to division, and the prophets sent to judge it.

tree:15yy0ca02tdqn4.why: A people before you asked such questions (5:102) and let no people mock another (49:11): a generic noun and preposition, unrelated.

tree:0nmd6pv1ukfmy7.why: God knows the good you do (4:127) and his Lord saw him (84:15): a common ending structure with different subjects.

tree:1ruea8m0lvxc4k.why: In Maryam, Yahya was God-fearing (19:13), and Paradise is inherited by whoever was God-fearing (19:63). The same ending in one surah, and a link worth pondering. Both rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:1ruea8m0lvxc4k.relation: Yahya is the model of the God-fearing to whom Paradise is given.

tree:1qfz3rv1ql2ra7.why: God is ever accepting of repentance: closing a ruling on two who repent (4:16) and closing an-Nasr (110:3). A memorizer ending, once with Merciful, once alone. The row for 110:3 reads on into a new surah, which the match does not need.
tree:1qfz3rv1ql2ra7.relation: Repentance is accepted from the sinner and asked of the Prophet at his moment of victory.

tree:0s2acv41yu570k.why: Two neighbouring ayat, whoever is an enemy: of Jibril (2:97), and of God, His angels and messengers (2:98). The second widens the first.
tree:0s2acv41yu570k.relation: Enmity to Jibril is enmity to God, and God is an enemy to the deniers.

tree:11i1s600bt7d9w.why: Two closings in an-Nisa, God is pardoning, then Forgiving (4:43) or Able (4:149). The second follows a call to pardon others.
tree:11i1s600bt7d9w.relation: God pardons though He has power; so should the believer.

tree:1ovy3p00ueds86.why: A party who distorted God's word (2:75) and a party of God's servants who prayed (23:109): a generic noun, opposite subjects without a shared point.

tree:1619x191ywjddv.why: A rare clause, if it is hard on you: on the Prophet, the deniers' turning away (6:35), and on Nuh's people, his standing among them (10:71).
tree:1619x191ywjddv.relation: The burden falls on the Prophet, who is told to be patient, and on the deniers, whom Nuh defies.

tree:0sa2xej1izun29.why: Satan was disobedient to the Merciful (19:44) and if the Merciful had a son (43:81): the shared words are a different structure.

tree:00dn9dm0rajbx4.why: Two cups in al-Insan, one mixed with camphor (76:5), one with ginger (76:17). A classic memorizer pair.
tree:00dn9dm0rajbx4.relation: Two drinks of the righteous, cooling and warming.

tree:1pmjpm81fq8age.why: The same argument for God's oneness: had there been gods with Him, they would seek a way to the Throne (17:42) or each would take what he created (23:91).
tree:1pmjpm81fq8age.relation: Several gods would mean rivalry and disorder; the order of creation shows one God.

tree:1ozz1pz0v7pxw3.why: The deniers' challenge if this is the truth (8:32) and this Quran could not be forged (10:37): the shared words are a different structure.

tree:057vrw80nrjl2w.why: The promise of my Lord, said by the people of knowledge who prostrate (17:108) and by Dhul-Qarnayn of the barrier's end (18:98). Neighbouring surahs, close wording.
tree:057vrw80nrjl2w.relation: Believers and a just king alike are certain that God's promise comes.

tree:1pv7fxk1rf7w9e.why: His promise is sure to come: the gardens promised (19:61) and the sky splitting (73:18). Same closing shape, two different promises.
tree:1pv7fxk1rf7w9e.relation: God keeps both His promise of reward and His warning.

tree:1n1asng0s09mue.why: If the next abode is yours alone (2:94) and you have an example in Ibrahim (60:4): only the verb and pronoun meet.

tree:1u0fzmm016amaw.why: The believers' gardens described as theirs: Firdaws as a welcome (18:107), the garden of eternity as reward and destination (25:15).
tree:1u0fzmm016amaw.relation: Paradise as hospitality and as final home.

tree:000rkwz019wn3b.why: The day they see what they were promised it will seem they stayed only an hour (46:35) or an evening or a morning (79:46). Same image of life's shortness.
tree:000rkwz019wn3b.relation: This world seems a moment when the Hour arrives.

tree:1h2t5sy0m7arp2.why: Heirs more than that (4:12) and nations more numerous (40:82): the same words in different senses.

tree:1soaluo0n7huqy.why: Two closings in al-Anbiya about prophets: they were worshippers to Us (21:73), they were humble to Us (21:90).
tree:1soaluo0n7huqy.relation: The prophets praised by their worship and their humility.

tree:1hms2tw0518728.why: A common closing about not being believers, said of Hud's people (7:72) and of hypocrites (9:62). Different subjects; both rows read on into the next ayah.

tree:0gucuxh1dua85x.why: The deniers will wish they had been Muslims (15:2), while those who were Muslims enter Paradise (43:69). Both rows read on into the next ayah, which completes each picture.
tree:0gucuxh1dua85x.relation: Contrast: the wish of the deniers is the state of the believers.

tree:0r0zayd1s91m8b.why: In 41:48 they called on idols, in 68:43 they were called to prostrate: the same verb in active and passive senses. Different structures.

tree:0j4v8mj1ojwt2f.why: A frequent closing about wrongdoing, here after the changed word of the Israelites (7:162) and after the parable of the denier (7:177). A stock ending with different subjects; both rows read on.

tree:0nn4yxj1eninph.why: Fasting prescribed for you (2:183) and God prescribed mercy for Himself (6:12): the same verb, unrelated subjects.

tree:0mvdrim0afdsdc.why: A book from the sky (4:153) and a book before it (43:21): the same noun and preposition, different points.

tree:02cfer3092kwyz.why: Had We prescribed killing themselves (4:66) and the law of retaliation in the Torah (5:45): the same verb, different subjects.

tree:0fueo5a03ncicy.why: The parable misleads many (2:26) and wisdom is much good (2:269): only an adverb and a conjunction.

tree:0yl0zef11p9pxz.why: Two peoples denied the messengers, with the same shape: the people of al-Hijr (15:80) and of the Thicket (26:176).
tree:0yl0zef11p9pxz.relation: The denial of messengers by Thamud and Madyan, told alike.

tree:06u7l7t05t02cz.why: Ad denied: the messengers (26:123), then how was My punishment (54:18). Each surah repeats its own pattern for every people.
tree:06u7l7t05t02cz.relation: Ad's denial told in two surahs with their own refrains.

tree:0tb2tul1x1mmmn.why: They denied him, so the punishment took them: a messenger from among them (16:113) and Shuayb with the day of the canopy (26:189).
tree:0tb2tul1x1mmmn.relation: Denial of a messenger is followed by punishment.

tree:00kvsp51m64pvr.why: So you will be brought out, after the earth revived (30:19) and after a dead land raised by rain (43:11). The resurrection argued from the rain. Both rows read on.
tree:00kvsp51m64pvr.relation: Reviving dead land is the sign of resurrection.

tree:0e3xyzk04jl52i.why: Thus no warner came before you except they said: we follow our fathers (43:23), a sorcerer or madman (51:52). Same pattern, different replies.
tree:0e3xyzk04jl52i.relation: Every people answered their messenger the same way.

tree:1gvfijt1h52gj1.why: After Pharaoh drowned, We made it the inheritance of the Children of Israel (26:59) and of another people (44:28). Same story, different heirs.

tree:10iehle1n9uih6.why: An ending, thus they do: Ibrahim's people about their fathers (26:74) and the queen about kings (27:34). Neighbouring surahs, an easy slip. Both rows read on.

tree:0ap2nhl1uq5ber.why: Removing harm: God removed Ayyub's harm and he became a reminder (21:84), but had He removed the deniers' harm they would persist (23:75).
tree:0ap2nhl1uq5ber.relation: Contrast: the same mercy makes one grateful and the other more defiant.

tree:1176cjl0ox7d2z.why: We disbelieve in what: earlier nations reject what the messengers brought (14:9), and later at the punishment they reject what they had associated (40:84).
tree:1176cjl0ox7d2z.relation: The deniers' words turn around: first they reject the message, at the end they reject their idols, too late.

tree:0q454bi0vt161o.why: Informing the deniers of what they did (41:50) and they disbelieved in the truth (60:1): the shared words are a different structure.

tree:1ui45cz0mks3id.why: Believed then disbelieved (4:137) and I gave respite to the deniers then seized them (13:32): different structures.

tree:0474mcz0hwwdev.why: All of that is evil (17:38) and all of that is enjoyment of this world (43:35): a common phrase, different subjects.

tree:04pf32u0ss61m0.why: All in it, in the Fire: the idols and their worshippers will abide there (21:99), and the arrogant tell their followers all are in it (40:48).
tree:04pf32u0ss61m0.relation: In the Fire, leaders, followers and their gods are all together.

tree:1pq75j80nfluaa.why: Every persistent denier, then an adjective: sinful, whom God does not love (2:276), and stubborn, thrown into Hell (50:24). A memorizer pair.
tree:1pq75j80nfluaa.relation: God's dislike in this world and the sentence in the next fall on the same kind of person.

tree:13lwz6q1gks840.why: In Saba, the deniers mock the idea of rising after being torn to pieces (34:7), and the people of Saba are themselves torn to pieces (34:19).
tree:13lwz6q1gks840.relation: Irony: the people who mock being scattered are scattered in this world.

tree:0hv1rcd0x8bjxl.why: All who are in the heavens and earth come as servants (19:93), all who are on it perish (55:26). Both declare the state of every creature before God.
tree:0hv1rcd0x8bjxl.relation: Every creature is a servant and every creature passes away; only God remains.

tree:1gq4nw50vcx9or.why: Two short openings, no indeed, when: the soul reaches the throat (75:26), the earth is pounded (89:21). The moment of death and the Day of Judgement.
tree:1gq4nw50vcx9or.relation: The end of the person and the end of the world, announced the same way.

tree:1oo3w430ebz07d.why: Two times in al-Muddaththir, no indeed, he/it: the denier was stubborn to Our ayat (74:16), and the Quran is a reminder (74:54).
tree:1oo3w430ebz07d.relation: The stubborn denier and the reminder he rejected.

tree:12yuvxc0v29n4c.why: We gave him Ishaq and Yaqub and made each: prophets (19:49), righteous (21:72). A classic memorizer pair on Ibrahim.
tree:12yuvxc0v29n4c.relation: The reward of Ibrahim's leaving his people: a line of prophets.

tree:07l6kho040cnje.why: No refuge (75:11) and do not obey him (96:19): the shared words are a different structure, unrelated.

tree:1oj64cb0v1wjcl.why: God spoke: among the messengers is one to whom God spoke (2:253), and God spoke to Musa directly (4:164). The second names the one the first hints at.

tree:1m7czd50v12opx.why: The word of punishment came due: on the one the Prophet cannot save (39:19) and on the deniers who admit it at Hell's gates (39:71). Same surah.
tree:1m7czd50v12opx.relation: Once the word of punishment is due, no one can save and the deniers themselves confess.

tree:0vh7eac1dg8ouq.why: All of it belongs to God: the whole matter (3:154) and all religion (8:39). Both answer believers in battle.
tree:0vh7eac1dg8ouq.relation: Command and religion belong wholly to God.

tree:03wkob11kdgytt.why: How long did you stay, asked by the youths of the cave (18:19) and by God to the dead (23:112). Both answer a day or part of a day.
tree:03wkob11kdgytt.relation: Sleep in the cave and death in the grave both feel like a day.

tree:13cm1wg1mu39l0.why: As We sent a messenger: to you from among yourselves (2:151) and to Pharaoh (73:15). Grace and warning in the same words.
tree:13cm1wg1mu39l0.relation: A messenger sent is a favour to the believers and a warning to the deniers.

tree:01j99r81opp87u.why: Two parables in al-Baqara, like one who: kindles a fire (2:17) and shouts at animals (2:171). Both end in deafness and blindness.
tree:01j99r81opp87u.relation: Hypocrites and deniers both pictured as deaf and blind.

tree:03gr671110jaop.why: Like one who is: blind (13:19), abiding in the Fire (47:15). Both are comparisons that are not equal.
tree:03gr671110jaop.relation: The one who knows the truth or is promised Paradise is not like the blind or the damned.

tree:1fkixll1id0wtz.why: We knew him well (21:51) and what we used to associate (40:84): the same verb and pronoun, unrelated.

tree:1qit19o0d2le7i.why: We were in heedlessness (21:97) and we would not be among the people of the Blaze (67:10): different structures, though both are deniers' regrets.

tree:138lha31xwkirh.why: We were sending: messengers to past peoples (28:45) and the Quran on the blessed night (44:5). In both, the next ayah says it is mercy from your Lord, so the run-on rows carry the match.
tree:138lha31xwkirh.relation: Sending messengers is a mercy from God.

tree:1nqif0h0foxlkn.why: We were only engaging in idle talk: the hypocrites' excuse (9:65) and the damned's confession (74:45).
tree:1nqif0h0foxlkn.relation: The excuse in this world becomes the confession in Hell.

tree:02dxmgk0kxaqhy.why: If you are in doubt (10:94) and you were in heedlessness (50:22): a common frame, different subjects.

tree:0qkeatn098akc9.why: Your arrogance: the people of the Heights rebuke the arrogant (7:48), and the deniers are punished for it (46:20). Both rows end on the same reason.
tree:0qkeatn098akc9.relation: Arrogance is the cause named for the deniers' end.

tree:046c0mo02xfng8.why: You were, before: astray before God guided you (2:198), and you were like this before God favoured you (4:94). God reminds the believers of their past.
tree:046c0mo02xfng8.relation: Remembering one's past state teaches gratitude and fairness.

tree:0r96f650qx7qpj.why: The deniers' demand that a treasure be sent down or an angel come with him (11:12, 25:8). Same objection, worded apart.
tree:0r96f650qx7qpj.relation: The deniers measure a prophet by treasure and angels.

tree:0vz4l5t0hnfh25.why: The deniers' plot: God weakens it (8:18), it is only in error (40:25). The plot fails both at Badr and with Pharaoh. The run-on adds 8:19.

tree:16fekn80drxuju.why: Their plot will not harm you at all (3:120), and on the Day it will not avail them at all (52:46).
tree:16fekn80drxuju.relation: The plot neither hurts the believers nor helps the plotters.

tree:1m4qygd1k51z19.why: To see how you act: Musa promises his people succession in the land (7:129), and God makes later generations successors (10:14). Both rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:1m4qygd1k51z19.relation: Being given the land is a test of conduct.

tree:0g8vemm0dfyoes.why: How can you disbelieve: when you were dead and He gave you life (2:28), when His ayat are recited to you and His messenger is among you (3:101).
tree:0g8vemm0dfyoes.relation: Two reasons that make disbelief impossible: life itself and present revelation.

tree:0uxwvc00276eo0.why: I find nothing forbidden in revelation (6:145) and I find nothing to carry you (9:92): the same verb, unrelated.

tree:19aqflr0240tvh.why: Wavering between neither side (4:143) and unable to return to their families (36:50): different structures.

tree:091t9gu1x78mku.why: Two neighbouring rulings about the Prophet's wives: he may not exchange them (33:52), the believers may not marry them after him (33:53).
tree:091t9gu1x78mku.relation: The bond of the Prophet's wives is protected from both sides.

tree:0qopvxy0m9vqp4.why: Do not trust except your own (3:73) and believe or do not (17:107): different senses of the verb.

tree:1lhc09e16d8lr4.why: No change: to God's words (10:64) and to God's creation (30:30), each followed by that is. A memorizer pair.
tree:1lhc09e16d8lr4.relation: God's promise and God's natural order are both unchanging.

tree:0oinfu609b8lqe.why: Do not void your charity with reminders and harm (2:264), do not void your deeds (47:33). Both warn believers about losing good deeds.
tree:0oinfu609b8lqe.relation: Good deeds can be cancelled, by harm or by disobedience.

tree:1ogcoaa1yej1ns.why: Do not turn away as criminals (11:52) and do not take as allies (60:13): the same verb in two meanings.

tree:1a40tww1t4ukg0.why: Do not place me among the wrongdoing people: Harun to Musa (7:150) and the Prophet to God (23:94). Preposition differs.
tree:1a40tww1t4ukg0.relation: Prophets ask not to be counted with the wrongdoers.

tree:05uqlu31jvse69.why: Do not grieve: after Uhud, for you are uppermost (3:139); from the angels to the steadfast, with the good news of Paradise (41:30).
tree:05uqlu31jvse69.relation: Comfort to the believers in defeat and at death.

tree:0hatjx61l7wprc.why: Do not lay a burden on us (2:286) and creatures that do not carry their provision (29:60): the same verb in different senses.

tree:11lct9z0c1925x.why: Ibrahim's question about fear (6:81) and entering the Mosque without fear (48:27): different structures and subjects.

tree:0y2k1pz08l04br.why: Do not fear them, fear Me: at the change of the qibla (2:150) and on the day religion was perfected (5:3). Both end with God completing His favour.
tree:0y2k1pz08l04br.relation: At turning points of the Ummah, God says fear Me and completes His favour.

tree:19gd43t0pdb76t.why: Do not cry for one ruin (25:14) and do not call on anyone with God (72:18): the same verb in different senses.

tree:1escija03azh9g.why: Nuh's prayer to leave no denier (71:26) and Saqar that leaves nothing (74:28): the same verb, unrelated scenes.

tree:1j3viy30nwz9f3.why: Only whispers are heard on the Day (20:108) and no idle talk is heard in Paradise (88:11): the same verb, different scenes and points.

tree:0uythfh1v8p8p7.why: Do not associate: God's command to Ibrahim at the House (22:26) and Luqman's counsel to his son (31:13). The first rule of a prophet and of a wise father.
tree:0uythfh1v8p8p7.relation: Tawhid comes first, in building the House and in raising a child.

tree:0pqb05c16ukrtm.why: Do not transgress: after the command to be upright (11:112), after the gift of good food (20:81). A rare command a memorizer must place.
tree:0pqb05c16ukrtm.relation: Uprightness and blessing both bring the warning not to overstep.

tree:0tiv4jq0er07c4.why: Worship none but God, Nuh's message (11:26), and do not worship Satan, God's covenant with the children of Adam (36:60). The same command from two sides.
tree:0tiv4jq0er07c4.relation: Worshipping God alone means refusing to worship Satan.

tree:0935jf91aj3t25.why: Do not hasten: against the deniers, their days are counted (19:84), and with the Quran before its revelation is complete (20:114). Neighbouring surahs.
tree:0935jf91aj3t25.relation: Patience with the deniers and with revelation.

tree:07f3f7i0js49ki.why: Do not prevent them: from remarrying their former husbands (2:232), and to take back their dowry (4:19). Two rulings that protect women from the same harm.
tree:07f3f7i0js49ki.relation: Men may not block women's choices for their own gain.

tree:0jy98yz0ez5ftj.why: Do not sit with mockers (4:140) and do not lurk on every path (7:86): the same verb in different senses.

tree:1gtte2i0drn5h2.why: Do not stand: at a hypocrite's grave (9:84) and in the mosque of harm (9:108). Same surah, both about hypocrites.
tree:1gtte2i0drn5h2.relation: The Prophet may not honour the hypocrites in death or in their mosque.

tree:1wvjaxv1hemrrv.why: No soul is charged: beyond its capacity (2:233), and you are charged only for yourself (4:84). A memorizer pair.
tree:1wvjaxv1hemrrv.relation: Responsibility is limited to capacity and to one's own self.

tree:1x6vz7e1n6s9co.why: Do not marry: idolatresses (2:221) and your fathers' wives (4:22). Two marriage prohibitions in the same words.
tree:1x6vz7e1n6s9co.relation: Marriage is barred by faith and by kinship.

tree:0f1wd5w0dg0n8q.why: No hostility except against the wrongdoers (2:193) and Musa's terms with his father-in-law (28:28): a rare phrase, different subjects and little to ponder together.

tree:1jhtklv1tkkigx.why: No welcome for them, then no welcome for you: the leaders and the followers curse each other in Hell in neighbouring ayat.
tree:1jhtklv1tkkigx.relation: In Hell the leaders and followers turn on each other.

tree:0icfsfy0q88i86.why: Nor from behind it (41:42) and nor from those who disbelieved (57:15): a negation and a preposition, unrelated.

tree:0b98zqj0ztxl59.why: A rare phrase, no child: in this life parents and child must not harm each other (2:233); on the Day no child avails his father (31:33).
tree:0b98zqj0ztxl59.relation: Duties between parent and child in this life; no help between them on the Day.

tree:0n53b6f0knacht.why: No helper: a stronger town destroyed with none to help it (47:13), and man on the Day with no strength or helper (86:10). The row for 86:10 reads on into an oath that does not belong to the match.
tree:0n53b6f0knacht.relation: Strength fails and no one helps, for towns and for each soul.

tree:13fiu8j0gf2kwz.why: They would not give people a speck (4:53) and those who do not give zakat (41:7): the same verb, different subjects.

tree:0sjeqnl0vmyktp.why: Not permitted: the deniers are not allowed to speak or make amends (16:84), nor to excuse themselves (77:36).
tree:0sjeqnl0vmyktp.relation: On the Day the deniers have no voice and no excuse.

tree:1m9dru11nil3yj.why: Believers taking deniers as allies (3:28) and taking one another as lords (3:64): different constructions and subjects.

tree:0nn7kob0dp0nvz.why: On the Day they will not ask one another: no ties of kinship (23:101), all news lost to them (28:66). Each row reads on into an ayah about the successful, which carries the parallel.
tree:0nn7kob0dp0nvz.relation: On the Day, the bonds and the news fail, and only deeds bring success.

tree:1pp2gsi0ef1xiy.why: Fearing no blame (5:54) and not fearing the hereafter (74:53): the same verb, different subjects.

tree:1bk2uqw0y0b9ii.why: Nothing is hidden from God: in earth or heaven (3:5), and from them on the Day they come forth (40:16).
tree:1bk2uqw0y0b9ii.relation: God's complete knowledge, now and on the Day.

tree:0p944qe0y70kf4.why: Idols that do not create: worshipped though they are themselves created (7:191), compared with the Creator (16:17).
tree:0p944qe0y70kf4.relation: The argument from creation against idols.

tree:16tn5oo01lmrw0.why: His might is not turned back from the criminal people: a warning after mercy (6:147) and the end of the messengers' trial (12:110).
tree:16tn5oo01lmrw0.relation: God's mercy is wide, but His punishment of criminals is certain.

tree:0eof0jy0rps1h2.why: They will keep fighting you (2:217) and they will keep differing (11:118): a common verb, unrelated.

tree:0oz8uln1l0y6un.why: It increases the wrongdoers only in loss: the Quran (17:82), and disbelief itself (35:39).
tree:0oz8uln1l0y6un.relation: What heals the believers only adds to the loss of the wrongdoers.

tree:18in32h19nw7nf.why: God is not shy: to give a parable of a gnat (2:26), of the truth (33:53). A rare attribute in two settings.
tree:18in32h19nw7nf.relation: God does not hold back the truth, small or awkward.

tree:0jdy2qu0i3xwsa.why: They are not equal: those who serve pilgrims and those who strive (9:19), the believer and the sinner (32:18). The row for 32:18 reads on into its explanation.
tree:0jdy2qu0i3xwsa.relation: Faith and striving are not equal to outward service or to sin.

tree:18pmibv0p79kff.why: He does not ask you: the messengers ask no wage (36:21), and God does not ask your wealth (47:36).
tree:18pmibv0p79kff.relation: Guidance is offered free; neither messenger nor God asks a price.

tree:1wm27nd0zpyczz.why: If you call them, they do not hear: idols in 7:198 and 35:14, with different continuations.
tree:1wm27nd0zpyczz.relation: The idols are deaf to their worshippers.

tree:09m2pjd02qwy7v.why: He shares with none: God in His rule (18:26), and the believer in his worship (18:110). Same surah.
tree:09m2pjd02qwy7v.relation: God has no partner in judgement, so the believer gives Him none in worship.

tree:05vq7260hogmcs.why: Believers who do not associate others with God (23:59, 24:55): a common description in different contexts, no particular point together.

tree:0uomoyh07h1173.why: Let no one turn you away: Musa from the Hour (20:16), the Prophet from God's ayat (28:87).
tree:0uomoyh07h1173.relation: Prophets warned against being turned aside by deniers.

tree:1btvqqy0vj8ij8.why: In Taha, my Lord neither errs nor forgets (20:52), and whoever follows My guidance neither errs nor suffers (20:123).
tree:1btvqqy0vj8ij8.relation: God does not err, and following Him protects from error.

tree:1kgxoe91if8dtj.why: He can hardly swallow it (14:17) and he can hardly speak clearly (43:52): a rare construction, but different subjects and points.

tree:0tp62gl0nd2uy5.why: Let there be no unease in your chest (7:2) and let not your plan be obscure (10:71): different structures.

tree:1d6rxza18b1kuw.why: So that there is no blame on believers (33:37) and so that wealth does not circulate among the rich (59:7): a common purpose clause, different rulings.

tree:0kgmmdm00phmtm.why: They will not be like you (47:38) and let them not be like those (57:16): the same verb, different senses.

tree:0wdq0ue1wq7i16.why: Nothing touches them: no fatigue in Paradise (15:48), no evil on the Day (39:61). Both for the God-fearing.
tree:0wdq0ue1wq7i16.relation: The God-fearing are safe from fatigue and from harm.

tree:0yx53tp13q692h.why: They will not speak: when the word falls on them (27:85), on the Day of Separation (77:35). Both rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:0yx53tp13q692h.relation: The deniers fall silent when judgement comes.

tree:04ttkb50qi4vwn.why: Nuh's advice will not benefit you (11:34) and idols that cannot benefit (21:66): the same verb, different subjects.

tree:1jqcyta0igjmc0.why: In at-Tawba, the hypocrites spend only unwillingly (9:54), while the believers' every spending, small or large, is written for them (9:121).
tree:1jqcyta0igjmc0.relation: Contrast: spending refused by God and spending recorded for reward.

tree:03aqd071ld4i53.why: The calf cannot guide them (7:148) and God does not guide those who reject His ayat (16:104): the same verb with different subjects and points.

tree:08berw60vjwyra.why: A son says to his father, O my father: Yusuf telling his dream (12:4), Ibrahim calling his father to faith (19:42).
tree:08berw60vjwyra.relation: Two prophets speak tenderly to their fathers, one with good news and one with a call.

tree:1ktsu2e11ma9ig.why: The reward of the hereafter is better (12:57) or greater (16:41): after Yusuf's rise and after the emigrants' reward in this world.
tree:1ktsu2e11ma9ig.relation: Worldly reward is given, but the hereafter's reward is more.

tree:1om53gw1yqi9tg.why: You stayed: God asks how long they stayed on earth (23:112), and the people of knowledge answer that they stayed until the Day of Resurrection (30:56).
tree:1om53gw1yqi9tg.relation: The deniers misjudge the time they spent; the people of knowledge know it was God's decree.

tree:0x20stp079cznr.why: The youths stayed in their cave (18:25) and the jinn would not have stayed in punishment (34:14): the same verb and preposition, different subjects.

tree:1lyi2ak1tms708.why: God acts on a heart so that its owner may be: one of the warners, the Prophet's heart receiving revelation (26:194), one of the believers, Musa's mother's heart steadied (28:10).
tree:1lyi2ak1tms708.relation: God strengthens the heart for its task, a prophet's and a mother's.

tree:0qrjy4s0wqyjd8.why: The remembrance of God is greater (29:45) and hearts humbled for the remembrance of God (57:16): different constructions.

tree:0mcbgjc0gftawe.why: The wine of Paradise, a delight to drinkers, in 37:46 and 47:15. The row for 37:46 reads on to say it does not intoxicate.
tree:0mcbgjc0gftawe.relation: The drink of Paradise is pure pleasure without harm.

tree:0l6fv9g0vmjag2.why: An honoured mention: Ibrahim asks for it (26:84) and God grants it to him and his sons (19:50).
tree:0l6fv9g0vmjag2.relation: Prayer and its answer in the same words.

tree:1gid5rj1qn8p8h.why: To Sulayman the wind: storming at his command (21:81), with its morning and evening course a month each (34:12).
tree:1gid5rj1qn8p8h.relation: The same gift to Sulayman, described by its force and by its reach.

tree:09571hy0oiuy3g.why: The same scene told twice: Musa sees the fire and tells his family he may bring news or a brand. The rows read on into the call from the fire, also told twice.
tree:09571hy0oiuy3g.relation: Musa's first call, told in two surahs with small differences.

tree:0gih4g50togmof.why: On guidance: you are on straight guidance (22:67), and either we or you are on guidance or in error (34:24).
tree:0gih4g50togmof.relation: The Prophet is assured of his guidance, then invites the deniers to weigh it fairly.

tree:082ia3a08kqdhq.why: The curse of God on the liars: in the mutual curse with the Christians (3:61) and in the husband's fifth oath (24:7).
tree:082ia3a08kqdhq.relation: Calling God's curse on the liar settles a dispute when no other proof exists.

tree:1opzn101tqm3qo.why: God cursed Satan (4:118) and whom God cursed among the People of the Book (5:60): a common verb phrase, different subjects.

tree:0306yz00ef95ii.why: Those who denied Our ayat and the meeting of the hereafter: their deeds void (7:147), and they are brought to punishment (30:16).
tree:0306yz00ef95ii.relation: Denying the hereafter voids deeds and leads to punishment.

tree:000yg7s1hija0o.why: We took a covenant (5:70) and We seized Pharaoh's people (7:130): the same verb in different senses.

tree:1oxf8a00c3g3jo.why: The people of Paradise say the messengers came with the truth (7:43); the angels came to Ibrahim (11:69). Different senses of messengers and different scenes.

tree:0v0p1lo0cmaebg.why: Messengers came to them with clear proofs, then many still transgressed (5:32) or would not believe (7:101).
tree:0v0p1lo0cmaebg.relation: Clear proofs do not change those set on denial.

tree:0e2xzas0cgr0re.why: There has come to you: news of the messengers (6:34), the truth from your Lord (10:94). Both steady the Prophet.
tree:0e2xzas0cgr0re.relation: The Prophet is strengthened by the stories of earlier messengers and by certainty in the truth.

tree:12wyyf715m4ns3.why: He saw him: at another descent (53:13), on the clear horizon (81:23). Both on the Prophet seeing Jibril.
tree:12wyyf715m4ns3.relation: The two sightings of Jibril confirm the revelation.

tree:1voi74k0my8ryg.why: He has pardoned you (3:152), God has pardoned them (3:155): about Uhud, in neighbouring ayat.
tree:1voi74k0my8ryg.relation: After the failure at Uhud, God's pardon is stated twice.

tree:044hufr15gizsb.why: A frequent opening about earlier deniers; al-Hijr (15:80) and those before Quraysh (67:18) share only that. The 15:80 match with 26:176 is the stronger card.

tree:18gdnn80t5yi88.why: You used to wish for death (3:143) and you and your fathers were astray (21:54): unrelated.

tree:01d87aj0qf4ho9.why: We conferred favour: on Musa another time (20:37), on Musa and Harun (37:114).

tree:00yo4fo0thvjhs.why: We know: your chest is tight from what they say (15:97), and they say a man teaches him (16:103). Neighbouring surahs.
tree:00yo4fo0thvjhs.relation: God knows the Prophet's distress and the slander that causes it.

tree:1vwmvfh1di4i3x.why: The matter would have been settled: had an angel been sent (6:8) or had I what you hasten (6:58). Same surah.
tree:1vwmvfh1di4i3x.relation: God's delay is mercy; the deniers' demands would end their time.

tree:1ovrtmz14hsvut.why: Only a stock ending, for a people who remember, after two different subjects. Both rows read on without adding a link.

tree:17djv780x63438.why: What is wrong with you that you are not (15:32) and you will not hunger (20:118): different structures, though both are in the story of Adam.

tree:0uzpq3315e6sz3.why: Nothing is said to you but what was said (41:43) and they cite it to you only to argue (43:58): only an exception structure.

tree:1pgadtq1uc9tb0.why: The angels and Yusuf's temptress, joined only by a pronoun and said.

tree:17j9bet03tvik7.why: Why do you not trust us (12:11) and for me and you, do not kill him (28:9): different constructions.

tree:1elfod60f2gsea.why: For each We made: heirs (4:33) and a law and a way (5:48). Neighbouring surahs.
tree:1elfod60f2gsea.relation: God assigns to each their share and their law.

tree:1hc9rvo1c478fa.why: No one changes God's words: after the help that came to the messengers (6:34) and after the good news to the friends of God (10:64).
tree:1hc9rvo1c478fa.relation: God's promises are sure, for messengers and for His friends.

tree:1ihk0eg058za30.why: Why, when you are told (9:38) and they will swear to you when you return (9:95): different structures.

tree:16eo1aw0dc3hgi.why: Cattle made lawful (22:30) or made for you to ride and eat (40:79). A favour mentioned with different purposes.
tree:16eo1aw0dc3hgi.relation: Cattle as lawful food and as means of travel.

tree:1pen6f90eg2wit.why: Ships made to sail for you: in a list of God's gifts (14:32) and as His mercy at sea (17:66).
tree:1pen6f90eg2wit.relation: Ships at sea as a favour and a sign.

tree:0skpdye0dhfq2u.why: Pharaoh's before I permit you (7:123) and God's I will answer you (40:60): a pronoun and particle only.

tree:08t3mi31gh06av.why: I perfected your religion (5:3) and to you your religion (109:6): different constructions and meanings.

tree:0pijneb1ufj3wh.why: Neighbouring rulings: God gave you no way against those who keep peace (4:90), and clear authority against those who do not (4:91).
tree:0pijneb1ufj3wh.relation: Contrast: peace for the peaceful, fighting for those who break it.

tree:0vhj67v1ia0409.why: Sacrificial camels (22:36) and entering houses (24:27): a pronoun and the common hope clause, nothing else.

tree:0n7ed6601hj7zc.why: Purer for you: letting divorced women remarry (2:232) and giving charity before private counsel with the Prophet (58:12). Same closing words for two rulings.
tree:0n7ed6601hj7zc.relation: God's rulings are described as purifying those who follow them.

tree:0r4fzc40z0cby0.why: A hostile people while he is a believer (4:92) and God forgives you, He is most merciful (12:92): pronouns only.

tree:010qdyv0bgrcxd.why: Ibrahim was upright (3:67) and the companion was in error (50:27): a common contrastive frame.

tree:0ozi87n1i3m8g9.why: I would have been among: the believer in Paradise thanks God he is not among those brought to Hell (37:57), the sinner wishes God had guided him (39:57).
tree:0ozi87n1i3m8g9.relation: Contrast: gratitude for guidance received and regret for guidance refused.

tree:0ciryjx1s2cqrv.why: So that he knows nothing after knowledge (16:70) and so that there is no blame (33:37): a purpose particle only.

tree:0rtxica0bauynu.why: The truth came to them, but most of them hate the truth (23:70, 43:78). The rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:0rtxica0bauynu.relation: Denial comes from hating the truth, not from lack of proof.

tree:0n475eg0ifu7qs.why: The arrogant speak to the weak: in Thamud about Salih (7:75), and on the Day, disowning them (34:32).
tree:0n475eg0ifu7qs.relation: The arrogant mock the weak who believe, and later blame the weak who followed them.

tree:0003t2j00y7b29.why: Ask the People of the Book (3:20) and the hypocrites asking the people of knowledge (47:16): a generic phrase, different subjects.

tree:1i962380unkddw.why: Neighbouring ayat on repentance: accepted from those who do evil in ignorance and repent soon (4:17), not from those who wait until death (4:18).
tree:1i962380unkddw.relation: Contrast: when repentance is accepted and when it is too late.

tree:0trdeot08ncvbb.why: A right in their wealth for the beggar and the deprived (51:19, 70:25). The rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:0trdeot08ncvbb.relation: The same description of the believers' giving.

tree:12a3dck1nf5s7c.why: Asking forgiveness for oneself and for the believing men and women: the Prophet (47:19) and Nuh (71:28).
tree:12a3dck1nf5s7c.relation: Prophets include all believers in their prayer for forgiveness.

tree:0lp0au30acl6m1.why: No argument against God (4:165) and forgiveness despite wrongdoing (13:6): different structures.

tree:05umzrj00w7tef.why: Every kind of parable (18:54) and whatever mercy God opens (35:2): a preposition only.

tree:1fe1d7e0744iuu.why: Make it clear to people (3:187) and do not turn your cheek to people (31:18): unrelated.

tree:0osars80poqyf0.why: The command belongs to God: all of it (13:31), before and after (30:4).
tree:0osars80poqyf0.relation: Every outcome, in signs and in victories, is God's.

tree:1bstkf8193tuy6.why: Honour belongs to God: all of it (35:10), and to His messenger and the believers, against the hypocrites' boast (63:8).
tree:1bstkf8193tuy6.relation: True honour is God's, and He gives it to those who obey Him.

tree:02zh4un020je11.why: Those who answered God and the Messenger after Uhud (3:172) and the spoils belong to God and the Messenger (8:1): a common pairing in different roles.

tree:1juod2g1djqhis.why: Sincere to God and His messenger (9:91) and obedient to God and His messenger (33:31): a common pairing, different subjects.

tree:16r6fbt0qzkt5d.why: Answer God and the Messenger (8:24) and the spoils are for God and the Messenger (59:7): different structures.

tree:1056p760p06r6o.why: Love of God (2:165) and witnesses for God even against yourselves (4:135): a preposition and a conditional.

tree:1pc6mhj1ci6jir.why: I submit to God and those who follow me (3:20) and be grateful to God, whoever is grateful (31:12): different structures.

tree:0w8bdsn05c1qzf.why: Parents and near relatives first: in the bequest (2:180) and in spending (2:215). Same surah.
tree:0w8bdsn05c1qzf.relation: Family comes first in giving, in life and at death.

tree:0pk9x561fwei5g.why: If you do not believe me (44:21) and you have not believed (49:14): the same verb, unrelated.

tree:120oud41pc9glg.why: Why do you argue: about Ibrahim (3:65), about what you know nothing of (3:66). Neighbouring ayat.
tree:120oud41pc9glg.relation: The People of the Book argue beyond their knowledge.

tree:08nsx9j1ttwjs7.why: We did not make for: a people with no shelter from the sun (18:90), and no one named Yahya before (19:7). Neighbouring surahs, a rare structure.
tree:08nsx9j1ttwjs7.relation: Two firsts, a people without cover and a child with a new name.

tree:1yqfnak0q4bjd4.why: Two consecutive lines of the same confession in Hell (74:43, 74:44). They are read together anyway; the card adds nothing.

tree:0org7dl0nyiv07.why: Talut was not given wealth (2:247) and what was not given to anyone (5:20): the same verb in different senses.

tree:1994e2z0aiuu9h.why: Same surah: those who accuse chaste women and do not bring four witnesses are flogged (24:4), and are liars before God (24:13).
tree:1994e2z0aiuu9h.relation: Accusation without witnesses is punished in law and is a lie before God.

tree:07rrtot0gjba7r.why: One who did not believe in his Lord's ayat (20:127) and in God and His messenger (48:13): a common phrase, different contexts.

tree:1252bvl13jtgz1.why: They found no escape: the criminals from the Fire (18:53), and Nuh's people no helpers (71:25).
tree:1252bvl13jtgz1.relation: No escape and no helper from God's punishment.

tree:0brhzr30bsmqt5.why: No crookedness in the Book (18:1) and one God gives no light (24:40): the same verb, different subjects.

tree:1n502oh0yw1jnz.why: Believers who do not leave without permission (24:62) and hypocrites who think the confederates have not left (33:20): unrelated.

tree:1h0rbxm05jae2i.why: God did not will to purify their hearts (5:41) and who wants only this world (53:29): different subjects.

tree:0v1tchw1n8jy18.why: Those who did not fight you: no way against them (4:90), and you may be kind and just to them (60:8).
tree:0v1tchw1n8jy18.relation: Peace and kindness to those who do not fight the believers.

tree:1d7y7so12pekzk.why: They could not escape (11:20) and what they did not expect (39:47): the same verb, unrelated.

tree:0aju9j60el9p12.why: They did not attain: the hypocrites' plot (9:74), the confederates' gain (33:25). Both enemies whose schemes failed.
tree:0aju9j60el9p12.relation: The schemes of hypocrites and of armies both fail.

tree:1g1pmhk1vyxtia.why: When they threw: the magicians enchant the people (7:116), and Musa says God will undo their magic (10:81).
tree:1g1pmhk1vyxtia.relation: The same moment told from two sides: the magic and Musa's answer.

tree:15r6mgz1iln6cn.why: When Our signs came to them: Pharaoh's people called them magic (27:13), and earlier nations were content with their own knowledge (40:83).
tree:15r6mgz1iln6cn.relation: Clear signs are met with scorn.

tree:0t7zxkf06fnzan.why: When they saw it: Ad thought the cloud was rain (46:24), the deniers see the punishment near (67:27).
tree:0t7zxkf06fnzan.relation: The punishment, once seen, is not what they expected.

tree:12ozmol003jbsd.why: We destroyed them when they did wrong: past generations (10:13) and those towns with a set time (18:59).
tree:12ozmol003jbsd.relation: Wrongdoing is the cause of destruction, on a fixed appointment.

tree:1bmajw60t7ulxe.why: He who revives the dead earth will revive the dead, and He has power over all things (30:50, 41:39).
tree:1bmajw60t7ulxe.relation: The rain on dead land is the proof of resurrection.

tree:0k5ld5m0045uvs.why: The arrogant to the believers of Thamud (7:75) and God's reward for whoever believes (28:80): a common phrase, different subjects.

tree:0som9821xxbztc.why: No sin for whoever is God-fearing in the days of Mina (2:203) and the hereafter is better for the God-fearing (4:77): a stock phrase, different rulings.

tree:177f5fr1f0qb7h.why: He is among the liars: the wife's oath in the mutual cursing (24:8), and Madyan's accusation of Shuayb (26:186). Both rows read on into an ayah ending if he is among the truthful, a memorizer pattern.

tree:1y8v4u10fmwjbb.why: Captives in your hands (8:70) and angels asking forgiveness for those on earth (42:5): a preposition only.

tree:0o5ri420nzpkk0.why: For whoever fears: the Quran is a reminder (20:3), Pharaoh's end is a lesson (79:26). Both rows read on into an ayah about the heavens.
tree:0o5ri420nzpkk0.relation: Revelation and history benefit only those who fear God.

tree:0iq4iqc0jh0ip2.why: It will not be accepted: another religion than Islam (3:85), a ransom of the earth's fill of gold (3:91). Same surah.
tree:0iq4iqc0jh0ip2.relation: Nothing is accepted from one who dies outside submission.

tree:1qgqchx0m5t3ol.why: Flight will not save you from death (33:16) and sharing punishment will not help (43:39): the same verb, different subjects.

tree:08evcdt0z1z6nr.why: We have no knowledge (5:109) and forgive us (66:8): a pronoun and the start of an ending formula.

tree:13x5n080i0oz5c.why: The magicians' hope for forgiveness (26:51) and Ibrahim's people's prayer (60:5): a pronoun and our Lord, different structures.

tree:05ndp4211ndhd0.why: Musa's prayer for good (7:156) and Lut's people's reply (11:79): unrelated.

tree:0vx7xpo1kqe7xi.why: Followers cursing their leaders (38:61) and the prayer for riding (43:13): unrelated.

tree:15hgh7a1voxibq.why: We shall make them taste: a nearer punishment so they may return (32:21), a harsh punishment for deniers (41:50).
tree:15hgh7a1voxibq.relation: Punishment in this world as a call to return, and in the next as a sentence.

tree:1qxz7e91x47deh.why: To test them by it: worldly splendour (20:131) and abundant water (72:17).

tree:1y8wfgt0tnvs73.why: Listen to it, the parable of the fly (22:73) and He measures provision for him (29:62): a pronoun and a particle.

tree:0zrofiz050asbz.why: Setting up rivals to God: the weak blame their leaders for ordering it (34:33), the Prophet asks how they can do it to the Creator (41:9).
tree:0zrofiz050asbz.relation: Rivals to God are urged by leaders and rejected by reason.

tree:0m0eix317w6vk9.why: Hell is his: for whoever wanted only this world (17:18), for whoever comes as a criminal (20:74).
tree:0m0eix317w6vk9.relation: Two descriptions of the one whose end is Hell.

tree:0hxtcsf1qbqsiv.why: To Him belongs the true call (13:14), and the idol has no call in this world or the next (40:43).
tree:0hxtcsf1qbqsiv.relation: Contrast: calling on God is answered, calling on idols is empty.

tree:1ckogze12fn8lq.why: God tells Ibrahim to submit (2:131) and God answered Yusuf (12:34): a common phrase in different scenes.

tree:178um911dx8yuv.why: Speak to him gently (20:44) and one whose word He approves (20:109): the same noun, unrelated; the run-on adds nothing.

tree:1iz9qz4118lyxy.why: A light given by God: to the one He revived to walk among people (6:122), and whoever God gives no light has none (24:40).
tree:1iz9qz4118lyxy.relation: Light is God's gift; without it there is only darkness.

tree:1106svr09v6fu3.why: No turning back of God's decree (13:11) and whatever you spend (34:39): a pronoun and a particle.

tree:0c1dv4b0vh6fy9.why: In al-Araf, people with ears that do not hear (7:179) and idols without ears that hear (7:195).
tree:0c1dv4b0vh6fy9.relation: The deniers' unused senses and the idols' missing senses.

tree:1xb3csm0hh59u2.why: The Israelites ask for a god like the idolaters' gods (7:138), and the deniers' gods cannot protect them (21:43). Different points, little slip risk.

tree:1b9e5vv0cx9q1n.why: For them is good news: God's friends in this life and the next (10:64), those who turn from false gods (39:17).
tree:1b9e5vv0cx9q1n.relation: The good news is for those who avoid false worship and fear God.

tree:0kog1kj1kjza3n.why: After the truth became clear to them (2:109) and if the right is theirs (24:49): different senses of the noun.

tree:15wzzys094y04m.why: They have no choice: God creates and chooses (28:68), and believers cannot choose against God's decree (33:36).
tree:15wzzys094y04m.relation: The choice is God's, in creation and in command.

tree:173b1bp1ln7urv.why: To make clear to them what they differ about: on the Day (16:39) and through the Book (16:64). Same surah.
tree:173b1bp1ln7urv.relation: Differences are made clear by the Book now and by the Day later.

tree:0n5s5lu1bc8nqq.why: Punishment doubled (11:20) and punishment hastened (18:58): different verbs and points.

tree:18t71va17ycqoa.why: God said to them (2:243) and ask God's forgiveness for them (24:62): an accidental adjacency.

tree:1s6ofzh0i73pvz.why: Paradise as reward and destination (25:15) and a double reward (34:37): a generic reward phrase in different constructions.

tree:1yp1fz71fz9847.why: Setting orphans right is good (2:220) and respite is not good for the deniers (3:178): unrelated.

tree:1j1utoh0iqqgo1.why: Or do they have partners: who legislated religion (42:21), let them bring them (68:41).
tree:1j1utoh0iqqgo1.relation: Challenging the idolaters' partners, as lawgivers and as witnesses.

tree:1wk3wvh0gen36x.why: Hearts: they have hearts they do not understand with (7:179), if only they had hearts to reason with (22:46).
tree:1wk3wvh0gen36x.relation: The real blindness is of the heart.

tree:0189tlj1c4pp85.why: As if they stayed an hour (46:35) and servants like hidden pearls (52:24): accidental adjacency.

tree:015i0rr0j6otqz.why: No oaths for them, so that they may stop (9:12) and the biggest idol left, so they may return to it (21:58): accidental.

tree:1g7ezyy1k790vy.why: Woe to them for what they wrote (2:79) and cattle made for them (36:71): unrelated.

tree:15jmzoh0fap6yn.why: A share of what they earned (2:202) and a share of the kingdom (4:53): the same noun, unrelated.

tree:11nb3t3091di2l.why: Good for them, and if (9:74) and the Fire their home, and if (41:24): particle glue.

tree:10tmruh0e3qtn9.why: Two neighbouring rulings on divorce before consummation: when no dower was fixed (2:236) and when one was (2:237). The shared phrase is the hinge between them.
tree:10tmruh0e3qtn9.relation: Divorce before consummation, with and without a fixed dower.

tree:0ed2prt1kczs7f.why: Patience is better for the patient (16:126) and God is the best provider (22:58): a common emphatic phrase, different subjects.

tree:0zq7gn40zke3d4.why: A rare clause, even if it pleases you: the abundance of the bad (5:100), the beauty of women (33:52).
tree:0zq7gn40zke3d4.relation: What pleases the eye is not the measure of what is lawful or good.

tree:05mr16q0d0so5q.why: Had We sent an angel (6:8) and had We sent this Quran on a mountain (59:21): a common conditional with different subjects and points.

tree:0rk7fqj052al2n.why: A great oath, if you knew (56:76) and if you knew with certainty (102:5): a short common phrase, different contexts.

tree:1cgkv9u090zdzi.why: They wish you would disbelieve: the hypocrites (4:89) and the enemies to whom some showed friendship (60:2). Both warn against taking them as allies. The row for 60:2 reads on into 60:3.
tree:1cgkv9u090zdzi.relation: The enemy's wish for the believers' disbelief is the reason not to befriend them.

tree:12laat71ctleh1.why: Had We made it: an angel, it would still look like a man (6:9); a foreign Quran, they would have objected (41:44).
tree:12laat71ctleh1.relation: Whatever form revelation took, the deniers would find an excuse.

tree:1bdsajf1hwi615.why: Musa's plea, had You willed (7:155), and his remark to al-Khidr, had you wished (18:77): unrelated.

tree:1n3jsyq1eb29sa.why: Even if we were truthful (12:17) and had we listened (67:10): a common conditional, unrelated.

tree:1jgxvbj1d1zwbv.why: Had you been harsh (3:159) and had I known the unseen (7:188): a common conditional, different points.

tree:0mzfiqm1plw4oc.why: My Lord granted me ... and made me among: Musa, made one of the messengers (26:21), and the man of Ya-Sin, made one of the honoured (36:27). Same structure.
tree:0mzfiqm1plw4oc.relation: Both thank God for His gift and for the rank He gave them.

tree:0pxr0v70yxu5ej.why: Be grateful to Me and do not deny (2:152) and give me leave and do not tempt me (9:49): a pronoun and a negation.

tree:0rl9cn90qwtvi7.why: A messenger in his people's language (14:4) and the Day that makes differences clear (16:39): a common purpose phrase, different subjects.

tree:1lhnrft1n33sgb.why: Let those who rely, rely on Him: Yaqub sending his sons (12:67) and the messengers facing threats (14:12). Both rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:1lhnrft1n33sgb.relation: Taking means, then relying on God, as Yaqub and the messengers did.

tree:0vliapi0ol6e20.why: That God may repay every soul (14:51) and the truthful (33:24): a common purpose phrase, different contexts.

tree:0ep1hhn0s2q851.why: Righteousness is not: facing east or west (2:177), entering houses from the back (2:189). Same surah, a memorizer pair.
tree:0ep1hhn0s2q851.relation: True righteousness is faith and God-fearing, not outward form.

tree:0oqwige1k79bbk.why: He has nothing to do with God (3:28) and he is not of your family (11:46): different structures.

tree:1n33bi8170j1u0.why: Musa on Pharaoh's wealth (10:88) and idolaters setting up rivals (14:30) share a purpose clause about leading astray; the subjects differ.

tree:0sugw7j0etn9e1.why: So that what they hide is known (24:31) and your Lord knows what their breasts conceal (27:74): different structures.

tree:05seqk30j4sj1n.why: Yusuf will be humbled (12:32) and the misleaders trampled (41:29): a rare dual form, but different subjects and points.

tree:0bz5q610aji537.why: Let them be behind you in prayer (4:102) and that they be among the people of the Blaze (35:6): unrelated.

tree:0r54ifw0jqg6fu.why: Let man look: at his food (80:24), at what he was created from (86:5).
tree:0r54ifw0jqg6fu.relation: Reflection on food and on one's origin leads to God.

tree:07twx3f017cnsh.why: What you give in nursing pay (2:233) and what you give in usury or zakat (30:39): the same verb, different subjects.

tree:1q0ao9s1hn9aci.why: Neighbouring ayat: Quraysh were given no scriptures (34:44), while those before were given far more and still denied (34:45).
tree:1q0ao9s1hn9aci.relation: Quraysh have less excuse and less strength than those destroyed before.

tree:0aa2af7150fzlt.why: None believed except a few: with Musa, some youths of his people (10:83); with Nuh, a few (11:40).

tree:1sthucg1xtdho0.why: God has not taken a son (23:91), nor a wife or son (72:3), the second from the jinn.
tree:1sthucg1xtdho0.relation: Men's revelation and the jinn's testimony deny God a son.

tree:0c77f7l1649txb.why: Those given the Book differed only after clear knowledge came, out of rivalry (2:213, 3:19).
tree:0c77f7l1649txb.relation: Division among the people of scripture comes from envy, not ignorance.

tree:03s37581rwwx6c.why: As much as you can: prepare strength (8:60), fear God (64:16). Effort is measured by ability.
tree:03s37581rwwx6c.relation: God asks for full effort within one's capacity, in war and in piety.

tree:15evxs31pa1yzr.why: A rare verb, they did not yield: the companions of the prophets did not give in to the enemy (3:146), the deniers did not humble themselves to God (23:76).
tree:15evxs31pa1yzr.relation: Contrast: not submitting to enemies is praised, not submitting to God is condemned.

tree:1s5wr0v1rnjvcp.why: Whatever good befalls you (4:79) and be patient with what befalls you (31:17): a common verb, different points.

tree:1fpwqnq0t225fu.why: Two consecutive ayat of one opening; because the rows read on, 69:3 appears in both rows. Nothing to compare: they are read together anyway.

tree:05j2r5a1citqtm.why: Two consecutive ayat of one opening; because the rows read on, 101:3 appears in both rows. Nothing to compare.

tree:1fn8eno148q962.why: Pharaoh's command was not right (11:97) and the matter of the Hour (16:77): the same noun, unrelated.

tree:0ayfs4r08e9nsb.why: What of the women (12:50) and what of the former generations (20:51): a common question, unrelated.

tree:1yqcvco1xt56a0.why: What the devils recited (2:102) and what you recite of the Quran (10:61): the same verb, opposite subjects without a point.

tree:1bb8hqn18fx39h.why: What breasts hide: the enemies' hatred is greater than what shows (3:118), and God knows what breasts hide (40:19).
tree:1bb8hqn18fx39h.relation: Hidden hatred is known to God.

tree:0oti5n20s0avcy.why: You forget what you associate (6:41) and I do not fear what you associate (6:80): a common phrase, different points.

tree:1t8adoq0qk43xu.why: A common ending about what you do; 37:96 is about God creating your deeds. Different points; rows read on.

tree:193jkad07ess57.why: After you came to us (7:129) and you brought us no proof (11:53): different structures.

tree:05fk9to0e9692e.why: The purpose of creation: the believers say You did not create this in vain (3:191), and God says He created jinn and men only to worship Him (51:56).
tree:05fk9to0e9692e.relation: Creation has a purpose, and worship is that purpose.

tree:1w7t0wq07lh8io.why: A threat in command form: worship what you will besides Him (39:15), do what you will (41:40).
tree:1w7t0wq07lh8io.relation: God leaves the deniers to their choice as a warning, not a permission.

tree:0dx15cx1ag1ai5.why: Yusuf's brothers testify only to what they know (12:81) and the plotters plan to deny witnessing (27:49): the same verb, different stories.

tree:0jzv7941ua0wbi.why: Deeds come to nothing (11:16) and the staff swallows what they made (20:69): the same verb, unrelated.

tree:0g6va6w0xvpuvm.why: After they were wronged: the emigrants for God's sake (16:41), and the believing poets who defended themselves (26:227).
tree:0g6va6w0xvpuvm.relation: The wronged believers who answer injustice rightly are promised good.

tree:0611v3a1g6zygq.why: It is not your concern: the account of the poor believers you might push away (6:52), and whether the proud man purifies himself (80:7). Both teach the Prophet whom to attend to.
tree:0611v3a1g6zygq.relation: Do not turn from the sincere poor for the sake of the proud rich.

tree:0dykatw1nqetny.why: A rare verb, your hardship: the enemies within wish it on you (3:118), the Prophet is grieved by it (9:128).
tree:0dykatw1nqetny.relation: Contrast: the enemy wants your distress, the Prophet feels it as his own.

tree:13vqrzq134i0ea.why: Same surah, the same verb of neglect: the deniers regret what they neglected (6:31), and God neglected nothing in the Book (6:38).

tree:0s71npq1xp8iuq.why: What you did, in ignorance: Yusuf asks his brothers about what they did when ignorant (12:89), and believers are warned against acting in ignorance and regretting what they did (49:6).
tree:0s71npq1xp8iuq.relation: Acting in ignorance leads to deeds one must later face.

tree:1nloz4y0by3q9q.why: We will record what they said (3:181) and they swear they did not say it (9:74): the same words in different structures.

tree:01hgjzc0yi386m.why: Same surah: the hypocrites claim their brothers would not have died or been killed had they stayed (3:156, 3:168). God answers both times.
tree:01hgjzc0yi386m.relation: The hypocrites' claim that staying home saves from death.

tree:020q0dx08rmukj.why: Your mother was not unchaste (19:28) and what she used to worship (27:43): different structures.

tree:106bho41ljufwk.why: Same surah: the plot of the deniers is only in error (40:25), the plot of Pharaoh only in ruin (40:37).

tree:1uflopg0w2uiga.why: The criminals swear they stayed only an hour (30:55) and the jinn would not have stayed in punishment (34:14): different structures.

tree:0brtnqa0fgtata.why: Each of us has a known place (37:164) and none of us is a witness (41:47): unrelated.
