tree:100mkqj0r7tg51.why: We do not see your intercessors (6:94) and we see you only as a man (11:27): the same verb, unrelated.

tree:1c9g24g0xo375s.why: They resented nothing except: that God enriched them (9:74), that they believed in God (85:8).
tree:1c9g24g0xo375s.relation: The enemies' grudge is against the very favour of faith and blessing.

tree:1jfhou00u8h99e.why: What are these statues (21:52) and this life is nothing but play (29:64): different structures.

tree:0g9opta0pzd0xi.why: What He promised: the people of Paradise ask if the Fire's people found it true (7:44), and the risen say this is what the Merciful promised (36:52).
tree:0g9opta0pzd0xi.relation: On the Day, everyone admits God's promise came true.

tree:1q16cpz0zc0zht.why: Same surah: most of them follow only conjecture (10:36), those who call on partners follow only conjecture (10:66).

tree:08mfys609l8tn8.why: A lifetime in which one could reflect (35:37) and only those who turn reflect (40:13): different senses of the particle.

tree:1egzior1hrvo1l.why: Nothing is hidden from God (14:38) and He knows what is hidden (87:7): the same idea in different structures; the run-on adds nothing.

tree:091xmoy17xtnfs.why: They give themselves what they desire (16:57) and they are kept from what they desire (34:54): different points; the run-on adds nothing.

tree:1gsf7nk002r4ru.why: None knows but God: the interpretation of the ambiguous ayat (3:7) and the number of your Lord's soldiers (74:31). Both name the hearts with deviation or disease and the trial for them.
tree:1gsf7nk002r4ru.relation: What only God knows becomes a trial for sick hearts and firmness for the believers.

tree:10qpdj11h3bsbt.why: What would God do with your punishment (4:147) and I do not know what will be done with me (46:9): different structures.

tree:10miq4o07batcm.why: God witnesses what they do (10:46) and they witness what they do to believers (85:7): a common phrase, different subjects.

tree:11yw04t1kmoqwd.why: Two consecutive ayat about the same denier (19:79, 19:80): read together anyway, nothing to compare.

tree:03hi35t0swf6sp.why: What did he say: the angels ask what their Lord said and answer the truth (34:23), the hypocrites ask what the Prophet just said with contempt (47:16).
tree:03hi35t0swf6sp.relation: Contrast: awe at God's word and mockery of the Prophet's word.

tree:112as5a0ot6rmo.why: What is with this: the criminals about the book of deeds (18:49), the deniers about the messenger who eats (25:7). A rare phrase.
tree:112as5a0ot6rmo.relation: The deniers question the messenger now and the record later.

tree:1iqvsi31wvj3b5.why: Wealth and sons: the deniers think it is God's favour (23:55), and the denier rejects the ayat because he has them (68:14). Both rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:1iqvsi31wvj3b5.relation: Wealth and sons deceive the deniers.

tree:1aeu5gk18flvk4.why: Wealth and children: the believer has less than his proud friend (18:39), the denier boasts he will be given them (19:77). Both rows read on.
tree:1aeu5gk18flvk4.relation: Boasting of wealth and children, answered with God's power.

tree:17cgwmr1gzrw5l.why: A rare question, why do I not: Sulayman missing the hoopoe (27:20), the man of Ya-Sin explaining his faith (36:22).
tree:17cgwmr1gzrw5l.relation: Two questions, one of care and one of conviction.

tree:052wrip1px75ir.why: A brief enjoyment, then Hell (3:197) or painful punishment (16:117).
tree:052wrip1px75ir.relation: The deniers' pleasure is short and the end lasting.

tree:05qlbga0eofotg.why: Same surah: those without knowledge said the like of their words (2:113), those before said the like (2:118).
tree:05qlbga0eofotg.relation: Denial repeats itself; their hearts are alike.

tree:0sp6dbs1hxqyjy.why: Like this raven (5:31) and we could say the like of this (8:31): unrelated.

tree:159hu0v1kr46dd.why: A parable of two men: one dumb and one just (16:76), one with two gardens and one believer (18:32).
tree:159hu0v1kr46dd.relation: Two parables comparing two men, on uselessness and on pride.

tree:0l0o88p0q2l2gz.why: An example from those before (24:34) and a parable from yourselves (30:28): the same noun and preposition, unrelated.

tree:0oqjjet1aasbbf.why: Only a man like us: Nuh's people (11:27) and the town's people to the messengers (36:15).
tree:0oqjjet1aasbbf.relation: The same objection to every messenger: he is only human.

tree:0hlr5g91o65fib.why: His likeness is like: a smooth rock washed bare, for charity spoiled by show (2:264); a panting dog, for the scholar who followed desire (7:176).
tree:0hlr5g91o65fib.relation: Two parables of good things lost: charity voided and knowledge abandoned.

tree:0g4itzz0gm3gvj.why: Of varied colours: the honey from the bee (16:69), and people, animals and cattle (35:28).
tree:0g4itzz0gm3gvj.relation: Variety of colours as a sign that leads to reflection and to awe of God.

tree:19crbed0jnb2xb.why: Of varied colours, accusative: what God spread on earth (16:13), crops grown by rain (39:21).
tree:19crbed0jnb2xb.relation: Colours in creation as signs for those who remember.

tree:0hn7lsl01eq3h9.why: Twice, then: the hypocrites are punished twice before the great punishment (9:101), and tried once or twice a year but do not repent (9:126). Same surah, same subject.
tree:0hn7lsl01eq3h9.relation: The hypocrites are tried repeatedly and still do not turn back.

tree:07fyg8c1o2upcy.why: He let the two seas flow: one sweet, one salt, with a barrier (25:53), meeting each other (55:19).
tree:07fyg8c1o2upcy.relation: The two seas meet without mixing, a sign of God's measure.

tree:0ryhytw1oasuv0.why: Maryam's guardianship (3:44) and the Messiah son of Maryam taken as lord (9:31): her name and a conjunction, unrelated.

tree:09bt31m17dtqby.why: Same surah: Hell is an evil abode and station (25:66), the Garden a fine one (25:76). The rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:09bt31m17dtqby.relation: Contrast: the same words describe the worst and the best dwelling.

tree:15hq0uv0rcwevd.why: You will see the criminals or wrongdoers fearful of what is written or what they earned (18:49, 42:22).
tree:15hq0uv0rcwevd.relation: On the Day the wrongdoers fear their own deeds.

tree:1v7pwto1k973la.why: Bow with those who bow: to the Children of Israel (2:43) and to Maryam (3:43). Both rows read on.
tree:1v7pwto1k973la.relation: Congregational worship commanded to a people and to Maryam.

tree:1764nbg1bqctq8.why: Two consecutive ayat of the same scene with Iblis; because the rows read on, 15:32 appears in both rows. Nothing to compare.

tree:1ij0vwv0o1geqz.why: With those who sit at home: said of the hypocrites by God's decree (9:46) and in their own request (9:86). Same surah, both rows read on.
tree:1ij0vwv0o1geqz.relation: The hypocrites ask to stay behind, and God lets them.

tree:13aznnq0kd442k.why: The repentant are with the believers (4:146) and God is with the believers (8:19): a stock phrase, different points.

tree:0y6slcv0qz97s3.why: Numbered days, then whoever: the fast with its exemptions (2:184), the days of Mina with their choice (2:203). Same surah.
tree:0y6slcv0qz97s3.relation: Two acts of worship on counted days, each with ease built in.

tree:1wxb3c40evrp10.why: Confirming what is with you (2:41) and we will go out with you (59:11): unrelated.

tree:0b41wxe0jgigko.why: He sent down the Book with them: to judge between people (2:213), with the balance so people uphold justice (57:25).
tree:0b41wxe0jgigko.relation: The Book is sent with the messengers to settle disputes and establish justice.

tree:001qzwy1slwhj6.why: Pharaoh's people left treasures or crops and a noble station (26:58, 44:26). Both rows read on into what followed.
tree:001qzwy1slwhj6.relation: The same loss of Pharaoh's people, told in two surahs.

tree:1j73rs51cesn8p.why: They plotted a plot: the plotters against Salih, met by God's plan (27:50), and Nuh's people, a great plot (71:22).
tree:1j73rs51cesn8p.relation: The deniers' plotting, and God's answer.

tree:1gcpuea0cnn15o.why: They will meet their Lord: the humble believers (2:46), and the poor believers Nuh refuses to drive away (11:29).
tree:1gcpuea0cnn15o.relation: Those certain of meeting their Lord are the ones a prophet keeps close.

tree:06pzktz0pwd62d.why: The religion of Ibrahim, in two ayat of al-Baqara: no one turns from it but a fool (2:130), and it is the answer to Jews and Christians (2:135).
tree:06pzktz0pwd62d.relation: Ibrahim's way as the true way, defended twice.

tree:1o1hp231pk2eg3.why: Yusuf's plan for the harvest (12:47) and the deniers' complaint that the messenger eats as they do (23:33): unrelated; the run-on adds nothing.

tree:1rnlwwu0ufchbm.why: Ibrahim disowns what his people worship (43:26), and the believers are told to follow his example in the same disavowal (60:4). The row for 43:26 reads on into the exception of his Creator.
tree:1rnlwwu0ufchbm.relation: Ibrahim's disavowal of idols as an example for the believers.

tree:0ixbupn125sx15.why: Of what He creates: had God wanted a son He would choose (39:4), and would He take daughters (43:16).
tree:0ixbupn125sx15.relation: Refuting the claim that God has children.

tree:0csum1x159xsx1.why: You are humans of His creation (5:18) and revelation from the Creator (20:4): different structures.

tree:1519tq30oy3tq9.why: A community among those We created (7:181) and honoured above many We created (17:70): a common phrase, different points.

tree:0gx33zm1ykdibe.relation: Prophets reproach their people's folly and their harm.

tree:0r9xpbl0vwzkp3.why: Establish prayer, then spend (14:31) or give zakat (98:5).
tree:0r9xpbl0vwzkp3.relation: Prayer and giving as the core of the religion.

tree:0tzbjlc1q9t0nq.why: Disbelieving in what God revealed out of envy (2:90) and did they not disbelieve in what Musa was given (28:48): different points.

tree:0y0yk1s10j1seg.why: Lest people become one community (43:33) and the day people are like moths (101:4): unrelated.

tree:11e5hac03lgc6i.why: An-Nisa ending pair: who will be a guardian over them (4:109), he will be a witness over them (4:159).
tree:11e5hac03lgc6i.relation: No advocate for traitors, and Isa as witness on the Day.

tree:0muaw2c14jfyty.why: It is not for you to be proud (7:13) and or you have a house of gold (17:93): unrelated.

tree:0art56p18d7pk1.why: May be among the successful (28:67) and no secret talk of three (58:7): unrelated.

tree:0aq3xw30th4mgt.why: Until they become believers: will you compel people (10:99), you may destroy yourself because they do not (26:3). Both rows read on.
tree:0aq3xw30th4mgt.relation: The Prophet's grief for unbelievers, answered: faith is by God's leave.

tree:1nwp3rs1p25yci.why: Those who have not yet joined them: the martyrs rejoice for those still behind (3:170), and later generations not yet joined (62:3).
tree:1nwp3rs1p25yci.relation: Those still to come, awaited by the martyrs and included in the Prophet's mission.

tree:05xprzt065ixrv.why: None attains it but the patient (28:80, 41:35).
tree:05xprzt065ixrv.relation: Patience is the key to God's reward and to good character.

tree:0uje4p81g5bz5g.why: Would that I had been: with them, to win spoils (4:73); dust (78:40).
tree:0uje4p81g5bz5g.relation: Two wishes: one for worldly gain, one of despair at judgement.

tree:1c2uml80ir1pw2.why: Has power for you: idols that have no power of harm or benefit (5:76), and who has power for you against God (48:11).
tree:1c2uml80ir1pw2.relation: Harm and benefit are in God's hand alone.

tree:1y1ehsa0d6jef2.why: O Musa, there are giants (5:22) and O Musa, the chiefs plot (28:20): an address and particle, different stories.

tree:0djrv5s16e49ac.why: O Musa, I: have chosen you (7:144), am God (28:30).
tree:0djrv5s16e49ac.relation: God's address to Musa: revealing Himself and choosing him.

tree:1kcyeng1wjnu76.why: He sends down rain: among the things only God knows (31:34), after people despaired (42:28).
tree:1kcyeng1wjnu76.relation: Rain as God's knowledge and mercy.

tree:0gichy10mgm5v1.why: O wives of the Prophet: a double punishment for sin (33:30), you are not like other women (33:32).
tree:0gichy10mgm5v1.relation: Their higher rank brings higher responsibility.

tree:19yap5u1hwmmzo.why: Who will help you besides Him: after God forsakes you (3:160), besides the Merciful (67:20).

tree:0d3y6vs1mvt0tq.why: Ships with what benefits people (2:164) and what benefits people remains (13:17): a common phrase, different points.

tree:0154y5a1902hoq.why: Same surah: what the deniers spend in this life is like crops struck by frost (3:117), the God-fearing spend in ease and hardship (3:134).
tree:0154y5a1902hoq.relation: Contrast: spending that is wasted and spending that is loved by God.

tree:15jopa01vqzq1e.why: How would God guide those who disbelieved (3:86) and God guides to His light whom He wills (24:35): different points.

tree:08imlgf15s5qnf.why: In Sad, the day of reckoning: the deniers ask for their share before it (38:16), and Dawud is warned of those who forget it (38:26). Both rows read on.
tree:08imlgf15s5qnf.relation: Mockery of the reckoning and warning about forgetting it.

tree:1yb92w81625q60.why: The day every soul comes pleading (16:111) and the day the sky brings smoke (44:10): unrelated.

tree:0w3o73i0vax29i.why: The day the earth quakes (73:14), the day the quake quakes (79:6).
tree:0w3o73i0vax29i.relation: The shaking of the Day of Judgement.

tree:1mpmljw0759be2.why: The day it is split: the sky with clouds (25:25), the earth from over them (50:44).
tree:1mpmljw0759be2.relation: Heaven and earth split open on the Day.

tree:09kthzm1691ep0.why: The day We gather: the God-fearing to the Merciful as honoured guests (19:85), from every nation a troop of deniers driven (27:83).
tree:09kthzm1691ep0.relation: Contrast: two ways of being gathered.

tree:1n7soby1menqiy.why: The day they come forth (40:16) and the day they are tried in the Fire (51:13): a common opening.

tree:127sm961a957ro.why: Do they await only ... the day it comes: some of the signs (6:158), its fulfilment (7:53). Neighbouring surahs.
tree:127sm961a957ro.relation: When the signs come, faith and regret are too late.

tree:06cx0y60h3pgja.why: The day it comes to them: the deniers mock its delay (11:8), and then ask for delay (14:44).
tree:06cx0y60h3pgja.relation: Those who mocked the delay of punishment beg for delay when it comes.

tree:0k45tq603w9bjg.why: The day they see the angels (25:22) and the day they see what they were promised (46:35): different scenes.

tree:0cd932m17wj56e.why: The day they meet Him: hypocrisy remains until then (9:77), and the believers' greeting then is peace (33:44).
tree:0cd932m17wj56e.relation: Contrast: the meeting with God, for the hypocrites and for the believers.

tree:1of39sh145qzur.why: That day the truth: the weighing (7:8), the sovereignty of the Merciful (25:26). An easy slip.
tree:1of39sh145qzur.relation: On the Day both the weighing and the kingdom are true.

tree:18gbpor1nx6elj.why: Whoever is spared that day, He has had mercy on him: in 6:16 by God, in 40:9 in the angels' prayer. Both end with the triumph.
tree:18gbpor1nx6elj.relation: Being spared on the Day is the great triumph.

tree:0mj18jo1cp6vs2.why: That day it belongs to God: the kingdom (22:56), the command (82:19). The row for 82:19 reads on into a new surah, which the match does not need.
tree:0mj18jo1cp6vs2.relation: On the Day all authority is God's.

tree:0lpvzhc0xvpnlc.why: We gave them and their fathers enjoyment until: life grew long (21:44), they forgot the reminder (25:18), the truth came (43:29). A classic three-way memorizer card.
tree:0lpvzhc0xvpnlc.relation: Long ease leads to forgetfulness until the truth arrives.

tree:04p454y1oypl86.why: Two of the rows are about the Children of Israel: how many clear signs We gave them (2:211), and We gave them signs holding a clear trial (44:33). 34:44 is about Quraysh, who were given no books, a different point.
tree:04p454y1oypl86.changes: Removed 34:44: its subject is Quraysh and it says the opposite, that they were given no scriptures.
tree:04p454y1oypl86.relation: The signs given to the Children of Israel were a favour and a test.

tree:16xc6vv195e44b.why: God gave him kingship, in two neighbouring stories of al-Baqara: Dawud, who used it justly (2:251), and the king who argued with Ibrahim (2:258). 65:7 is about spending from what God gave, a different structure.
tree:16xc6vv195e44b.changes: Removed 65:7: there the phrase means what God provided, in a ruling on spending.
tree:16xc6vv195e44b.relation: Contrast: kingship from God in the hands of a prophet and of a tyrant.

tree:1283htj1ghei3b.why: Adam received words from his Lord (2:37), God took from the children of Adam (7:172), and We made a covenant with Adam before (20:115): the shared words are a name and a preposition used three different ways.

tree:1hf9hdu0utr6ka.why: Three unrelated sentences where those who believed is followed by a particle: forgiveness for idolaters, despair of guidance, hearts humbled.

tree:1pdntrd11am205.why: Believing in him or it is said of the Prophet's followers (7:157), the Quran (17:107) and the jinn's call (46:31): a common phrase, no shared point.

tree:0ker9aw0bdyxnq.why: They believed, then disbelieved: the waverers who are not forgiven (4:137) and the hypocrites whose hearts are sealed (63:3). 5:93 repeats believe and fear for the righteous, a different structure.
tree:0ker9aw0bdyxnq.changes: Removed 5:93: there faith is followed by fearing God, not by disbelief.
tree:0ker9aw0bdyxnq.relation: Going back and forth between faith and denial ends in a sealed heart.

tree:013dckt0naj0fv.why: Had they believed and feared God: a better reward for the Jews (2:103), sins removed for the People of the Book (5:65), blessings opened for the towns (7:96).
tree:013dckt0naj0fv.relation: Faith and God-fearing bring reward, forgiveness and blessing.

tree:1weajh405ankwi.why: A rare phrase, the hours of the night, for night worship: some of the People of the Book (3:113), the Prophet (20:130), the devout believer (39:9).
tree:1weajh405ankwi.relation: Night worship as the mark of the sincere.

tree:0ki64g71aexid1.why: Ya-Sin's refrain, a sign for them: the dead earth revived (36:33), the night (36:37), the laden ship (36:41).
tree:0ki64g71aexid1.relation: Signs in earth, sky and sea.

tree:0pu4gh70i78jvb.why: Seeking the face of God, of their Lord, of his Lord: in spending (2:272), patience (13:22), and Abu Bakr's charity (92:20). Easy to swap.
tree:0pu4gh70i78jvb.relation: Sincere deeds are done only for God's face.

tree:0ygarut1ermdhr.why: Ibrahim and Ishaq, with or without Yaqub: in Yusuf's dream interpreted (12:6), his creed (12:38), and the praise of the patriarchs (38:45).
tree:0ygarut1ermdhr.relation: The line of Ibrahim, its favour and its faith.

tree:0541tuc0897dpa.why: Ibrahim and Musa in lists of the great messengers: the covenant (33:7), the religion ordained (42:13), the scrolls (87:19). The row for 87:19 reads on into a new surah, which the match does not need.
tree:0541tuc0897dpa.relation: One religion carried by the great messengers.

tree:0yoz6jx1twtkcf.why: Dhul-Qarnayn's three journeys, each opening he followed a way (18:85, 18:89, 18:92). The rows read on to where each journey reached.
tree:0yoz6jx1twtkcf.relation: West, east, and between the two barriers.

tree:0dlni1k0wypzk4.why: Whoever follows you among: the believers, enough for the Prophet with God (8:64) and to be treated gently (26:215); and among the deviators, Satan's followers (15:42).
tree:0dlni1k0wypzk4.relation: Following the Prophet or following Satan.

tree:1b2nv9d0wn2ulh.why: They followed their desires: twice in Muhammad (47:14, 47:16) and with denial in al-Qamar (54:3).
tree:1b2nv9d0wn2ulh.relation: Desire is behind denial and a sealed heart.

tree:0dfxpru0iahwci.why: Fear God said to an arrogant man (2:206), to the Prophet (33:1), and by the Prophet to Zayd (33:37): a common command in three different scenes.

tree:0qwur0a0p4vixc.why: Those who fear their Lord: gardens (3:198), lofty rooms (39:20), driven in groups to Paradise (39:73).
tree:0qwur0a0p4vixc.relation: The reward of the God-fearing in three pictures.

tree:0331s141yk101w.why: Fear a day: no soul avails another, with intercession and ransom in different order (2:48, 2:123), and when you return to God (2:281).
tree:0331s141yk101w.relation: The Day when each soul stands alone.

tree:0de4waq1bebwpc.why: Recite what was revealed to you: from the Book of your Lord (18:27), from the Book with prayer (29:45). 6:151 is I will recite what your Lord forbade, a different structure.
tree:0de4waq1bebwpc.changes: Removed 6:151: its phrase is a first-person promise to recite what God forbade, not the command to recite what was revealed.
tree:0de4waq1bebwpc.relation: The Prophet is told to recite the revelation.

tree:0yrhjiv0lpycd3.why: They came upon a people, a town, a valley: a common verb in three unrelated stories.

tree:1w84o1p1b7k15p.why: A generous reward: for those who fear the Merciful (36:11), for those who lend God a good loan (57:11, 57:18). All rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:1w84o1p1b7k15p.relation: The generous reward of fear and generosity.

tree:1ye159v1rle6un.why: Judge between them: with justice (5:42), by what God revealed (5:48, 5:49). Same surah.
tree:1ye159v1rle6un.relation: The Prophet's judgement must follow God's revelation.

tree:0acdru60eghwyc.why: Do not forbid what God made lawful: for you (5:87), for yourself, O Prophet (66:1). 2:275 says God made trade lawful, a different structure.
tree:0acdru60eghwyc.changes: Removed 2:275: there the phrase states what God allowed, not a forbidding of the lawful.
tree:0acdru60eghwyc.relation: No one may forbid what God allowed, not even the Prophet for himself.

tree:12xpm7q10jwxme.why: His brother Harun: a prophet (19:53), sent with signs (23:45), a minister (25:35).

tree:0ys7su51inre4n.why: The Book was differed over: Musa's Book in identical words (11:110, 41:45), and all Books (2:213).

tree:14dk7xy0pxychm.why: The blast seized them: at sunrise (15:73), in the morning (15:83), in truth (23:41).
tree:14dk7xy0pxychm.relation: The blast as punishment of Lut's people, Thamud and others.

tree:1w901nr1wb8dxp.why: Enter Paradise: no fear for you (7:49), for what you did (16:32), you and your wives (43:70).

tree:1p8aj3p03wzfwf.why: Call to your Lord's way with wisdom (16:125), call to your Lord (22:67, 28:87).
tree:1p8aj3p03wzfwf.relation: The Prophet's mission of calling to God.

tree:0qv7uxd0zbwu79.why: When God or your Lord took a covenant: from the prophets (3:81), from the People of the Book (3:187), from Adam's descendants (7:172).
tree:0qv7uxd0zbwu79.relation: God's covenants with prophets, scripture holders and all mankind.

tree:1l89z7g0gpz7tm.why: When they entered upon him: Ibrahim's guests (15:52, 51:25) and Dawud's litigants (38:22). Each prophet is startled.

tree:0hk42pr0z7ezsf.why: When you said: O Musa, we will not believe (2:55), we will not endure (2:61); and we hear and obey (5:7).
tree:0hk42pr0z7ezsf.relation: Contrast: the Israelites' refusals and the believers' obedience.

tree:1xmfgqp0qvl6db.why: When We let people taste mercy: they scheme (10:21), rejoice then despair (30:36, 42:48).
tree:1xmfgqp0qvl6db.relation: Human ingratitude in ease and hardship.

tree:0digzs50fbzql9.why: Then behold you: spreading as humans (30:20), coming out (30:25), kindling fire (36:80).

tree:16ypwp00xjzrrm.why: When there comes: the great catastrophe (79:34) and the deafening blast (80:33). Neighbouring surahs. 6:109 is about signs coming to deniers, a different structure.
tree:16ypwp00xjzrrm.changes: Removed 6:109: there the verb is about signs coming to the deniers, not the Day.
tree:16ypwp00xjzrrm.relation: Two names of the Day, announced the same way.

tree:1yndutl1ajf8oj.why: When they come to you: the believers (6:54), believing women to pledge (60:12), the hypocrites (63:1).
tree:1yndutl1ajf8oj.relation: How the Prophet receives each group.

tree:1m4bij11ki6mhd.why: When reminded: they do not fall deaf and blind (25:73), they fall prostrate (32:15), they do not take heed (37:13).
tree:1m4bij11ki6mhd.relation: Contrast: believers respond to reminders, deniers ignore them.

tree:1cbf7c313a2hf3.why: Then they would remain only a little: the deniers after expelling the Prophet (17:76), and you after fleeing (33:16). 4:53 is then they would not give, a different structure.
tree:1cbf7c313a2hf3.changes: Removed 4:53: it shares only the particle, not the clause about remaining a little.
tree:1cbf7c313a2hf3.relation: Escaping or expelling does not buy time.

tree:1haj90d1hii8g3.why: Then we or you would be losers: the chiefs of Madyan (7:90), Yusuf's brothers (12:14), the deniers in al-Muminun (23:34).

tree:1q6ytbz0wj4i03.why: When you meet: the deniers in battle, do not flee (8:15), strike their necks (47:4); a force, be firm (8:45).

tree:1h27u1j1x0aex9.why: Created from a drop, then he is an open adversary (16:4, 36:77). 21:18 says falsehood vanishes, a different subject.
tree:1h27u1j1x0aex9.changes: Removed 21:18: it shares only then behold it, about falsehood, not man.

tree:0j0b1au0cla52g.why: Remember your Lord: much, said to Zakariyya (3:41); within yourself (7:205); when you forget (18:24).
tree:0j0b1au0cla52g.relation: Three ways of remembering God: much, humbly, and on recalling.

tree:08tikxs1swwd4o.why: Sad's refrain, remember Our servant: Dawud (38:17), Ayyub (38:41), Ibrahim with his sons (38:45).
tree:08tikxs1swwd4o.relation: Models of patience and turning to God set before the Prophet.

tree:1kryiq40623uz6.why: Except whom He permits: no intercession (20:109, 34:23), no speech on the Day (78:38).
tree:1kryiq40623uz6.relation: On the Day, speech and intercession only by God's leave.

tree:1don9u11r8w9g1.why: Four months: the oath of abstention (2:226), the widow's waiting (2:234), and the respite for idolaters (9:2). A memorizer must keep the three apart.

tree:166wg5x1lgflp1.why: When We intend to destroy a town (17:16), We wished their Lord would replace him (18:81), had We wanted a pastime (21:17): a common verb, three unrelated points.

tree:1jfs8zv1ehwsrz.why: Send with us: Yusuf's brothers ask for Binyamin (12:63), Musa and Harun ask Pharaoh for the Israelites (20:47, 26:17).
tree:1jfs8zv1ehwsrz.relation: A request to release someone held, by brothers and by prophets.

tree:0cxqxga0sqneso.why: What I was sent with: Shuayb (7:87) and Hud (11:57, 46:23) say they have delivered it.
tree:0cxqxga0sqneso.relation: The prophets' task is to deliver what they were sent with.

tree:1cszevg198fljc.why: We sent messengers to the Israelites (5:70), no warner to Quraysh (34:44), two to the town (36:14): a common verb, unrelated contexts.

tree:1g8cluk1wlar36.why: We sent before you: our way with messengers (17:77), only men inspired (21:7), messengers who ate and walked in markets (25:20).
tree:1g8cluk1wlar36.relation: The messengers before were human, and God's way with them does not change.

tree:057a7jo14ln62c.why: Show me what they created: almost identical in 35:40 and 46:4, and in 31:11 after this is God's creation.
tree:057a7jo14ln62c.relation: The challenge to idolaters: their gods created nothing.

tree:03auoe81aznorm.why: Purified spouses in Paradise, each ayah ending differently: abiding (2:25), God's pleasure (3:15), deep shade (4:57). A memorizer card.
tree:03auoe81aznorm.relation: The same reward, completed three ways.

tree:1ds5i6s0wayhtk.why: The challenge: bring a sura or ten like it and call whomever you can besides God (10:38, 11:13). 8:60 prepare what you can of strength is a different subject.
tree:1ds5i6s0wayhtk.changes: Removed 8:60: there the phrase is about preparing strength for war, not the challenge.
tree:1ds5i6s0wayhtk.relation: The challenge of the Quran, raised from ten suras to one.

tree:09z5ijc03ybgiy.why: Ask God's forgiveness, God is forgiving and merciful: after the hajj (2:199), at the end of al-Muzzammil (73:20), and with the messenger's prayer (4:64). The row for 73:20 reads on into a new surah.
tree:09z5ijc03ybgiy.relation: Seeking forgiveness after worship and after wrong.

tree:12ptq751jnrizd.why: They were arrogant in: themselves (25:21), the land, Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman (29:39), and Ad (41:15).
tree:12ptq751jnrizd.relation: Arrogance in the land leads to destruction.

tree:0q3024j1ltl4oh.why: Travel by night with My servants: strike a dry path (20:77), you will be pursued (26:52), by night (44:23).
tree:0q3024j1ltl4oh.relation: The exodus told in three surahs.

tree:04pkkdg06kxlym.why: Israil forbade to himself (3:93), cursed by the tongue of Dawud (5:78), a witness from the Israelites (46:10): a name and preposition only.

tree:0r3t7zw093nnnc.why: A good example: in God's Messenger (33:21), in Ibrahim and those with him (60:4, 60:6), for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day.
tree:0r3t7zw093nnnc.relation: The Prophet and Ibrahim as models.

tree:1jrewoo1mcxy1q.why: Associating with Him: I do not (13:36, 72:20), and you call me to (40:42).
tree:1jrewoo1mcxy1q.relation: The refusal of shirk by the Prophet and by the believer of Pharaoh's people.

tree:181406r1wumgv7.why: When a calamity struck you in battle: at Uhud, it is from yourselves (3:165); the laggard thanks God he was absent (4:72). 5:106 is the calamity of death in travel, a different subject.
tree:181406r1wumgv7.changes: Removed 5:106: there the calamity is death on a journey, in a ruling on testimony.
tree:181406r1wumgv7.relation: Defeat is answered with self-blame and with the hypocrite's relief.

tree:19clvb80ri8vpc.why: Strike with your staff: the rock, twelve springs (2:60, 7:160), the sea, split (26:63).
tree:19clvb80ri8vpc.relation: Musa's staff brings water and splits the sea.

tree:04cbj4s1uycoc0.why: Who is more astray than one who: follows desire (28:50), is in far dissension (41:52), calls on what will not answer (46:5).
tree:04cbj4s1uycoc0.relation: Three faces of the worst error.

tree:0t38h0o13f3xpw.why: I am forbidden to worship those you call besides God (6:56, 40:66), and I do not worship those you worship (10:104).
tree:0t38h0o13f3xpw.relation: The Prophet's refusal of idol worship.

tree:0jh105a0f67hyc.why: We have prepared for them a painful punishment (4:18, 17:10) or the punishment of the Blaze (67:5). Rows read on.

tree:098v3s5084s40l.why: I do not know the unseen: the Prophet (6:50) and Nuh (11:31) in almost the same words, and had I known it (7:188).
tree:098v3s5084s40l.relation: Prophets disclaim knowledge of the unseen.

tree:05m1nzl18gm3wx.why: I know what: you do not know (2:30), you reveal and conceal (2:33), and Isa says I do not know what is in You (5:116).
tree:05m1nzl18gm3wx.relation: God's knowledge and the limits of others' knowledge.

tree:0pu1quy09kcvwi.why: That I may do good: Sulayman (27:19) and the grown man (46:15) in the same prayer, and the dead man's too-late plea (23:100).
tree:0pu1quy09kcvwi.relation: Contrast: the prayer for good deeds in life and the wish for them after death.

tree:1u0irvx18wa3fh.why: I seek refuge in You: Nuh from asking what he does not know (11:47), the Prophet from the devils' whispers and presence (23:97-98). 23:97 and 23:98 are one prayer.
tree:1u0irvx18wa3fh.changes: Merged 23:97 and 23:98 into one row: they are one continuous prayer.
tree:1u0irvx18wa3fh.relation: Prophets seek refuge from error and from devils.

tree:19fvcz1150kxn5.why: What God gave to His messenger as spoils without fighting: captives (33:50), from them (59:6), from the towns (59:7).
tree:19fvcz1150kxn5.relation: The Prophet's share of fay and its distribution.

tree:1atunfu1nkfhi8.why: Other than God: shall I seek a judge (6:114), will you fear (16:52), do you order me to worship (39:64).
tree:1atunfu1nkfhi8.relation: No judge, object of fear or worship but God.

tree:00no6k90o1eo8n.why: Will you not see: the night as mercy (28:72), Pharaoh's boast of his rivers (43:51), signs in yourselves (51:21). A memorizer ending.

tree:0g22s4f1habcl5.why: Three rhetorical questions of the same form: is one who stands on clear proof, or who believes, like one who does not? 11:17 and 47:14 open identically, and 32:18 gives the plainest version of the comparison.
tree:0g22s4f1habcl5.relation: The same question asked three ways: guidance and faith cannot equal misguidance and defiance.

tree:02y6wr20e3w37i.why: The command to fight is worded nearly the same in 2:191, 4:89 and 4:91, differing only in the verb for finding the enemy. A real trap for memorizers.

tree:0fi6iw313gozm1.why: 6:50 and 11:31 are close parallels: the Prophet and Nuh both disclaim treasures, knowledge of the unseen and being an angel. 40:44 only shares a common phrase in a different sense.
tree:0fi6iw313gozm1.changes: Removed 40:44: its phrase is part of a different sentence (what I tell you, you will remember), not the disclaimer.
tree:0fi6iw313gozm1.relation: Two messengers deny the same three claims in almost the same words.

tree:0m74esa12k1gb4.why: Three prayers that each end with the speaker fearing or hoping which group he will be among: Nuh (11:47) and Yusuf (12:33) fear loss and ignorance, the dying man (63:10) wishes he could be among the righteous.
tree:0m74esa12k1gb4.relation: Prophets ask for help before the fall; the negligent man asks only when it is too late.

tree:0v3fnck0nxf4f2.why: Spending only to seek the face of God appears in 2:272 and 92:20; 57:27 uses the same construction for monasticism invented to seek God's pleasure but not kept up. A useful lesson about sincere intention.
tree:0v3fnck0nxf4f2.relation: Seeking God's face through charity, set beside a self-made devotion that was not kept.

tree:0z3w9031ij2jwp.why: 12:40 and 17:23 both state the decree to worship none but Him, then branch: Yusuf to the upright religion, al-Isra to kindness to parents. 17:67 uses the exception in a different structure (those you call on vanish except Him).
tree:0z3w9031ij2jwp.changes: Removed 17:67: its exception belongs to a different sentence, not the command to worship.
tree:0z3w9031ij2jwp.relation: One command, followed in one place by the true religion and in the other by duty to parents.

tree:1xmacum0by3nwm.why: 2:255 and 11:105 both say no one intercedes or speaks on that Day except by His leave. 22:65 is about holding back the sky, a different subject.
tree:1xmacum0by3nwm.changes: Removed 22:65: same words but about the sky being held up, not speech or intercession.
tree:1xmacum0by3nwm.relation: Nobody speaks or intercedes before God without His permission.

tree:0cxddj00vtn6b2.why: Success (11:88), patience (16:127) and strength (18:39) are each said to come only through God. A clear lesson that every ability is from Him.
tree:0cxddj00vtn6b2.relation: Success, patience and power: none of them is had except through God.

tree:0qm1r1g0k2by7e.why: The refrain of surah Hud closing the stories of Ad, Thamud and Madyan, with small differences each time. Memorizers mix these up; the pattern ties the destroyed nations together.
tree:0qm1r1g0k2by7e.relation: One curse closes three stories of nations that rejected their prophets.

tree:0egetau05tlm8a.why: Only a two-word particle phrase is shared; God's knowledge, the punishment of wrongdoers and the brothers' testimony have nothing in common.

tree:1nv6bge06yhnm8.why: Three things that only increase loss: the Quran for wrongdoers (17:82), disbelief for disbelievers (35:39), wealth and children for those who follow it (71:21). Same closing, worth pondering.
tree:1nv6bge06yhnm8.relation: What should benefit only adds loss to those who turn away.

tree:1pi7iq01uidp2e.why: The same dismissal of a messenger as just a man: twice in surah al-Muminun by Nuh's and another people, and by Quraysh in 34:43. Same theme of peoples refusing their prophets.
tree:1pi7iq01uidp2e.relation: Every people belittled its messenger in the same words: he is only a man.

tree:072ogpa1mt4k6y.why: Refusing everything but disbelief, in nearly identical closings: most people in 17:89 and 25:50, the wrongdoers in 17:99. A real memorizer trap.

tree:1susvyt066hxap.why: Only a comparison particle is shared; usury, the idolaters' worship and Yaqub's distrust are unrelated.

tree:1dqbe1e023zg8m.why: 21:28 and 34:23 both limit intercession to whom God approves or permits. 3:73 uses the same words for a different thing (trust only those who follow your religion).
tree:1dqbe1e023zg8m.changes: Removed 3:73: the shared words there are about whom to trust, not intercession.
tree:1dqbe1e023zg8m.relation: Intercession is only for those God allows.

tree:00cfy5k0l14r04.why: The worldly life as mere enjoyment, said in 3:185 and 57:20 with the same words and in 13:26 compared with the Hereafter. Same theme, small differences worth learning.
tree:00cfy5k0l14r04.relation: The worldly life is little enjoyment beside the Hereafter.

tree:0p1qmna1lm4dhw.why: The righteous in bliss, said identically in 82:13 and 83:22, and in 83:18 their record in the highest place. Useful for memorizers, and the run-on in 82:14 shows the contrast with the wicked.
tree:0p1qmna1lm4dhw.relation: Contrast: the righteous in bliss, the wicked in fire.

tree:12cb5vo1chzea0.why: 19:37 and 43:65 are near identical ayat on the sects differing about Isa, ending with a woe on the disbelievers or the wrongdoers. 40:5 only shares the word for the factions in a different sentence.
tree:12cb5vo1chzea0.changes: Removed 40:5: the factions there are the past nations, a different structure.
tree:12cb5vo1chzea0.relation: The same verdict on those who split over Isa, with one word changed.

tree:1hj746f162v02z.why: Only a stock phrase about belief in the Last Day is shared, followed by different sentences on charity for show, a good example and divorce.

tree:0rqtyz21vphhm0.why: The shared words are the common pairing of this world and the Hereafter; reward for the righteous, captives at Badr and spreading indecency are different subjects.

tree:0lk20wu0k1nw28.why: Only the end of a stock phrase about the heavens and the earth followed by an opening particle is shared; the statements after it differ in subject.

tree:1m33fhf0btkeip.why: Only the word for the earth followed by a particle is shared; God's knowledge, Qarun's corruption and God's wealth are unrelated.

tree:0nhe044042wncw.why: The same question and answer pattern in 6:12, 13:16 and 34:24: ask who owns, rules or provides from the heavens and earth, and answer God. A clear memorizer group with a single argument.
tree:0nhe044042wncw.relation: The idolaters are made to answer their own question: it is God.

tree:1hshy791pp0peh.why: 2:116 and 30:26 say all in the heavens and earth are devoutly obedient to Him, in nearly the same words. 55:29 continues with a different sentence (every day He is about some matter).
tree:1hshy791pp0peh.changes: Removed 55:29: the shared word begins a different phrase there.
tree:1hshy791pp0peh.relation: Everything in creation submits to God.

tree:1hs8tcg151qd4s.why: Signs in the creation of heavens and earth, each for a different people: those who reason, those who fear God, the believers. Good for memorizers and for pondering who benefits from signs.
tree:1hs8tcg151qd4s.relation: The same signs, and three kinds of people who see them.

tree:1fbvafp0n7xfwx.why: Only the word for the earth followed by a particle is shared, in three different sentences on destroyed nations, the evil tree and God's knowledge.

tree:0pdy6ff1npidaz.why: 69:14 and 73:14 describe the earth and mountains on the Day, lifted and crushed or quaking. 33:72 is about the Trust offered to them, a different subject.
tree:0pdy6ff1npidaz.changes: Removed 33:72: same pair of words but the subject is the Trust, not the Day.
tree:0pdy6ff1npidaz.relation: Two images of the earth and mountains shattered on the Day.

tree:1d1pte50dk90a5.why: 23:79 and 67:24 are almost identical: He spread you through the earth and to Him you will be gathered. 11:123 shares only the return to Him in another structure.
tree:1d1pte50dk90a5.changes: Removed 11:123: the shared words belong to a different sentence (the whole matter returns to Him).

tree:0luft1h0hkj9p9.why: Only the earth followed by a common verb is shared; creation of light, rivers on earth and Pharaoh's tyranny are different subjects.

tree:0nqlncd05c2fez.why: The shackles on the necks of disbelievers in three scenes: deniers of resurrection, followers and leaders blaming each other, and those dragged into fire. One image of punishment repeated.
tree:0nqlncd05c2fez.relation: The same punishment for those who denied, shown three times.

tree:1k1f8150pexsk1.why: The shared words are a common noun and preposition in three different sentences: the hypocrites' complaint at Uhud, the Romans' defeat and victory, and God directing affairs from the sky. No shared wording to learn.

tree:0svh2mn136ghez.why: Men and jinn named together about speech: their devils whisper false words (6:112), together they cannot produce the Quran (17:88), and the jinn thought none of them would lie about God (72:5).
tree:0svh2mn136ghez.relation: Men and jinn can deceive and be deceived, but cannot match God's word.

tree:13y0oxi0sliqsk.why: 22:62 and 31:30 are near identical (God is the truth, what they call on is falsehood), differing by one pronoun. 47:3 applies the same truth and falsehood split to the people who follow each.
tree:13y0oxi0sliqsk.relation: God is the truth and their idols are falsehood; so people divide into followers of each.

tree:1medzm40m9up5e.why: Only a relative pronoun and a verb are shared; the burdens lifted by the Prophet, the Sabbath town and Lut's town are separate subjects.

tree:1f2z422162xqac.why: God establishes the truth by His words in three places: at Badr (8:7), against Pharaoh's magicians (10:82) and against those who accuse the Prophet (42:24). Same promise with different endings.
tree:1f2z422162xqac.relation: Whatever the battle, God makes the truth prevail by His words.

tree:1eef3cy0dokrl8.why: Only the word for truth followed by a negation is shared; extremism in religion, haste with revelation and hardened hearts are unrelated sentences.

tree:1p51pv310toq53.why: God speaks the truth, then one attribute follows: He is the best of judges (6:57), He guides to the way (33:4), He is the High, the Great (34:23). A tidy memorizer group with the same meaning.
tree:1p51pv310toq53.relation: God's word is the truth, said three times with a different attribute after it.

tree:0hl2uvv0t86rfr.why: Wine and gambling across the stages of their ruling: harm greater than benefit (2:219), then a filth to avoid (5:90), then Satan's aim to divide and distract from prayer (5:91).
tree:0hl2uvv0t86rfr.relation: The gradual prohibition of wine and gambling, read in order.

tree:1ysey6515t5zer.why: 18:104 and 30:7 describe people absorbed in the worldly life while deluded about their deeds or heedless of the Hereafter. In 8:42 the same word means the near bank of the valley at Badr.
tree:1ysey6515t5zer.changes: Removed 8:42: there the word means the nearer side of the valley, a different word sense.
tree:1ysey6515t5zer.relation: Two kinds of loss in the worldly life: wasted effort and heedlessness of the Hereafter.

tree:0hq81f418ahgbm.why: The creation of male and female in three late surahs: as a sign (53:45), as proof of resurrection (75:39), and as an oath (92:3). Short ayat a memorizer can confuse.
tree:0hq81f418ahgbm.relation: The pairing of male and female as a sign of God's power to create and to resurrect.

tree:0yr523g18udr8i.why: 36:83 and 67:1 are close: glory and blessing to Him in whose hand is the dominion of all things. 2:237 is the husband who holds the marriage tie, a different subject.
tree:0yr523g18udr8i.changes: Removed 2:237: the same words describe the husband holding the marriage contract.
tree:0yr523g18udr8i.relation: Dominion over all things is in His hand.

tree:14dh5s01tysenk.why: God subjected the sea (16:14, 45:12) and the riding animals and ships (43:13) for people to travel and seek His bounty, with a call to thank Him. Same favour, close wording.
tree:14dh5s01tysenk.relation: The means of travel are subjected to us so that we give thanks.

tree:0mik5xd0ib5jcd.why: Hud (11:51), the man in surah Ya-Sin (36:22) and Ibrahim (43:27) each speak of God as the one who created me. Callers to God use the same personal argument.
tree:0mik5xd0ib5jcd.relation: Each caller points to the One who created him as the reason to worship Him.

tree:1e72c6s0riip9a.why: Only a relative clause frame is shared; Yusuf's dream interpretation, the dispute about Isa and the Day the deniers meet are different subjects.

tree:1hvykyv15dvc6x.why: Only the term for the criminals is shared, in three different scenes: punishment for demanding signs, vengeance on past nations, and mocking believers.

tree:1ns177i0tyt2g4.why: People of the Book who differed: about the Book (2:176), about Isa (4:157) and about the Sabbath (16:124). Same phrase, three disputes, each judged.
tree:1ns177i0tyt2g4.relation: Every dispute over what God revealed ends in doubt, division or God's judgement.

tree:0fkn1va1uwriuk.why: Two outcomes for the oppressed: God makes the oppressed believers leaders and heirs (28:5), while the weak who followed the arrogant blame them in the fire (34:31, 34:33).
tree:0fkn1va1uwriuk.relation: Contrast: the oppressed who held to faith inherit the land; the weak who followed their masters share their punishment.

tree:10owfsc0shgyuw.why: 3:142 and 9:16 are a close pair: did you think you would be left before God knows who strives among you? 29:69 gives the striver's reward: God guides them to His ways.
tree:10owfsc0shgyuw.relation: Striving is the test, and guidance is its reward.

tree:07sri2x007wa1b.why: 9:43 and 29:3 both speak of God making clear who is truthful and who lies; 2:177 describes who the truthful are. Worth reading together.
tree:07sri2x007wa1b.relation: Trials separate the truthful from the liars, and 2:177 says what truthfulness looks like.

tree:1ob4bzp03tc7kx.why: Three treaty rulings at the start of at-Tawba with almost the same words: the release from treaties, the exception for those who kept them, and those at the Sacred Mosque. A real memorizer trap.

tree:0ljobu609csuaw.why: 3:169 and 47:4 speak of those killed in God's cause: they are alive and their deeds are not lost. 6:140 is about those who killed their children, a different verb form and subject.
tree:0ljobu609csuaw.changes: Removed 6:140: the same letters read as an active verb there (those who killed), a different word and subject.
tree:0ljobu609csuaw.relation: The martyrs are not dead and their deeds are not wasted.

tree:1vuw3ic0hfjhta.why: Only a relative pronoun and a helper verb are shared; three unrelated sentences.

tree:0d6c58y19a1zvw.why: 11:18 and 39:60 both show those who lied about God on the Day of Judgement, shamed with darkened faces or named by witnesses. In 9:90 the verb takes a direct object (lied to God), a different structure.
tree:0d6c58y19a1zvw.changes: Removed 9:90: the verb there has a different construction and is about the Bedouins staying back.
tree:0d6c58y19a1zvw.relation: Those who lie about God are exposed on the Day.

tree:1kszmpj18nxgeh.why: Those who harm the Prophet (9:61), God and His Messenger (33:57), and the believers (33:58), each with its punishment. A clear set for pondering the weight of harming others.
tree:1kszmpj18nxgeh.relation: Harm to the Prophet, to God and to believers, each with its own sentence.

tree:0ju2ye50172mbv.why: 4:37 and 57:24 open identically on the misers who command miserliness, then diverge; 3:180 says what the misers will carry on the Day. A memorizer trap and one theme.
tree:0ju2ye50172mbv.relation: The miser thinks he gains but will be collared with what he withheld.

tree:1hh8tiq022xck4.why: Three rulings in surah an-Nur on accusing chaste women and wives, with small changes in wording. Same subject, clear memorizer value.
tree:1hh8tiq022xck4.relation: Accusing the chaste: the legal penalty, the oath between spouses, and the curse in both worlds.

tree:1m5hsbs0fvejn2.why: 17:9 and 18:2 are nearly identical: good news for believers who do good deeds, a great or good reward. 29:4 is about those who do evil deeds and think they escape, a different sentence.
tree:1m5hsbs0fvejn2.changes: Removed 29:4: shares only two words, in a different sentence about evildoers.

tree:0pch9nl1jixevf.why: The Hour coming suddenly on the deniers, in three places with three different results: regret, unawareness, and the punishment of a barren day.
tree:0pch9nl1jixevf.relation: Those who doubt the Hour will be overtaken by it without warning.

tree:1rhjamm09u5b1o.why: 2:215 and 4:36 share a stock list of relatives, orphans, the poor and wayfarers that recurs often; 40:37 is Pharaoh barred from the way, unrelated.

tree:0mtu6d70yhbdw7.why: 67:16 and 67:17 are two parallel warnings that open alike (do you feel safe from Him above that He...) and a reader can swap them. 22:65 is about holding the sky up, a different sentence.
tree:0mtu6d70yhbdw7.changes: Removed 22:65: the sky there is the object of a different verb, not the one above who threatens.
tree:0mtu6d70yhbdw7.relation: Two threats side by side: the earth swallowing, or a storm of stones.

tree:1hyf1n319k3wc9.why: 2:235 and 2:284 both warn that God knows, and will reckon with, what you hide in yourselves. 51:21 (signs in yourselves) and 57:22 (afflictions) use the phrase for unrelated things.
tree:1hyf1n319k3wc9.changes: Removed 51:21 and 57:22: same phrase, unrelated subjects.
tree:1hyf1n319k3wc9.relation: God's knowledge of what is hidden in the self, as a warning in a law of marriage and as a general reckoning.

tree:1kbc6t003oam5m.why: 2:164 and 3:190 open the same way and a memorizer must keep apart the long list in 2:164 from the short one in 3:190. 3:191 and 67:3 carry the same call to look into creation.
tree:1kbc6t003oam5m.relation: Creation as a sign: listed, then reflected on by the people of understanding, then shown to have no flaw.

tree:0qqlksl0bmc77f.why: 2:49, 7:141 and 14:6 tell the rescue from Pharaoh in almost the same words; a memorizer must track the verb that differs in each. 6:99 is the stock closing about signs, a different phrase.
tree:0qqlksl0bmc77f.changes: Removed 6:99: its words are a different phrase (signs for believers), not the trial from your Lord.

tree:1khadwg043i6ja.why: 3:29 and 3:154 both speak of what is in your chests as known and tested by God. 17:51 and 40:80 use the phrase for something unrelated (a hard substance, a need).
tree:1khadwg043i6ja.changes: Removed 17:51 and 40:80: same phrase, unrelated meaning.
tree:1khadwg043i6ja.relation: What is hidden in the chest is known to God and brought out by trial.

tree:19pkro31ojd2l7.why: All four are about heedlessness before the Hour: two describe people heedless now, two have them confess on the Day that they were heedless.
tree:19pkro31ojd2l7.relation: Heedless in this life, then the confession on the Day when the cover is lifted.

tree:1rpenay0pme6zk.why: All four are about the benefits God put in cattle; a memorizer must tell apart how each one continues.
tree:1rpenay0pme6zk.relation: The favour of cattle, each time joined to a different lesson: the sacrifice, the drink, thanks, and travel.

tree:01dqdc919ilz8p.why: Only a speech opener with a conditional is shared; the speakers and subjects are unrelated (Pharaoh, Noah, Moses, a denier).

tree:0qxg2j51b5c9qf.why: 15:57 and 51:31 are Ibrahim's identical question to the angels, and 20:95 is Moses asking the Samiri in the same form; 20:51 is Pharaoh's question in the same surah. Useful for a memorizer keeping these questions apart.

tree:1jhhjif0mcvgnz.why: A set of the sayings the Quran reports from the Jews, each answered; worth seeing together.
tree:1jhhjif0mcvgnz.relation: The claims of the People of the Book, one after another, and how each is refuted.

tree:1bph3e91gpmirj.why: Four women addressing their Lord: the mother of Maryam, Maryam, the Queen of Sheba and the wife of Pharaoh.
tree:1bph3e91gpmirj.relation: Women's prayers in the Quran: a vow, wonder at a promise, repentance, and a plea for a house in Paradise.

tree:0ajr3em06590bs.why: The deniers' question about being raised after turning to bones and dust, repeated with small differences a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:0ajr3em06590bs.relation: The same denial of resurrection and the answers given to it.

tree:089wtfu0cz7nm8.why: Peoples answering their prophets with the same question (Hud twice, Moses and Ibrahim); 7:70 and 46:22 even end the same way.
tree:089wtfu0cz7nm8.relation: Different prophets, the same rejection: you came to turn us from what our fathers worshipped.

tree:1pow2rw1uuiwte.why: 11:69, 15:52 and 51:25 are the angels greeting Ibrahim, each with a different reply; a classic set for memorizers. 25:63 is the servants of the Merciful answering the ignorant, another subject.
tree:1pow2rw1uuiwte.changes: Removed 25:63 (with 25:64): a different scene and meaning.

tree:1vin96l098p9hb.why: 26:116 and 26:167 are the threats to Noah and to Lot in the same mould; 7:149 and 12:14 share the opening and the losers ending. Good for a memorizer.

tree:0nf8oxt02h8jdt.why: The cry of woe of those who see the punishment or the resurrection, each followed by a different confession.
tree:0nf8oxt02h8jdt.relation: Confessions at the moment of truth: we were wrongdoers, we were transgressors, this is the Day of Judgement.

tree:1cex98g1ctkpgq.why: Only a time phrase is shared; the subjects are unrelated (news of the unseen, Salih's people, Maryam in labour, a challenge to idolaters).

tree:1v7h4ty1dlundw.why: What true success is: the believers, the one who purifies himself, while Pharaoh's magicians claim success goes to whoever dominates today.
tree:1v7h4ty1dlundw.relation: Contrast: the magicians' worldly idea of success against the success of purification and faith.

tree:0s22xu312yui61.why: 6:31 and 10:45 are the same sentence about those who deny meeting God; 6:140 and 4:119 name others who lost. Useful for a memorizer.
tree:0s22xu312yui61.relation: Who the losers are: deniers of the meeting with God, killers of their children, followers of Satan.

tree:0c9x5a20ji88ky.why: A common phrase about going astray, said of different groups in unrelated contexts; nothing to learn from the grouping.

tree:1k11fsb18arc3h.why: The Quran described as an Arabic Quran, each time with a different purpose; 20:113 and 42:7 open the same way, which a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:1k11fsb18arc3h.relation: Why the Quran came in Arabic: so they may be mindful, so people who know understand, to warn the mother of towns.

tree:1q5lh4v1sv9kyb.why: Towns God destroyed, each mention adding something: the sudden punishment, their not believing, their not returning, their ruins.
tree:1q5lh4v1sv9kyb.relation: The destroyed towns as a lesson, seen from four sides.

tree:0ftuney0pnblw8.why: 17:56 and 34:22 are the same challenge to call on the false gods; 7:195 is the same challenge. 17:110, in the same surah, tells them to call on God by His names.
tree:0ftuney0pnblw8.relation: Contrast: call on the false gods and see they own nothing; call on God by any of His beautiful names.

tree:11v5dir1cu3mb9.why: The challenge to bring a scripture: the Torah, one surah, ten surahs, a better book. A memorizer must keep the amounts apart.
tree:11v5dir1cu3mb9.relation: The graded challenge to the deniers of the revelation.

tree:14h6goy0e0aul0.why: 9:83 and 48:15 are the same ruling on those who stayed behind: they will not go out with the Prophet. 9:51 and 33:16 are other replies with different subjects.
tree:14h6goy0e0aul0.changes: Removed 9:51 and 33:16: same reply opener, different subjects.
tree:14h6goy0e0aul0.relation: The same answer to the laggards in two campaigns.

tree:0v0mdjg12ep2sa.why: Only the end of one clause and the start of a closing are shared; the subjects (regret of the hypocrites, the mosque of harm, Moses' people) are unrelated.

tree:1i5c7od0b2gtpl.why: Each ayah commands decent, proper speech in a delicate setting: to a woman in her waiting period, to those unable to manage wealth, to relatives at the division of an estate, and by the Prophet's wives to men. 4:5 and 4:8 end the same way, a trap for memorizers.
tree:1i5c7od0b2gtpl.relation: Proper speech as a duty wherever money, marriage or modesty is at stake.

tree:05f7yv50uhb46d.why: 7:109 and 7:127 open the same way in one surah; 26:11 and 44:17 name the same people as the ones Moses was sent to.
tree:05f7yv50uhb46d.relation: Pharaoh's people: their chiefs' accusation and plotting, and God's sending Moses to them as a trial.

tree:189ctge1xbns5m.why: Only a phrase about the prophet's people is shared; the subjects are unrelated (unseen news, Moses' mission, the calf, Noah's mission).

tree:0umiy9c1vupsyy.why: Two separate pairs: the chiefs of Noah's people dismissing him as a mere man (11:27, 23:24), and Ibrahim questioning his father and people about their idols (21:52, 26:70). Each pair is a good memorizer set; together they are two different things.
tree:0umiy9c1vupsyy.changes: Split into the two pairs that belong together.
tree:0umiy9c1vupsyy.relation: Noah rejected as only a man; Ibrahim's question about what his people worship.

tree:0ceo6v11uxxgfd.why: 5:106, 6:152 and 35:18 say the same rule: kinship changes nothing, in testimony, in justice, and in bearing another's burden. 68:14 is about a man who has wealth and sons, a different phrase.
tree:0ceo6v11uxxgfd.changes: Removed 68:14: same words, a different meaning (owning wealth).
tree:0ceo6v11uxxgfd.relation: Kinship never bends testimony, justice or the reckoning.

tree:1nfuua60nst24i.why: 12:38 and 14:11 are believers saying what is not theirs to do; 14:11 and 37:30 both deny having any authority. 3:154 is the hypocrites' wish, a conditional with a different structure.
tree:1nfuua60nst24i.changes: Removed 3:154: its words are a conditional wish, a different structure.
tree:1nfuua60nst24i.relation: What is not ours: to associate partners, to bring a proof without God's leave, to have power over others.

tree:1h47p280pvz9c8.why: Hope in meeting God as the motive for action; 33:21 and 60:6 are near-identical lines about a good example (the Prophet, then Ibrahim), a memorizer trap.
tree:1h47p280pvz9c8.relation: Who hopes for God and the Last Day has a model to follow and deeds to do.

tree:1mu3l7t0je5b43.why: Only a stock closing about what people used to do is shared; the subjects are unrelated (the Children of Israel, sects, Noah's people, the disbelievers' reward).

tree:0yj07el0imtyxt.why: The Quran described as a blessed Book God sent down, each time with a different purpose; 6:92 and 6:155 in one surah open the same way.
tree:0yj07el0imtyxt.relation: The blessed Book: to confirm what came before, to be followed, to bring people to light, to be pondered.

tree:1jd27ea0fmcuuk.why: Thamud's denial, told in four short openings that differ in what they denied; easy to mix up.
tree:1jd27ea0fmcuuk.relation: The same denial seen four ways: the messengers, the warnings, the Hour, out of their arrogance.

tree:115vnec0tc35mw.why: A common phrase for denying the signs, said of unrelated subjects (Pharaoh's people, a warning to the Prophet, the evildoers' end, those given the Torah).

tree:0r12ejn1j7b3a3.why: Each ayah says evil deeds were made to seem fair to someone: the disbelievers, the idolaters killing their children, the wasteful, Pharaoh.
tree:0r12ejn1j7b3a3.relation: How falsehood is made attractive to those who follow it.

tree:0q20doo033nebw.why: 9:54, 9:80 and 9:84 give the same reason for the hypocrites' rejection, with small wording differences a memorizer must catch. 29:52 is a general statement in another context.
tree:0q20doo033nebw.relation: One cause behind three rulings on the hypocrites: their spending refused, no forgiveness, no funeral prayer.

tree:0a4c48017985ms.why: What is said of those who disbelieve in their Lord: they set up equals, they wear chains, their deeds are ashes, they have Hell. The phrase is distinctive and the four continuations are easy to confuse.
tree:0a4c48017985ms.relation: The state and end of those who disbelieve in their Lord.

tree:16pfaou030wjvs.why: 83:7 and 83:18 are a matched pair: the record of the wicked and the record of the righteous. 26:62 (Moses' trust) and 96:6 (man's transgression) share only the particle.
tree:16pfaou030wjvs.changes: Removed 26:62 and 96:6: only the opening particle is shared.
tree:16pfaou030wjvs.relation: Contrast: the record of the wicked in the lowest place and of the righteous in the highest.

tree:0zvdo6o00gcsbi.why: Two separate pairs: the entry into the town by the Children of Israel (2:58, 7:161), a classic memorizer pair, and eating from the sacrificial animals in the Hajj (22:28, 22:36).
tree:0zvdo6o00gcsbi.changes: Split into the two pairs that belong together.

tree:17zwzph19ok6w1.why: Three ayat are excuses or disclaimers of heedlessness, and 23:17 says God is never heedless of His creation.
tree:17zwzph19ok6w1.relation: Contrast: people plead they were heedless, while God is never heedless.

tree:0p4dr9v1wzal8p.why: The question on the Day about the partners they claimed; 28:62 and 28:74 are identical in one surah.
tree:0p4dr9v1wzal8p.relation: The false partners abandon their worshippers on the Day.

tree:0wp41hk09w5t6k.why: A warning form: how will it be when they are gathered, when witnesses are brought, when calamity strikes, when the angels take them.
tree:0wp41hk09w5t6k.relation: Four moments of reckoning, each introduced the same way.

tree:0mz33hn13tkilt.why: 7:188 and 10:49 differ only in the order of harm and benefit, a classic memorizer pair; 72:21 makes the same disclaimer. 5:25 is Moses saying he controls only himself and his brother, a different statement.
tree:0mz33hn13tkilt.changes: Removed 5:25: same verb, a different statement.
tree:0mz33hn13tkilt.relation: The Prophet has no power of benefit or harm except what God wills.

tree:0ksvih017cowf2.why: Two separate things: no fear on the people of Paradise (7:49, 43:68), and the repeated lines of the Kafirun surah (109:3, 109:5).
tree:0ksvih017cowf2.changes: Split into the Paradise pair and the repetition in surah 109.

tree:11jepkl187sdv1.why: Three commands in one passage of al-Isra end with similar threats that a memorizer must keep apart. 59:10 is a prayer about the heart, another subject.
tree:11jepkl187sdv1.changes: Removed 59:10: a prayer, unrelated to the commands of al-Isra.

tree:0tjmepc1kqdx6c.why: 2:22 and 51:51 both forbid setting up partners with God. 2:224 (oaths) and 24:63 (addressing the Messenger) are different prohibitions.
tree:0tjmepc1kqdx6c.changes: Removed 2:224 and 24:63: same prohibition form, different subjects.
tree:0tjmepc1kqdx6c.relation: The ban on setting up equals with God, after the signs of creation and after the call to flee to Him.

tree:1i07ulu189dz1y.why: 2:272 and 8:60 promise the same full repayment of what is spent, in almost the same words. 2:279 (usury) and 4:77 (fighting) use the phrase about other things.
tree:1i07ulu189dz1y.changes: Removed 2:279 and 4:77: same closing, different subjects.
tree:1i07ulu189dz1y.relation: Spending in God's cause is repaid in full.

tree:1x2ya9a048o13k.why: No protector or intercessor besides God, said four times with different continuations; a memorizer set and a clear theme.
tree:1x2ya9a048o13k.relation: No one can intercede for a soul except by God's leave.

tree:1cqf67c0ukf4mo.why: All four lift blame from those with a real excuse: the weak, the sick, the poor, the blind and the lame. 24:61 and 48:17 open identically and then go to different subjects (eating in houses, staying from battle), a memorizer trap.
tree:1cqf67c0ukf4mo.relation: Who is excused, and from what: from fighting, and from the rules of eating together.

tree:1ey6zz009o1i8y.why: 6:160, 28:84 and 40:40 state the same justice: an evil deed is repaid only by its like, while good is multiplied. A close memorizer set. 31:33 is about no parent paying for a child, a different statement.
tree:1ey6zz009o1i8y.relation: God's justice and generosity: evil repaid only in kind, good repaid many times.

tree:13x93cp1afczdp.why: Four prohibitions in the rulings on women and marriage: concealing pregnancy, taking back the dower, inheriting women by force, and new marriages for the Prophet.
tree:13x93cp1afczdp.relation: What is not lawful in marriage, for wives, husbands and the Prophet.

tree:0oa8zqd040ggg7.why: 20:112 and 72:13 promise the believer the same safety from injustice in matched pairs of words, a memorizer pair (the jinn echo it). 27:10 (the messengers do not fear) and 91:15 (God does not fear the outcome) are different statements.
tree:0oa8zqd040ggg7.changes: Removed 27:10 and 91:15: same verb, different subjects.
tree:0oa8zqd040ggg7.relation: The believer fears no wrong: said by God in Taha and by the believing jinn.

tree:1p19bf105qu9yz.why: God never breaks His promise, said four ways; the endings differ (the appointment, His promise) and a memorizer must keep them apart.
tree:1p19bf105qu9yz.relation: Certainty of God's promise: the gathering, the punishment, victory, and Paradise.

tree:0qbzuam1myh73y.why: Each ayah denies that two groups are equal: those who strive and those who sit, the bad and the good, those who spent before the victory and after, the people of the Fire and of Paradise.
tree:0qbzuam1myh73y.relation: The Quran's scale of who is not equal to whom.

tree:09zhyv41j8cvls.why: Who is questioned and who is not: God is not questioned while they are; the criminals are not asked about their sins. 70:10 is a friend not asking after a friend, a different sense.
tree:09zhyv41j8cvls.changes: Removed 70:10: the verb there means asking after someone, not being called to account.
tree:09zhyv41j8cvls.relation: Pondering the questioning: God is beyond question, and on that Day the guilty are known without being asked.

tree:00ehd0c0pmjkvo.why: The enemies of the believers will not be helped: 3:111 and 59:12 end the same way about turning their backs; 28:41 and 41:16 say it of Pharaoh's people and of Ad in the Hereafter.
tree:00ehd0c0pmjkvo.relation: Those who fight God's people end without help, here and in the Hereafter.

tree:0p3z5lq0g8y2wy.why: Ibrahim confronting his father and people, four times with different wording; a classic memorizer set.
tree:0p3z5lq0g8y2wy.relation: Ibrahim's challenge to idol worship, from questioning to disowning.

tree:0awe2fv1i40219.why: God's oath to fill Hell, said to Iblis (7:18, 38:85) and as His decreed word (11:119, 32:13); the endings differ in ways a memorizer must hold.
tree:0awe2fv1i40219.relation: The decree that Hell will be filled, from Iblis' followers among jinn and men.

tree:0oinr331gcwm9p.why: The descent of Adam with enmity between them, told three times with different continuations; 43:67 turns the same words to friends who become enemies on the Day.
tree:0oinr331gcwm9p.relation: Enmity on earth since the fall, and the friends who turn enemies on the Day except the God-fearing.

tree:0t2dwiy1dyueh6.why: 2:131, 6:71 and 40:66 are about submitting to the Lord of the worlds: Ibrahim's answer and the Prophet's command. 83:6 is people standing before Him on the Day, a different statement.
tree:0t2dwiy1dyueh6.changes: Removed 83:6 (with 83:7): same name of God, different subject.
tree:0t2dwiy1dyueh6.relation: Submission to the Lord of the worlds, by Ibrahim and by the Prophet.

tree:13a2m461scp1a2.why: God telling that He sent down clear signs, with different continuations; 24:34 and 24:46 in one surah are a memorizer trap.
tree:13a2m461scp1a2.relation: Clear revelation, and who benefits from it and who rejects it.

tree:0po3g9u11vm86k.why: The proof had already reached them: a messenger, Moses, guidance, warning news. Each time the people turned away anyway.
tree:0po3g9u11vm86k.relation: No excuse remains: guidance came, and was rejected.

tree:1s2rnwe05vgg30.why: 11:79, 17:102 and 21:65 have one side tell the other you know well; in 17:102 and 21:65 the opponent is made to admit a truth he knows. 37:158 is about what the jinn know, a different sentence.
tree:1s2rnwe05vgg30.changes: Removed 37:158: the jinn as subject, a different sentence.
tree:1s2rnwe05vgg30.relation: The truth the opponent already knows: Pharaoh knows who sent the signs, Ibrahim's people know idols cannot speak.

tree:10xz6bu1u4h8uo.why: A stock closing about people of certainty, after unrelated subjects (demands for a sign, judgement, creation, the Quran as insight).

tree:0ijz7qe1r23eba.why: 2:54, 5:20 and 61:5 are Moses addressing his people with the same opening and different messages: repent of the calf, remember God's favour, why do you hurt me. 10:71 is Noah, another story.
tree:0ijz7qe1r23eba.relation: Moses and his people: rebuke, reminder and complaint.

tree:0wl7y3m0bmtmjc.why: 6:154, 7:145 and 16:89 describe a scripture that explains everything: the Torah twice and the Quran. 65:3 is God setting a measure for everything, a different phrase.
tree:0wl7y3m0bmtmjc.changes: Removed 65:3: same words, a different meaning (a measure).
tree:0wl7y3m0bmtmjc.relation: The Torah and the Quran each given as a full explanation, guidance and mercy.

tree:1e11yto0taka30.why: 2:139, 28:55 and 42:15 use the same line of separation, each with a different ending. 33:71 is God setting your deeds right, a different phrase.
tree:1e11yto0taka30.changes: Removed 33:71: same words, different structure and meaning.
tree:1e11yto0taka30.relation: Parting with opponents without quarrel: we have our deeds and you yours.

tree:03e2w031w2oofl.why: Two unrelated subjects meet only on a short phrase: speaking without knowledge, and rain bringing out crops. The real pairs are kept elsewhere.

tree:15n3grz19nd0b7.why: 37:154 and 68:36 are the same rebuke, and 10:35 has it with a different opening. 14:45 is about what became clear to them, a different structure.
tree:15n3grz19nd0b7.relation: The rebuke to those who judge wrongly about God.

tree:1jhwx9u0yymjay.why: 11:2, 51:50 and 51:51 are the Prophet's declaration that he is a warner from God; 51:50 and 51:51 repeat it back to back. 16:10 is water to drink, a different meaning.
tree:1jhwx9u0yymjay.changes: Removed 16:10 and made the three warner ayat one row each (the old rows repeated 51:51).
tree:1jhwx9u0yymjay.relation: The messenger as a clear warner from God.

tree:1ahlfyq03q4clq.why: The reward of those who do good; 16:30 and 39:10 share the same clause, a memorizer pair.
tree:1ahlfyq03q4clq.relation: Good done is repaid with good, in this world and more in the next.

tree:1ejedju0oiehk8.why: The weak blaming the arrogant leaders on the Day; 14:21 and 40:47 open identically.
tree:1ejedju0oiehk8.relation: Followers and leaders turn on each other when they face the punishment.

tree:12apeh01iaxsy4.why: The same threat with small changes a memorizer must hold apart: the verb of preparing and the kind of punishment. 4:37 and 4:151 are identical in one surah.

tree:1r8iume1hang92.why: 17:89, 30:58 and 39:27 say God set forth every kind of example in this Quran, each with a different response; a memorizer must keep the verbs and endings apart. 2:159 is about hiding what was made clear in the Book, another subject.
tree:1r8iume1hang92.relation: Every example given in the Quran, met with rejection, mockery, or remembrance.

tree:0ojbc6y1jvcegu.why: Only a stock closing (God makes things clear to people so that they may...) is shared; the subjects are unrelated rulings and parables.

tree:01xag7a01pbr4w.why: 2:165, 4:139 and 10:65 say all power and all honour belong to God, in the same closing form. 14:21 is everyone appearing before God, a different meaning of the words.
tree:01xag7a01pbr4w.changes: Removed 14:21: the words mean appearing before God, not possession.
tree:01xag7a01pbr4w.relation: All power and honour are God's: no use seeking them from idols or disbelievers.

tree:0sbazzt08ipkb5.why: A plain negation of belief, in four unrelated contexts; nothing to learn from the grouping.

tree:1ye8skf0sjc8jl.why: 18:52 and 28:64 are the same scene: the idolaters call their partners on the Day and get no answer. 13:18 and 28:50 are about people not answering God or the Prophet.
tree:1ye8skf0sjc8jl.changes: Removed 13:18 and 28:50: same verb, different subjects.
tree:1ye8skf0sjc8jl.relation: The false partners cannot answer those who call them.

tree:0w9g77j00lotfl.why: Only a short negation is shared; the subjects are unrelated (God changing a favour, Ibrahim, man's creation, late faith).

tree:1ourtmg1du1zji.why: The brothers' entries in the story of Yusuf, in order; 12:69 and 12:99 are parallel (he takes in his brother, then his parents), a memorizer trap and a turning point of the story.
tree:1ourtmg1du1zji.relation: The stages of the reunion: entering the city, meeting Yusuf, pleading, and the family taken in.

tree:0uwktw410o2jl2.why: Only a time clause is shared; four unrelated scenes (Satan's speech, Moses' term, Zayd's marriage, the jinn).

tree:04hvwvc02x1qv8.why: 2:145, 5:107 and 11:31 have a speaker say he would then be a wrongdoer if he did a thing; the same phrase in three settings. 21:59 is Ibrahim's people accusing whoever broke the idols, a different statement.
tree:04hvwvc02x1qv8.changes: Removed 21:59 (with 21:60): the phrase there is an accusation, not a self-check.
tree:04hvwvc02x1qv8.relation: Binding oneself to justice: following desire, false testimony, or belittling the poor would make one a wrongdoer.

tree:129n1u01fdwch6.why: Only 33:21 and 60:6 belong together, and that pair is already in the card about hoping for God. 50:37 and 54:14 share only a short relative clause.

tree:1v8fckk1deci14.why: Al-Khidr's warning to Moses and its two reminders, growing in force; a classic memorizer set. 18:41 (the water sinking out of reach) is another story.
tree:1v8fckk1deci14.changes: Removed 18:41: a different story in the same surah.
tree:1v8fckk1deci14.relation: The test of patience with what one does not understand.

tree:1va13411tkmy13.why: 3:10, 3:116 and 58:17 are nearly identical about wealth and children not saving the disbelievers, with different endings. 8:19 is about a fighting force, another subject.
tree:1va13411tkmy13.relation: Wealth and children avail nothing against God.

tree:1x3eoni158ps4o.why: Prayers for forgiveness of sins with different additions; 12:97 has Yusuf's brothers ask their father to seek it for them.
tree:1x3eoni158ps4o.relation: Seeking forgiveness: the believers directly, the brothers through their father.

tree:1k6clnz19z9zlt.why: All praise belongs to God, in the first life and the last, in heavens and earth; four close variants a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:1k6clnz19z9zlt.relation: God's praise without limit of time or place.

tree:1afwzp81jl5dzg.why: 2:178 and 5:94 end with the same warning against transgressing after a concession. 4:14 and 24:11 threaten other punishments for other sins.
tree:1afwzp81jl5dzg.relation: Transgressing after a ruling is eased, in retaliation and in hunting.

tree:01j5ajk0as0w5g.why: Only a short phrase is shared; the subjects are unrelated (a garden burnt, worldly desire, mosques, good deeds).

tree:1mnuh2c1o9403g.why: Two different things: the heir's child in the inheritance rules (4:11, 4:176), and the denial that God has a son (4:171, 6:101).
tree:1mnuh2c1o9403g.changes: Split into the inheritance pair and the pair denying God a son.
tree:1mnuh2c1o9403g.relation: The same words carry law about a man's child and the denial of a child to God.

tree:12546oh1y8icuj.why: People invited to come and refusing: to fight, to God's revelation and the Messenger (4:61 and 5:104 open identically), to be prayed for.
tree:12546oh1y8icuj.relation: Each invitation met with turning away, out of hypocrisy, inherited custom or pride.

tree:0vmcgwr194glwx.why: The particle is a prohibition in some and a negation in others; no shared clause or subject.

tree:09ksne709ij1cn.why: 4:137 and 4:168 are the same verdict on those who persist in disbelief, differing in the last word. 36:43 and 60:10 share only a negation pattern.
tree:09ksne709ij1cn.changes: Removed 36:43 and 60:10: different subjects and structure.
tree:09ksne709ij1cn.relation: Those who keep turning away are not forgiven or guided.

tree:1feysbx1f8k9uh.why: The real pair (24:12, 24:16) is its own card; 6:43 and 18:39 share only the reproach form with other subjects.

tree:1sv4eeb0d8hu8z.why: The purpose of the return to God: to reward the believers who do good, each time with a different addition; 53:31 sets both rewards side by side.
tree:1sv4eeb0d8hu8z.relation: Why the creation is brought back: just and generous reward.

tree:09ty4m51mox3kx.why: 3:23, 24:48 and 24:51 are about people called to God's judgement: some turn away, the believers say we hear and obey. 16:124 is God judging on the Day, a different statement.
tree:09ty4m51mox3kx.changes: Removed 16:124: God's judgement on the Day, not a call to judgement.
tree:09ty4m51mox3kx.relation: Contrast: those who turn away when called to judgement, and the believers who obey.

tree:14ssbj61e6tuyy.why: No blame on the excused: the believers for what they ate before the ban, the weak and sick, the blind and lame. 24:61 and 48:17 open identically. It overlaps another card on the same theme.
tree:14ssbj61e6tuyy.relation: Who carries no blame, and why.

tree:0i5wj6b1sg8gdx.why: Only a short phrase is shared; the subjects are unrelated.

tree:00sf7e41kwp5pw.why: How people meet what God gave them: some hide it, some envy others for it, some should be content with it, and the righteous take it gladly.
tree:00sf7e41kwp5pw.relation: Attitudes to God's bounty: hiding, envy, contentment, acceptance.

tree:1p1wj820d15lji.why: The four groups of al-Waqi'a introduced with the same refrain; a memorizer must keep the order and names apart.
tree:1p1wj820d15lji.relation: The right and the left, named twice in the surah with different words.

tree:14aj86k0gilig2.why: 2:215, 2:270 and 34:39 are about what you spend: where it goes, that God knows it, and that He replaces it. 60:10 is about reclaiming dowries, another subject.
tree:14aj86k0gilig2.changes: Removed 60:10: same verb, a different matter (dowries returned).
tree:14aj86k0gilig2.relation: Spending: to whom, God's knowledge of it, and its return.

tree:17j2nh51gi5wnb.why: The real pair (28:60, 42:36) is its own card; 3:73 and 17:85 share only a short phrase about what you were given.

tree:1qf206t049qx3f.why: 39:38 and 46:4 challenge the idolaters about what they call on besides God; 19:48 is Ibrahim leaving it. 6:41 is about what they call on God to remove, a different sense.
tree:1qf206t049qx3f.changes: Removed 6:41: the words mean the distress they pray to be lifted, not the idols.
tree:1qf206t049qx3f.relation: What is called on besides God cannot create, harm or help, and Ibrahim turns from it.

tree:0xrjr1a1tsozly.why: Each ayah blames division or sin on people after clear proofs had already come to them.
tree:0xrjr1a1tsozly.relation: Division comes not from ignorance but after knowledge.

tree:14s7mri1hwd6hw.why: Three surahs say the People of the Book differed only after knowledge came, out of rivalry; 3:105 warns believers not to be like them. A close memorizer set.
tree:14s7mri1hwd6hw.relation: Division out of rivalry after knowledge, and the warning not to repeat it.

tree:0b0z1gp0qw2h21.why: A negation of what God made or decreed, in unrelated rulings (a truce, forbidden cattle, ease in religion, adoption).

tree:10ghe7f10qgflh.why: 2:143, 17:60 and 74:31 say God made something only as a test: the old qibla, the vision, the number of the keepers of Hell. 21:34 is about no one being given immortality, another statement.
